children.text: siddhe yatra sati trapākulam iva spardhābhilāṣāhater antardhiṃ vahati trilokamahitaṃ śeṣaṃ nijārdhadvayam /
children.translated_text: Where, upon the accomplished [union], as if embarrassed by the assault of competitive desire, he conceals half of his own self, which is honored by the three worlds,

children.text: snehaikībhavadāśayadvayajayākāṅkṣīva gāḍhaṃ miladdehārdhadvayam astu tad bhagavatos sadbhāvasampattaye || 1 ||
children.translated_text: May that [form] of the Lord, with two body-halves closely united, as if desiring victory through the merging of two minds in love, bring about the attainment of true being. (JRt 1)

children.text: dātuṃ bhaktāya kalyāṇaṃ garbhaṃ bibhrad ivānvaham /
children.translated_text: As if bearing a child daily to bestow welfare upon his devotee,

children.text: tundibho gaṇarājas sa vighnaśāntiṃ karotu naḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: May that pot-bellied lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, grant us the pacification of obstacles. (JRt 2)
By kings beginning with <s>Śrī Gonanda</s>, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, up to the present age,
The land of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, [founded by] <s>Kāśyapa</s>, was protected by those endowed with virtues. (JRt 3)
As they remained in the darkness of the night of winter of misfortune,

children.text: naiva kaścid apaśyat tān kāvyārkānudayāc ciram || 4 ||
children.translated_text: No one could see those [kings] for a long time before the sunrise of poetry. (JRt 4)
Then the poet <s>Kalhaṇa</s>, with speech full of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor), made ever-young
The fame of those [kings] up to <s>Śrī Jayasiṃha</s>, though it had grown old. (JRt 5)
Thereafter, due to defects of the land and such, or because of their misfortune,

children.text: kavir vāksudhayā kaścin nājijīvat parān nṛpān || 6 ||
children.translated_text: No poet revived the later kings with the nectar of his words. (JRt 6)
Now, while <s>Śrī Jainollābhadīna</s> [Zain al-Ābidīn] protects the earth without diminishing it,
The one named <s>Jonarāja</s> has undertaken the narration of the deeds of those [kings]. (JRt 7)
To destroy the continuous affliction of the royal travelers caused by the languor of pride,
This tree of poetry has been planted, whose fruits shall appear in the future. (JRt 8)
Nourished with the essence of refinement, cooled by the nectar of humility,
This [work] should be cultivated with great effort by good people. (JRt 9)
Desiring to rescue, out of the compassion of <s>Śrī Jainollābhadīna</s> [Zain al-Ābidīn],
These past kings who had sunk in the ocean of oblivion, (JRt 10)
And having received without disrespect the command from the mouth of the compassionate <s>Śrī Śiryabhaṭṭa</s>,
Who was appointed over all offices of <s>dharma</s>, (JRt 11)
My talent now endeavors to complete the succession of kings,
Out of desire for the fame of a poet, not because of my own initiative. (JRt 12)

children.text: kva cuṇṭhījalavan madvāk kva ca kāvyataraṅgitam /
children.translated_text: How can my speech, [sluggish] like the water of a shallow pool, compare to the waves of poetry?
By merely imitating a shadow, how can a reed become sugarcane? (JRt 13)

children.text: antaśśūnyāṃ laghuṃ prajñāṃ tumbīm iva vahann aham /
children.translated_text: Carrying within me a light intellect, hollow inside like a gourd,
Alas, I have undertaken the effort to cross the <s>Rājataraṅgiṇī</s>. (JRt 14)
My impetuousness in meditating on the virtues of kings is not a fault,
For even an ugly woman becomes attractive through ornaments and pride. (JRt 15)
My speech may be useful to poets, or for the purification of my own heart;

children.text: Gaṅgājalaṃ jalaṃ teṣāṃ yair na pītaṃ jalāntaram || 16 ||
children.translated_text: The waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> are [true] water for those who have not drunk any other water. (JRt 16)
I have merely laid the thread of the narrative of the kings' chronicle;
Let the clever artisans among poets create the [full] composition here. (JRt 17)
The skill of the great whetstone is only for the polishing of gems;
But it is the face-jewel [i.e., the gem itself] that bestows their lustre. (JRt 18)

children.text: vinaiva prārthanāṃ kāvyaṃ kaveḫ paśyanti sādhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The virtuous behold the poetry of a poet without any solicitation;

children.text: kim arthitaś śaśī viśvaṃ sudhāsāreṇa siñcati || 19 ||
children.translated_text: Does the moon sprinkle the world with the essence of nectar only when asked? (JRt 19)

children.text: anunīto 'pi kāluṣyaṃ khalaẖ kāvye na muñcati /
children.translated_text: Even when appeased, the wicked do not abandon their hostility toward poetry;
Even when washed with nectar, a charcoal never becomes white. (JRt 20)

children.text: paśyantu matkāvyam iti ciraṃ dūraṃ gatā kaveḥ /
children.translated_text: The poet's [desire] that 'people should see my poetry' has long since departed far away,
[Due to] the wretchedness of disposition that looks only toward the inner chambers [i.e., ignoring poetry]. (JRt 21)
The taste of the unskilled for song and Sanskrit would be the same [as nothing];
Crows string <s>guñjā</s> berries, mistaking them for sparks of fire in the cold. (JRt 22)
Poetry, even when heard, does not please those whose understanding is marred by ignorance;
What does sugarcane placed in the mouth accomplish for one whose teeth are weak? (JRt 23)
When poetry beautiful in its meaning is shown to those of pure mind,
The reflection of envy upon the gems of its virtues is irresistible. (JRt 24)
The Creator, defaming the moon with a spot, [and] afflicting <s>Budha</s> [Mercury] with the disease of envy,
Comes to be censured as the foremost among those who cannot bear the excellence of others. (JRt 25)
Let my speech gain flavor by entering into the poetry of <s>Kalhaṇa</s>;

children.text: naḍvalāmbu sarittoye patitaṃ pīyate na kim || 26 ||
children.translated_text: Is not the water of a swamp drunk when it has fallen into the water of a river? (JRt 26)
1) <s>Jayasiṃha</s> (LS 4203-4230)
He who delights the world, who is honored by gods and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
The glorious son of <s>Sussala</s>, a conqueror of the earth like <s>Saṅkrandana</s> [Indra], existed. (JRt 27)
Though she [<s>Śrī</s>, the goddess of fortune] bore the fame of having only the king of elephants as her vehicle,
It is wondrous that she always dwelt in him who bore the name <s>Jayasiṃha</s>. (JRt 28)

children.text: Vāgdevyā lālite mātrā Śriyo bhoktari bhūpatau /
children.translated_text: When the king, nurtured by <s>Vāgdevī</s> [Sarasvatī] as [his] mother, was the enjoyer of <s>Śrī</s> [Lakṣmī],
No enmity was seen between those two [goddesses], even in their relationship as mother-in-law and daughter-in-law. (JRt 29)
A certain <s>Malla</s>, a vassal of the lord of <s>Trigarta</s>, <s>Suśarman</s>,
Exiled by enemies and seeking livelihood, came [to Kaśmīra] and the king received him. (JRt 30)

children.text: sarvatrauṣadhayas tṛṇāni maṇayo grāvāṇa evākhilair manyante guṇino digantaragatās tāvaj janāḫ prākṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: All herbs are [deemed mere] grass, all gems [mere] stones by ordinary people who have gone to the ends of the earth, as long as the virtuous do not, through their deeds

children.text: yāvan naiva nayanti karmabhir abhidhyeyaprakarṣaprathaiś citraprāyadaśaiś ca nirmalam atisphāraṃ janaṃ rañjanam || 31 ||
children.translated_text: And their wondrous manifestations of renowned and contemplable excellence, bring about pure and expansive delight in people. (JRt 31)
When the lord of the earth [Jayasiṃha] went to conquer the land of the <s>Yavanas</s> [Muslims],
<s>Malla</s> became the favorite of the army due to his excess of valor. (JRt 32)
To weigh [i.e., assess] the remnant of the army of the lord of the <s>Turuṣkas</s> [Turks] after [their] defeat,
<s>Mallacandra</s>, fortified by his own daring, went at night to the enemy camp. (JRt 33)

children.text: yatra na prāviśad vāyur bhītyeva subhaṭair vṛte /
children.translated_text: Where even the wind did not enter, as if out of fear, [the camp] being surrounded by warriors,
He surely entered by the power of spells and medicines into the midst of the force. (JRt 34)
Out of fear of the sin of killing those asleep, he did not kill the lord of the <s>Yavanas</s>,
But carried away his shoes bearing the mark of his name as his head-trophy. (JRt 35)

children.text: upānahau parijñāya gṛhītvā cātha so 'py ariḥ /
children.translated_text: Recognizing and seizing the shoes, that enemy then

children.text: bhūpateś śibiraṃ yātaś śriyaṃ kīrtim ivādita || 36 ||
children.translated_text: Went to the camp of the king, [seeking] royal fortune as [one seeks] fame from the start. (JRt 36)

children.text: dve mūrtī tapanānalāv atha tathā Śaṃbhoś śaśāṅkāmbhasī netā hanta mitho gatānugatiko lokas tulāṃ tāṃ dvayīm /
children.translated_text: The sun and fire are two forms [of heat], and likewise the moon and water are [two forms of coolness] of <s>Śambhu</s>; the leader, alas, [follows] a pattern of mutual imitation — the world balances that pair,

children.text: sūryācandramasor yathāsvam upalaiẖ kāntair viśeṣaṃ paraṃ teṣāṃ tatpratiyogyasambhaviguṇair labdhā jano 'rocakī || 37 ||
children.translated_text: As the sun and moon [gain] special distinction through their respective beloved gems [sūryakānta and candrakānta], [so] people become disenchanted by the qualities of their opponents that rival those [gems]. (JRt 37)
In the thirtieth year, on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight of <s>Phālguna</s>, the lord of the earth
With his own good fortune, delighted the eyes of celestial women exceedingly. (JRt 38)
2) <s>Paramāṇuka</s> (LS 4230-4240)
Then his son, the foolish <s>Paramāṇuka</s>, was consecrated [as king],
[Insignificant] like a jasmine bush with leaves of the tiniest expanse in the days of <s>Māgha</s> [winter]. (JRt 39)
Shaking off the protection of subjects and disregarding the conquest of the quarters,
The king began tirelessly to amass the treasury. (JRt 40)
Unable to give or enjoy, like a <s>Śrotriya</s> [Vedic scholar] with his wealth,
The rogues <s>Prayāga</s> and <s>Janaka</s> robbed the king of his fortune. (JRt 41)

children.text: tau hi svabhṛtyair nissatyau kāritai rākṣasākṛtim /
children.translated_text: Those two, employing their own servants who were made to assume the appearance of <s>Rākṣasas</s> [demons],

children.text: tam atrāsayatāṃ rātrau rātrau citreṇa karmaṇā || 42 ||
children.translated_text: Terrified him night after night with various devices. (JRt 42)
The two wicked ministers, enacting a pretense of self-sacrifice for him,

children.text: "rakṣāsūn" iti tau vittaṃ tyājayām āsatur nṛpam || 43 ||
children.translated_text: Made the king give up his wealth, saying 'Save your life!' (JRt 43)
Appointing their own dependent in the place of '<s>Bhiṣāyaka</s>' [the Frightener],

children.text: tṛṇacchannaṃ mahāratnaiś caitryāṃ pūjayatas sma tau || 44 ||
children.translated_text: Those two worshipped [him] on the <s>Caitra</s> [full moon] with great jewels covered with grass. (JRt 44)

children.text: sa punaẖ kṛtasaṅketaḫ paśyatsv atha janeṣv aho /
children.translated_text: Then, having made a prearranged signal, while people watched — alas! —

children.text: rājñaẖ kṛtvāśiṣaṃ rātrau sālaṅkāro yayau vanam || 45 ||
children.translated_text: He [the fake demon], having given a blessing to the king at night, went fully adorned into the forest. (JRt 45)
'Since <s>Bhiṣāyaka</s> has accepted your offering and bestowed blessings,

children.text: nirvighnaṃ bhāvi tvadrājyam" iti tau bhūpam ūcatuḥ || 46 ||
children.translated_text: Your kingdom shall be free of obstacles' — thus those two spoke to the king. (JRt 46)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 1

children.text: Bhiṣāyakadine bhṛtyaṃ svaṃ kṛtvā tau Bhiṣāyakam /
children.translated_text: On the day of [the ritual of] <s>Bhiṣāyaka</s>, making their own servant [act as] <s>Bhiṣāyaka</s>,

children.text: ratnair abhyarcya vipinaṃ nītvātha pratyamuñcatām // JRt_B.47 //
children.translated_text: Those two, having worshipped [him] with jewels and led [him] to the forest, then released him. (JRt B.47)
'<s>Kubera</s> [god of wealth] is pleased with you today; adorned with various jewels,

children.text: kṛtvā tavāśiṣaṃ lokasamakṣaṃ sa tirohitaḥ" // JRt_B.48 //
children.translated_text: Having given you his blessing before the people, he has vanished.' (JRt B.48)

children.text:
ity uktvā bhūpates mugdhasya kṛpaṇasya ca /
PrayāgaJanakau dhūrtau prasādaṃ pratyadāpitām // JRt_B.49 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the rogues <s>Prayāga</s> and <s>Janaka</s> got back the gifts from the gullible and wretched king. (JRt B.49)
Thus, showing bogeymen to this lord of an age,

children.text: sandarśya kośaṃ niśśeṣaṃ luṇṭhayāṃ cakratur viṭau || 47 ||
children.translated_text: As [one would] to a child, the two scoundrels plundered the treasury completely. (JRt 47)

children.text: rājā sārdhān navābdān sa kṣmāṃ bhuktvā divasān daśa /
children.translated_text: That king, having ruled the earth for nine and a half years and ten days,
Passed away on the eighth day of the dark fortnight in the year forty of the [Laukika] era. (JRt 48)
3) <s>Vantideva</s> (LS 4240-4247)
<s>Vantideva</s> by name, in the forty-seventh year,
On the tenth day of the bright fortnight of <s>Bhādra</s>, his son, passed away. (JRt 49)
4) <s>Voppadeva</s> (LS 4247-4256)
The one named <s>Voppadeva</s> was made king by the citizens for lack of a suitable [candidate],
Like a <s>Bhiṣāyaka</s> [scarecrow] fashioned of grass receiving worship. (JRt 50)

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sthūlaśilā hṛṣṭo mūḍhas so 'tha svamantriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Upon seeing large stones, the delighted fool then instructed his ministers:
'Let the other [stones] be nourished by suckling!' (JRt 51)
Having heard of the greatness of that place, the foolish [king] along with his ministers
Once went to the shrine of <s>Sureśvarī</s> by boat. (JRt 52)
While making faces at his own reflection in the water,
His jeweled ring fell off when he angrily slapped [the reflection]. (JRt 53)
When asked 'Where is the king's jeweled ring?', he said:
'It fell in the water; the mark [on the water's surface] there is the proof,' so he acted. (JRt 54)
Thus becoming an example [of folly], holding mere nominal kingship over fools,

children.text: navābdāṃś caturo māsān sārdhān dve ca dine vyadhāt || 55 ||
children.translated_text: He ruled for nine years, four months and a half, and two days. (JRt 55)
Then his younger brother <s>Jassaka</s>, though unwilling to bear the burden of the earth,
Was consecrated by the <s>Lavanyas</s>, who were most ignorant, desiring their own advancement. (JRt 56)
Crows that repeat what is said are not captured like parrots;
The earth endures grinding like gravel, not like fertile soil;

children.text: aśmā saindhavavan na jātu gamito niṣpiṣya cūrṇīkṛtiṃ
children.translated_text: A stone is never ground to powder like rock salt;

children.text: keṣāñcid guṇavad guṇāya mahate doṣo 'pi sañjāyate || 57 ||
children.translated_text: For some, even a fault becomes a cause of great virtue. (JRt 57)
Two <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, brothers named <s>Kṣukṣa</s> and <s>Bhīma</s>, dear to that king
On account of their cunning, soon transgressed his commands. (JRt 58)
'We two are powerful and most mighty; how will he tolerate us?'

children.text: bhūpaṃ matvāpi sāmarṣaṃ nānyaṃ vavratur ity amū || 59 ||
children.translated_text: Though considering the king to be wrathful, those two chose no other [master]. (JRt 59)

children.text: svayaṃ yac ca na saṃbheje tayor eko nṛpaśriyam /
children.translated_text: That neither of them personally aspired to royal fortune
Was due to fear of the <s>Lavanyas</s>, not from any scruple about impropriety. (JRt 60)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 2

children.text: tatra hetur Lavanyendrabhayaṃ nānaucitī punaḥ / JRt_B.63ef /
children.translated_text: The reason there was fear of the chief of the <s>Lavanyas</s>, not impropriety. (JRt B.63ef)

children.text: yānty aṅgasaṅgamam anaṅkuśam aṅkayanti rāgaṃ pradarśya hṛdi kampam udañcayanti /
children.translated_text: They come into bodily contact unrestrained, they brand [one with] passion, they show agitation in the heart,

children.text: vyāpādayanti viṣavedanayā viśeṣād viśvāsya duṣṭapiṭikā yuvatīś ca hā dhik || 61 ||
children.translated_text: They especially kill with the pain of poison — alas, wicked boils and young women alike! (JRt 61)
His own wife, repulsed by the weakness of his old age,

children.text: hatvā Kṣukṣaṃ viṣeṇāśu Bhīmaṃ bhogam akārayat || 62 ||
children.translated_text: Having quickly killed <s>Kṣukṣa</s> with poison, took <s>Bhīma</s> as her lover. (JRt 62)
She, marked with white leprosy from her union with her brother-in-law,
Atoned for her sin through gifts to <s>Mādhava</s> and others. (JRt 63)
He [Jassaka], having ruled the earth for eighteen years and thirteen days,
Passed away on the last tenth day of <s>Māgha</s> in the <s>Yuga</s>-era year. (JRt 64)
6) <s>Jagadeva</s> (LS 4274-4289)
Then <s>Śrī Jagadeva</s>, his son, endowed with humility,
Spread the delight of the people even more than the spring season. (JRt 65)
When servants of mutually opposed [factions] were given equal treatment,
There, at the hour of twilight, it was like the union of the <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) and the <s>abja</s> (day lotus). || 66 ||
The lord of the earth, possessing vast knowledge and skill,
removed the thorn of disorder from the land, like a surgeon extracting a thorn. || 67 ||
That king, tormented by the thorn in his mind, possessing extraordinary qualities,
was expelled from the lands by his ministers through the force of intrigue. || 68 ||
He obtained <s>Guṇarāhula</s>, knowledgeable in counsel regarding punishment and reward, as his minister—

children.text: sa prāpat sacivaṃ mitraṃ kapīndram iva Rāghavaḥ || 69 ||
children.translated_text: a friend, as <s>Rāghava</s> obtained the lord of monkeys. || 69 ||
Eager for the attainment of prosperity, together with the lord of heroes and the chief of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
those two wondrous ones then came to the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s>. || 70 ||

children.text: ciraṃ bhuktāṃ śriyaṃ tyaktum anīśās samarodyatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Unable to relinquish the sovereignty long enjoyed, his enemies prepared for battle,
but consumed by the fire of his counsel, the foes attained the state of moths. || 71 ||
Having conquered the earth, the king enjoyed sovereignty adorned with parasol and <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk)—
<s>Lakṣmī</s> without the blemish of misrule—the illustrious <s>Guṇākararāhula</s>. || 72 ||
The king, free from selfish motives, in <s>Rajjupura</s>,
built a temple of <s>Harṣeśvara</s>, bearing the royal parasol of the king of kings. || 73 ||
Through the affection of <s>Padma</s>, who had gained entry at the gate,
the wicked one slew the king by secretly administering poison. || 74 ||

children.text: rakṣitvā kṣitim abdān sa satryahartūṃś caturdaśa /
children.translated_text: Having protected the earth for fourteen years, three seasons, and three days,
he passed away on the fourteenth day of the last <s>Caitra</s> in the year marked by the digits of <s>nanda</s> and eight. || 75 ||
7) <s>Rājadeva</s> (LS 4289-4312)
His son <s>Rājadeva</s> then went to <s>Kāṣṭhavāṭa</s> out of fear,
and was brought back by the adherents of <s>Vāmapārśva</s>, opponents of the gatekeeper. || 76 ||
When he had entered the fortress called <s>Salhaṇa</s>, the wicked <s>Padma</s>,

children.text: aveṣṭayad balaiḫ Padmo maṇḍalair iva pannagam || 77 ||
children.translated_text: surrounded him with troops, as <s>maṇḍalas</s> (coils) surround a serpent. || 77 ||
Distracted by the curiosity of beholding the unprecedented sandals offered as tribute,

children.text: pramattaṃ ko 'pi caṇḍālo dvāreśam avadhīd raṇe || 78 ||
children.translated_text: some <s>Caṇḍāla</s> slew the gatekeeper in battle. || 78 ||
Thereupon, anointed by the <s>Bhaṭṭas</s>, he, to the sound of drums and conches,
received as servants the bowing vassals of endless number. || 79 ||
That extraordinary one, grown mighty as lord of the earth, subjugated the <s>Lavanya</s> chiefs
to the status of resident householders, imposing upon them the burden of established taxes. || 80 ||
He crushed the pride of the wild elephants of the <s>Lavanya</s> forest; that great and brilliant <s>Narasiṃha</s> was like fire to the forests. // JRt_B.84 //

children.text:
Lavanyavanyakariṇāṃ darpanirdalanaṃ vyadhāt /
narasiṃho mahātejā vanānām iva pāvakaḥ // JRt_B.84 //

children.translated_text: The <s>Mallas</s>, the powerful forces of <s>Balāḍhyacandra</s>, lord of <s>Lahara</s>—

children.text: harataś Śrīnagaryardhasvāmyaṃ na prābhavat tu saḥ || 81 ||
children.translated_text: he could not prevail against them as they seized half the dominion of <s>Śrīnagara</s>. || 81 ||
Merit, as if becoming embodied and marked with his own name—
<s>Balāḍhyacandra</s>, of concentrated energy, established a <s>maṭha</s> (monastery) within the city. || 82 ||
"Who is this soft <s>Khaśa</s>? Let someone be anointed by us!"—
thus spoke the <s>Bhaṭṭas</s>, long disregarded by the king. || 83 ||

children.text: "na bhaṭṭo 'haṃ na bhaṭṭo 'haṃ na bhaṭṭo 'ham" idaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: "I am not a <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>! I am not a <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>! I am not a <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>!"—this utterance
was heard even from the <s>Bhaṭṭas</s> when the plundering of the <s>Bhaṭṭas</s> was decreed. || 84 ||
At that very time, <s>Vimalācārya</s>, in the <s>Śaka</s> year marked by sky-nine,
dispelled the confusion of impurity in the month of six-mountain-joy. || 85 ||
Detached from worldly things, <s>Rājadeva</s>, that moon among kings, who had earned auspiciousness since birth,
built <s>Rājapurī</s> and also <s>Rājolaka</s>. || 86 ||
Having protected the earth for twenty-three years,

children.text: māsatrayīṃ ca rājā sa kṣmāṃ rakṣitvā kṣayaṃ yayau || 87 ||
children.translated_text: twenty-seven days, and three months, that king passed away. || 87 ||
8) <s>Saṅgrāmadeva</s> (LS 4312-4328)
<s>Saṅgrāmadeva</s>, his son, devoted to protecting the lineage like a mother,
that lion among kings, inspired terror in the elephants of his enemies. || 88 ||

children.text: visrambhāt Sūryam anujaṃ cakre pratinidhiṃ svayam /
children.translated_text: Out of trust, he himself made his younger brother <s>Sūrya</s> his deputy,

children.text: kucakrikas sa bhogebhyo lubhyan droham acintayat || 89 ||
children.translated_text: but that schemer, lusting after pleasures, plotted treachery. || 89 ||
When his treachery was discovered, <s>Sūrya</s>, frightened of the lord of the earth,
entered the circle of <s>Candra</s>, lord of <s>Lahara</s>, desiring ascendancy. || 90 ||

children.text: dāruṇe raṇakāle sa Sūryaṃ Candrānvitaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: In the terrible time of battle, the lord of the earth then

children.text: svarbhānur iva bhūbhānuś citraṃ samam amīmilat || 91 ||
children.translated_text: eclipsed <s>Sūrya</s> together with <s>Candra</s>, wonderfully, at once—like <s>Svarbhānu</s> (Rāhu). || 91 ||

children.text: Śamālādhipatis Tuṅgas Sūryaṃ pārśvaṃ nayan madāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Tuṅga</s>, the lord of <s>Śamālā</s>, arrogantly taking <s>Sūrya</s>'s side,
was brought to a lowly state by the king who had marshalled his forces. || 92 ||
Wandering at night through paths devoid of moonlight, like a thief,

children.text: viṭatyaktas tatas Sūryo baddhvā rājñā vyapādyata || 93 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūrya</s>, abandoned by his spies, was then captured and executed by the king. || 93 ||

children.text: svalakṣmīṃ rakṣituṃ sākṣāt tasminn āttakṣaṇe prabhau /
children.translated_text: At that very moment when the lord seized his own sovereignty,
the sons of <s>Kalhaṇa</s>, like thieves, caused the terror of serpents. || 94 ||
Having lost hope in his powerful kinsmen, that king

children.text: śiṣṭam iṣṭaṃ ca śaraṇam agād Rājapurīpatim || 95 ||
children.translated_text: then sought refuge with the lord of <s>Rājapurī</s>, the remaining and desired shelter. || 95 ||
When that wielder of punishment had gone far away, the <s>Ḍāmara</s> demons,

children.text: antrāṇy api viśām āśur niśśeṣaṃ raktapāyinaḥ || 96 ||
children.translated_text: blood-drinkers, quickly devoured even the entrails of the people. || 96 ||

children.text: rājñā sumanasā tyaktaṃ dvijaiś ca sparśadūṣitam /
children.translated_text: The food abandoned by the king with a pure mind, and defiled by the touch of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: bhojyaṃ ḌāmaraḌombānāṃ tad rājyānnam abhūc ciram || 97 ||
children.translated_text: became for a long time the royal sustenance of the <s>Ḍāmaras</s> and <s>Ḍombas</s>. || 97 ||
When his own circle had disintegrated, the king, entering the circle of others,
was not approved by anyone, though a new dawn was near. || 98 ||

children.text: pratyakṣato Rājapuryās sa ripūn samare jayan /
children.translated_text: Visibly defeating his enemies in battle before <s>Rājapurī</s>,

children.text: brāhmaṇyāt Kālhaṇīn rakṣan rājyaṃ puṇyaṃ ca labdhavān || 99 ||
children.translated_text: protecting the <s>Kālhaṇīs</s> through his <s>Brāhmaṇya</s> (Brahmanical virtue), he obtained both the kingdom and merit. || 99 ||
That lord of the people built a spacious structure of twenty-one halls,
glorious and vast, at <s>Vijayeśvara</s>, for the residence of cows and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 100 ||
The king became hateful to the agents of <s>Kalhaṇa</s> and to the enemies who desired plunder,
like a lamp to thieves. || 101 ||
That king, a wish-fulfilling tree for poets, whose branches spread to the ends of the directions,
was cut down by the sons of <s>Kalhaṇa</s>, of wicked intentions and persistent malice. || 102 ||
The poet, the learned <s>Yaḥśaka</s>, making that king the hero,
elevated his garland of verses to the status of an ornament for the necks of the learned. || 103 ||

children.text: ṣoḍaśābdān daśāhāni sa bhuktvā kṣmāṃ vyapadyata /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed the earth for sixteen years and ten days, he passed away,
auspicious to the world, on the fifth day of <s>Bhādra</s> in the twenty-eighth year. || 104 ||
9) <s>Rāmadeva</s> (LS 4328-4349)
<s>Rāmadeva</s>, his son, having slain the murderers of his own father,
entrusted the entire burden of the people to <s>Pṛthvīrāja</s>. || 105 ||

children.text: Ledaryā dakṣiṇe bhāge Sallare sa mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: On the southern side of <s>Ledarī</s>, at <s>Sallara</s>, that king
established a fort bearing his own name, like another heap of glory. || 106 ||
Brought to defeat through carelessness in the campaign to conquer <s>Śamālā</s>,
by him the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in <s>Utpalapura</s> was renovated. || 107 ||

In the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, in the dark fortnight, on the twelfth day, in the thirtieth year, on a Monday, with devotion, when King <s>Rāma</s> was protecting the earth, his beloved, <s>Pṛthvīrāja</s>, at the time of the conquest of <s>Śamālā</s>, having restored the image of <s>Murāri</s> (Viṣṇu) that had been broken by the <s>Dasyus</s> (robbers) to its complete form, performed its consecration in the city of <s>Utpalapura</s>. // JRt_B.112 //

children.text:
vaiśākhe māsi pakṣe śaśadharaviṣade triṃśadabde sabhaktyā
dvādaśyāṃ Rāmarāje kṣitim avati nijapreyasīṃ somavāre /
Pṛthvīrājaś Śamālāvijayanasamaye Dasyubhagnaṃ Murāriṃ
sampūrṇāṅgaṃ vidhāyOtpalapuranagare svapratiṣṭhāṃ cakāra // JRt_B.112 //

children.translated_text: A flower of the sandalwood tree, a fruit of the <s>campaka</s> tree—

children.text: apatyaṃ tasya bhūpasya hanta nākāri Vedhasā || 108 ||
children.translated_text: alas, offspring of that king was not created by <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Creator). || 108 ||
He, of a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> residing in <s>Bhiṣāyaka</s>,
adopted the son named <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> as his own son, that king. || 109 ||
The genuine affection between father and son, a greater love,
made the two incomparably close, as if they were naturally suited to each other, like a painting. || 110 ||
The queen named <s>Śrīsamudrā</s>, born of the ocean of <s>Vimudrita</s>,
built a <s>maṭha</s> (monastery) bearing her own name within the city on the <s>Vitastā</s> (river). || 111 ||
Having enjoyed the earth for twenty-one years, one month, and thirteen days,

children.text: kṣmāṃ bhuktvaikonapañcāśe varṣe 'sau dyām agāt svayam || 112 ||
children.translated_text: he himself departed to heaven in the forty-ninth year. || 112 ||
10) <s>Lakṣmadeva</s> (LS 4349-4362)
Then <s>Lakṣmadeva</s>, with difficulty, distressed by his limbs being torn apart,

children.text: tām ākaṇṭakinīṃ vallīm iva kṣoṇīṃ babhāra saḥ || 113 ||
children.translated_text: bore that thorny creeper of the earth. || 113 ||
Though made a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, the king of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> origin did not abandon his own <s>dharma</s>—
even a stone, when polished, never possesses the splendor of a gem. || 114 ||
On the bank of the <s>Vitastā</s>, next to her mother-in-law's <s>maṭha</s> (monastery), a new <s>maṭha</s>,
the blameless Queen <s>Ahalā</s> built, bearing her own name. || 115 ||
Then <s>Kajjala</s>, a <s>Turuṣka</s> (Turk), having come from outside into the domain,
that impure one destroyed the sight of the people, tearing it out and causing blood to flow. || 116 ||

children.text: trayodaśābdān māsāṃs trīn dvādaśāhaṃ ca bhūpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed the earth for thirteen years, three months, and twelve days, the king
passed away at the end of <s>Pauṣa</s> in the sixty-second year. || 117 ||
11) <s>Siṃhadeva</s> (LS 4362-4377)
Due to the calamity caused by <s>Kajjala</s>, being merely the lord of <s>Ledarī</s>,
<s>Siṃhadeva</s> then, imperturbable with <s>Saṅgrāmacandra</s>, became king. || 118 ||

children.text: nagarāntar maṭhaṃ kṛtvā Laharendre mṛte sati /
children.translated_text: Having built a <s>maṭha</s> (monastery) within the city, after the lord of <s>Lahara</s> had died,
<s>Siṃhadeva</s>, like <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, then protected the earth afflicted by decline. || 119 ||
<s>Siṃhadeva</s>, accompanied by his teacher named <s>Siṃha</s>, at the <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> (temple),
performed the consecration at <s>Dhyānoḍḍāra</s>, that accomplished one, when the zodiacal sign was Leo. || 120 ||

children.text: kartā kāryaṃ ca lagnaṃ ca gurus siṃhaś ca kovidaḥ /
children.translated_text: The agent, the act, the zodiacal sign, the learned teacher—all were 'lion' (<s>siṃha</s>);
this succession of lions would fall into his observance. || 121 ||
He, by means of a hundred thousand measures of purchased milk, bathed <s>Vijayeśvara</s>

children.text: ekāha eva snapayan vrataśuddhiṃ yayau nṛpaḥ || 122 ||
children.translated_text: in a single day, and the king attained the purity of his vow. || 122 ||
The king's teacher, the revered <s>Śaṅkarasvāmī</s>, who imparted mantra-initiation,
was honored with the gifts of lordship over eighteen <s>maṭhas</s> (monasteries). || 123 ||
As a means of conquering the next world, an offering to <s>Vāgdevī</s> (Sarasvatī), the king
constantly recited this verse of his own composition upon rising from bed: || 124 ||
"I worship <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), Lord of <s>Gaurī</s>, whose gaze is pure as fire,
whose feet are worshipped by hosts of gods, adorned with the crescent moon upon his brow." || 125 ||
Ps-JRT 5
For the giving of water to travelers, for the offering of libations to the ancestors,
for the destruction of sins of the couple, and for the increase of <s>dharma</s>— // JRt_B.131 //
a drinking fountain was constructed on the road by the gift of her own ornaments,
at the border of the village of <s>Maḍavāśrama</s>, by <s>Gaurī</s>, the wife of <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // JRt_B.132 //

children.text:
Khonamoṣādhipasyāsīt kanyā Prajjadvijasya sā /
satyaśīlānvitā bhaktā Gaurī Gaurīva Śaṅkare // JRt_B.133 //
children.translated_text: She was the daughter of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Prajja</s>, lord of <s>Khonamoṣa</s>; that <s>Gaurī</s>, endowed with truth and virtue, devoted to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, was like <s>Gaurī</s> (Pārvatī) herself. // JRt_B.133 //

children.text: duhitur duścaritreṇa yo 'bhūd daṇḍaḫ pituḫ patan /
children.translated_text: The punishment that was falling upon the father due to the daughter's misconduct—
the king, entreated by the dancer <s>Iḍāgalyā</s>, averted it. || 126 ||
He, through the embrace of wicked people, was bereft of righteous wisdom,
and reflected his own self in the mirror of passion through a foster-sister. || 127 ||
<s>Darya</s>, the husband of his sister, instigated by <s>Kāmasūha</s>,
treacherously slew him, whose subjects had become alienated and whose discipline had been abandoned. || 128 ||
Having been king for fourteen years, six months less three days,

children.text: bhūtvā śucau divam agāt sa varṣe saptasaptate || 129 ||
children.translated_text: he departed to heaven in the pure month, in the year seventy-seven. || 129 ||
His brother <s>Sūhadeva</s> then, instigated by <s>Kāmasūha</s>,

children.text: jaḍo 'pi sakalām eva Kaśmīrakṣmāṃ vaśe vyadhāt || 130 ||
children.translated_text: though dull-witted, brought the entire land of <s>Kaśmīra</s> under his control. || 130 ||
Having come from distant quarters, many, desiring livelihood,
took refuge with that king, as bees resort to a flowering tree. || 131 ||
Ps-JRT 6
For livelihood, <s>Laṅkāracakka</s> too came from the <s>Darad</s> country at that time,
destined for future sovereignty, to the extensive domain of <s>Kaśmīra</s>. // JRt_B.140 //

children.text:
Kramarājyābhidhe rāṣṭre Trāhagrāmaṃ nṛgrāmaṇīḥ /
dadau vasataye tasmai niyates sa niyogataḥ // JRt_B.141 //
children.translated_text: In the kingdom called <s>Kramarājya</s>, the chief of men gave the village of <s>Trāha</s> to him for his residence; he was appointed by official decree. // JRt_B.141 //
Another one became like <s>Pārtha</s> (Arjuna), a veritable <s>Pārtha</s>, at the border of <s>Pañcagahvara</s>—
His son was <s>Babhruvāhana</s>, who built <s>Garbharapura</s>.
From his lineage arose <s>Kuruśāha</s>, upon the mountain of whose arm's rise,
the night assumed the guise of bowstring-marks and partook of fame having white radiance.
"<s>Kaśmīra</s> is <s>Pārvatī</s> there, and the king is to be known as born from a portion of <s>Hara</s>"—
as if to confirm this very conviction, he had three eyes.
In <s>Kaśmīra</s>, the lineage of <s>Kuruśāha</s> shall exercise sovereignty;
led by <s>Śaṃśadīna</s> and others, it shall attain celebrated fame.
From him was born <s>Tāharāja</s>, whose bowstring, resorted to with restlessness,
again and again, alas, reached the very end of hearing.
Then was born <s>Śāhamera</s>, a sun whose summer was the heat of his own valor,
whose fire of prowess was kindled by the tears of enemy women.
Once, while <s>Śāhmera</s> was sporting in the forest,

children.text: mṛgayā prathamaṃ dṛṣṭiṃ paścān nidrā vyalobhayat || 138 ||
children.translated_text: hunting first captivated his gaze, and then sleep enticed him.

children.text: "rājyam ā santater bhāvi Kaśmīreṣu tave"ti saḥ /
children.translated_text: "The kingdom in <s>Kaśmīra</s> shall be yours up to your descendants"—thus he
was consecrated in a dream there by the <s>Mahādevī</s> (Great Goddess) with the nectar of her words.
In the <s>Śaka</s> year measured by five, fires, and suns, in the year marked by nine, eight, and zero,

children.text: tatas saparivāras sa Kaśmīrān aviśac chanaiḥ || 140 ||
children.translated_text: then, with his retinue, he gradually entered <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
The king graciously received him as he came with his family, by granting him a livelihood,
with distinction, as a mango tree receives a bee.
The one named <s>Ḍalaca</s>, the general of the emperor <s>Karmasena</s>,

children.text: Kaśmīrān sa tadaivāgāt siṃho mṛgaguhām iva || 142 ||
children.translated_text: entered <s>Kaśmīra</s> at that very time, like a lion entering a deer's den.
As if to grant lordship over sixty thousand villages there,
he brought that same number of thousands of horsemen in his army.
The king, wishing to turn back <s>Ḍalca</s> through a payment of wealth,

children.text: sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ durvarṇo daṇḍam akṣipat || 144 ||
children.translated_text: imposed a tax that discolored all the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).
At the king's wrath regarding the sin of accepting that [tax], requiring the offering of life-breath,
the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, resorting to fasting unto death, performed an irregular act of penance.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 7

children.text:
daṇḍaduẖkhena viprair yaś śāpo datto mahībhujaḥ /
bhaviṣyan vaṃśavicchedo dhruvaṃ tasyaiva tat phalam // JRt_B.156 //
children.translated_text: The curse given by the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> upon the king due to the suffering of taxation— the extinction of his lineage shall certainly be its fruit.
At that very time, by the <s>Bhautta</s> people called <s>Kālamānya</s>, who had struck down enemies,
a kinsman of his clan, <s>Bakatanya</s>, was treacherously slain.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 8
In his own land, the one called <s>Vakatanya</s>, the son of his clansman, was killed.
The venerable one of uncommon intellect, a forest fire to the <s>Kālamānya</s> lineage—

children.text: avāśiṣyata tatputro daivād ekas sa Riñcanaḥ || 147 ||
children.translated_text: of his sons, by fate only one survived, that <s>Riñcana</s>.
Then, with <s>Vyāla</s>, <s>Ṭakka</s>, and others connected by the thread of counsel,

children.text: baddhvā saṃhatikanthāṃ sa tāñ jaḍāñ jetum iṣṭavān || 148 ||
children.translated_text: having tied the neck of their alliance, he desired to conquer those dull-witted ones.
"He seeks me as a servant when my treasury is about to be emptied"—thus he
proclaimed through the mouth of a messenger to those assassins.
That lion among men, on the riverbank, with weapons concealed under sand,

children.text: tān pratyaikṣata raktasya na tu kośasya pītaye || 150 ||
children.translated_text: awaited them—for the drinking of blood, not of treasure.
The <s>Kālamānyas</s>, led by <s>Vyāla</s> and others, came there unarmed,
and were reduced to straw by the hidden fire of his weapons buried in the sand.
Having washed away the stain of dust from the betrayal of his father with the blood of enemies,
he came to <s>Kaśmīra</s> with his kinsmen, driven by fear of the remaining enemies.
The king, like the full <s>Rāmacandra</s> (moon), whose splendor was stolen by another,
endured the rise of <s>Riñca-Rāhu</s> in the dark-blue sky of <s>Nīlā</s>.
While hope torments with weapons <s>Ḍalaca</s> on the dark path,
all the <s>Kāśmīrika</s> people attained the state of moths.
With <s>Ḍalca</s> and <s>Riñca</s> blocking the east and the north, many people

children.text: vasateḫ paścimām āśāṃ prāg Yamāśām athāgamat || 155 ||
children.translated_text: from their western dwelling first reached the direction of <s>Yama</s> (death).
Below, fear from the flood of <s>Ḍalca</s>, and on the mountain, from the wind of <s>Riñcana</s>—
such was the plight then of the fruit-laden <s>puṃnāga</s> trees sheltering in shade.
Like a bird's nestling dislodged from its place, with trembling wings,
the youthful splendor of <s>Riñcana</s> carried away the <s>Kāśmīrika</s> world.
Having obtained a flood of wealth from the <s>Bhauṭṭas</s> through the sale of <s>Kāśmīra</s> people,

children.text: garjann āśāḫ pyadhāt sarvās tadā Riñcanavāridaḥ || 158 ||
children.translated_text: the rain-cloud <s>Riñcana</s> then thundered and covered all directions.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 9
<s>Ḍuluca</s>, with the earth's surface covered by armies of <s>Turuṣkas</s>, <s>Tājikas</s>, and <s>Mlecchas</s>,

children.text: Ḍulucyo nagaraṃ prāpad athāgastya ivārṇavam // JRt_B.170 //
children.translated_text: reached the city like <s>Agastya</s> approaching the ocean.
Like deer seeing a mighty lion, like birds seeing <s>Garutmān</s> (Garuḍa),

children.text: tam āpatantam ālokya palāyanta puraukasaḥ // JRt_B.171 //
children.translated_text: the city-dwellers fled upon beholding him approaching.
Those who fled were caught by him, like serpents by a snake-charmer;

children.text: kecit palāyitā bhītyā praviṣṭā girigahvaram // JRt_B.172 //
children.translated_text: some who fled in fear entered mountain caves.

children.text: rājāpi kvāpi sañchanno bhītyā ghūkavad āsta saḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the king hid somewhere in fear, sitting like an owl;

children.text: itareṣāṃ tu lokānāṃ kā kathā tatra vāsinām // JRt_B.173 //
children.translated_text: what then can be said of the other people dwelling there?

children.text: vipraśāpo narendrāṇāṃ vṛthā jāto na jātucit /
children.translated_text: The curse of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> upon kings never goes in vain;

children.text: salakṣmā rājayakṣmā hi nāhatvā vinivartate // JRt_B.174 //
children.translated_text: indeed, the royal consumption (<s>rājayakṣmā</s>), marked with fortune, does not turn back without killing.
First, people were made to give up hidden wealth through severe bondage and torture;

children.text: vikrītā vājibhiḫ paścāt Turuṣkair hastagā janāḥ // JRt_B.175 //
children.translated_text: afterward, those in hand were sold by the <s>Turuṣkas</s> for horses.

children.text: viddhāẖ kecit pare baddhā virāddhās tena kecana /
children.translated_text: Some were pierced, others bound, some were injured by him;

children.text: ploṣaṃ kecit pare śoṣaṃ doṣaṃ yānty analād drumāḥ // JRt_B.176 //
children.translated_text: some to burning, others to withering—trees suffer harm from fire.
The captives, bound by a single leather strap pierced through their collar-bones,

children.text: teṣāṃ durāpam apy āsīd anyo'nyamukhadarśanam // JRt_B.177 //
children.translated_text: found it difficult even to see one another's faces.
Moment by moment, the captives were released by the <s>Mlecchas</s>

children.text: baddhā Mlecchair amucyanta biḍālair iva mūṣakāḥ // JRt_B.178 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of carrying loads of grass, firewood, and other supplies, like mice by cats.
Those who felt disgust at food due to the contamination of a cat's touch—

children.text: Mlecchocchiṣṭaṃ gavāṃś cāsthi tair baddhair bhakṣitaṃ kṣudhā // JRt_B.179 //
children.translated_text: those captives ate the leftovers of <s>Mlecchas</s> and the bones of cows out of hunger.

children.text: vaitastam api ye vāri na papuḫ paṅkasaṅkulam /
children.translated_text: Those who would not even drink the muddy water of the <s>Vitastā</s>—

children.text: baddhair maruṣu tair nītair mūtraṃ pītaṃ bhṛśaṃ tṛṣā // JRt_B.180 //
children.translated_text: those captives, led into deserts, drank urine out of severe thirst.

children.text: "kva Mlecchānnaṃ kva vaṃśo no dussahā kṣuc chrutena kim /
children.translated_text: "Where is the food of <s>Mlecchas</s> and where is our lineage? Unbearable is hunger—what use is learning?

children.text: nidrā nādyāpi mārgeṇa" te 'ntar evam acintayan // JRt_B.181 //
children.translated_text: Sleep has not come even by now through the road"—thus they pondered within.

children.text: gacchatāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ teṣām aśnatāṃ jalpatām api /
children.translated_text: Whether they walked, stood, ate, or spoke,

children.text: so 'bhūn naiva kṣaṇo yatra na te kāryam asādhayan // JRt_B.182 //
children.translated_text: there was not a single moment when they were not made to work.

children.text: Mlecchaiẖ kecit Khaśaiẖ kecid Daradbhir apare tathā /
children.translated_text: Some people were captured by <s>Mlecchas</s>, some by <s>Khaśas</s>, others by <s>Daradas</s>,

children.text: Bhoṭṭaiẖ kecit Turuṣkaiś ca kecid bandīkṛtā janāḥ // JRt_B.183 //
children.translated_text: some by <s>Bhoṭṭas</s>, and some by <s>Turuṣkas</s>.

children.text: annaṃ gṛhe vane vittaṃ mārge bandhūn vihāya ca /
children.translated_text: Abandoning food at home, wealth in the forest, and kinsmen on the road,
others fled in panic from fear of the <s>Turuṣkas</s>.
Compassion, respect, and pity—for those unable to go swiftly,
these fleeing ones abandoned children, the elderly, and women.

children.text: na bhuktaṃ kṣudhitair mārge na pītaṃ tṛṣitair api /
children.translated_text: The hungry did not eat on the road, the thirsty did not drink;

children.text: kim anyad bhayasaṃbhrāntaiḫ paścāt tair nāpi vīkṣitam // JRt_B.186 //
children.translated_text: what more—those bewildered by fear did not even look back.

children.text: kṣudhā kecit tṛṣā kecid bhiyā kecit pare hriyā /
children.translated_text: Some perished from hunger, some from thirst, some from fear, others from shame,

children.text: bhayād biladarīṣv eva praviśyāntar vipedire // JRt_B.187 //
children.translated_text: having entered caves and pits out of fear, they died inside.
Hearing that those people had entered caves, desiring to drive them out,

children.text: niṣkāruṇyās Turuṣkās te dhūmaṃ bilamukhe daduḥ // JRt_B.188 //
children.translated_text: the merciless <s>Turuṣkas</s> filled the cave mouths with smoke.
Of the people who perished inside from smoke, their remains are unstable;

children.text: dṛśyante 'dyāpi dhūmotthaṃ mālinyaṃ ca guhāmukhe // JRt_B.189 //
children.translated_text: even today, the discoloration from smoke can be seen at the mouths of caves.

children.text:
rājāpacāram akarot prajāsu phalitas tu saḥ /
nārīṇāṃ capalā dṛṣṭir dantair gaṇḍas tu khaṇḍyate // JRt_B.190 //
children.translated_text: The king committed offenses against the people, and that bore fruit; the fickle glance of women—the cheek is indeed shattered by teeth.
Then <s>Ḍalca</s>, having destroyed the entire land, troubled by severe cold and fear,
departed from <s>Kaśmīra</s> by the route of <s>Tārabala</s>.
The <s>Kāśmīrika</s> people, like mice from fortress-holes,
after <s>Ḍalaca</s>'s departure emerged—those who remained, the rest having been captured.

children.text: nālabdha pitaraṃ putraḫ pitā taṃ ca na kañcana /
children.translated_text: A son did not find his father, nor a father his [son];
nor brothers their brothers, after the catastrophe of the demon <s>Ḍalca</s>.
With few people, barren fields, without food, overgrown with <s>darbha</s> grass,

children.text: sargārambha iva prāyas tadā Kaśmīrabhūr abhūt || 162 ||
children.translated_text: the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s> was then almost as if at the beginning of creation.

children.text: samarthān nyagrahīd Ḍalco Riñcanaḫ prābhavat punaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ḍalca</s> subdued the powerful; <s>Riñcana</s> then rose to power again—
when darkness blinds the world, paramours find their pleasure.
The king, freed from the <s>Rāhu</s> of <s>Ḍalca</s>, [was challenged] with a horn touching the heights—
<s>Riñcana</s> then became the setting mountain for him.
Seeing <s>Riñcana</s> blazing, stationed on the peak of <s>Gaganagiri</s>,
no one doubted that the king's setting was imminent.
For the hawk-king <s>Riñcana</s>, who desired to seize the city as his prey,

children.text: kulacandro Rāmacandro vighnaṃ cakre pade pade || 166 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāmacandra</s>, the moon of his family, created obstacles at every step.
The <s>Bhauṭṭas</s>, from within <s>Laharakoṭṭa</s>, out of eagerness for the sale of silk,
<s>Riñcana</s>, ever engaged in schemes of deception, then released them.
When the <s>Bhoṭṭa</s> people were likewise admitted within <s>Lahara</s>,
<s>Riñcana</s> drank the honey of <s>Rāmacandra</s>'s tears with his weapons.
<s>Riñcana</s>, the great-armed one, placed <s>Koṭādevī</s>,
the wish-fulfilling creeper of <s>Rāmacandra</s>'s family garden, upon his chest.
Out of fear of glorious <s>Riñcana</s>, the king then abandoned the city;
for those burned by the fire of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s curse, whence could there be a sprout of prosperity?
The king, frightened, then entered the cave of <s>Pramaṇḍala</s>;

children.text: pāpasya tādṛśo mṛtyus sammukhasya raṇe katham || 171 ||
children.translated_text: for a sinner, how can such a death—face-to-face in battle—come?
Wondrously, the enemy, a wielder of sword-edge, by raining the king's blood in battle,
brought an eclipse upon the eyes of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who had been taxed.
For nineteen years less five days and four months,
that royal demon devoured the earth under the pretext of protection.
13) <s>Lha·chen rgyal·bu Rin·chen</s> (LS 4396-4399)
The glorious <s>Riñcana</s>, protector of the gods, through the pathway of his arm's wind,
put to rest the earth which was already exhausted by calamities of instability from misgovernance.
As a man sees everything previously seen when darkness is removed,
so the realm of <s>Kaśmīra</s> beheld the happiness of the former king.

children.text: dīpair iva pratisthānaṃ yair Lavanyais sthiraṃ sthitam /
children.translated_text: By those <s>Lavanyas</s>, like lamps through which the capital stood firmly established,
they were shaken by the strong wind of the king's dawn.
When a breach was made by the needle of counsel and the thread-arrow entered,
wondrously, the neck-bond of the <s>Lavanyas</s> became loosened then.
Where in the forest one would be troubled, naked among thorny plants,

children.text: tatraiva vyomni pattrīva deśe samacaran nṛpaḥ || 178 ||
children.translated_text: there the king moved freely like a bird in the sky of that land.
Of that one, skilled in courtesy, for the welfare of the people,

children.text: putre mantriṇi mitre vā duṣṭe nālakṣyata kṣamā || 179 ||
children.translated_text: forgiveness was not seen toward a son, minister, or friend when they were wicked.
Dealing blows to enemies of no small stature whose fortune was surging,
that parasol-bearing one once went for an excursion.
A <s>Ṭakka</s> brother named <s>Timir</s>, distressed by heat on the road,

children.text: gopālyāẖ kutracid grāme kṣīraṃ niṣpītavān haṭhāt || 181 ||
children.translated_text: at some village forcibly drank the milk of a cowherd woman.
When the king was informed, the cowherd woman then

children.text: anuyuktas Timir bhītyā vyadhāt sarvasya nihnavam || 182 ||
children.translated_text: questioned <s>Timir</s>, who out of fear denied everything.

children.text: asatye bhāvitā gopī yadā dhairyān na sāskhalat /
children.translated_text: When the cowherd woman, firm in truth, did not falter from her steadfastness,

children.text: pānāśayaṃ Timer eva sa satyaikṣī vyadārayat || 183 ||
children.translated_text: that truth-seer [the king] had <s>Timir</s>'s stomach cut open to reveal the drinking.
From his drinking vessel, through a stream of milk that flowed out,

children.text: rājñaẖ kīrtir mukhaśrīś ca gopyāḫ prāpat prasannatām || 184 ||
children.translated_text: the king's fame and the beauty of his face, like that of the cows, attained serenity.
While two were dwelling in <s>Vāravāla</s>, in some forest,

children.text: aśve kiśorakau tulyau kasminn api vanāntare || 185 ||
children.translated_text: two colts of equal age belonging to certain mares lost their breath.
One of the two mares in the forest, whose offspring had been seized by a lion,
out of maternal affection due to resemblance with her own horse, wished to adopt the other's foal.
"This one is mine! This one is mine!" — thus, having reached no certainty,
the two owners of the mares went in agitation to the king's presence.

children.text: sa vivādaṃ tayoś śrutvā svāntikaṃ svīyamānuṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard their dispute, he, through his own men, to his own presence,

children.text: vaḍave ca kiśoraṃ ca rājābhyānāyayat tataḥ || 188 ||
children.translated_text: the king then had both the mares and the colt brought.

children.text: tasmin kiśorake bālyād dūraṃ dhāvati līlayā /
children.translated_text: When that colt, due to its youth, playfully ran far away,

children.text: mātā dhātrī ca nitarām asnihyac cāpy aheṣayat || 189 ||
children.translated_text: the mother and the nurse both showed great affection and also neighed.
While the courtiers remained silent and motionless, and the litigants were agitated and ready,
they brought the horses to the middle of the <s>Vitastā</s> river in a boat, along with the colt.

children.text: bālāśvaṃ pātitaṃ nadyāṃ nāvo rājñā mahādhiyā /
children.translated_text: The young horse was thrown into the river from the boat by the wise king;

children.text: haṭhād anvapatan mātā parā param aheṣayat || 191 ||
children.translated_text: the mother forcibly jumped in after it, while the other merely neighed.
Thus, in that king who resolved doubtful cases,

children.text: tasmin rājñi jano 'maṃsta kṛtaṃ yugam ivāgatam || 192 ||
children.translated_text: the people believed the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> (Golden Age) had returned.
The king, seeking <s>Śaiva</s> initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) from <s>Śrī Devasvāmin</s>,
was not accepted by him, due to being a <s>Bhauṭṭa</s>, out of suspicion of his unworthiness.

children.text: anujas tanujo bandhur mantrī sahacaras sakhā /
children.translated_text: A younger brother, a son, a kinsman, a minister, a companion, a friend —
<s>Vyālarāja</s> was all these to the king, through his steadfast devotion to truth alone.

children.text: jahau Vyālaẖ kṛtaṃ rājñā na sa Vyālakṛtaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāla</s> abandoned what the king had done, but the king did not abandon what <s>Vyāla</s> had done;

children.text: mano hi kāyikaṃ hanti tatkṛtaṃ na vapuḫ punaḥ || 195 ||
children.translated_text: for the mind destroys what is done by the body, but what is done by the mind, the body does not destroy.
In <s>Vyāla</s>, a treasury of arts and full of aesthetic sentiment, the radiance of the light of the earth,

children.text: mūrchitā rucir acchaitsīd acchedyaṃ jagatāṃ tamaḥ || 196 ||
children.translated_text: having intensified, cut through the impenetrable darkness of the world.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 11
In order to easily turn back <s>Ḍulcya</s>, who wished to enter <s>Kaśmīra</s>,

children.text: Ḍulcyaṃ dhanaprayogeṇa yo visṛṣṭo mahībhujā // JRt_B.229 //
children.translated_text: he was dispatched by the king with an expenditure of wealth.

children.text:
avamantrya praviṣṭe 'tha Ḍulucye bhayato gataḥ /
Gāndhāradeśaṃ Udyānadevo labdhāntaras tataḥ // JRt_B.230 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Ḍulucya</s> entered after being deceived, <s>Udyānadeva</s>, out of fear, went to the <s>Gāndhāra</s> country, and then, having found an opportunity,
the illustrious <s>Udyānadeva</s>, intent on striking at the weak point,
stationed in <s>Gāndhāra</s>, incited the <s>Ṭakkas</s> and others out of fear, thus:
"Even while alive, one must go to that other city, I know,
which is served by a master who, lacking discernment, is driven by desire for honor.

children.text: bhuṅkte Vyālaś śriyaṃ prāṇapaṇair yuṣmābhir arjitām /
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāla</s> enjoys the royal fortune earned by you at the cost of your lives;
the hands toil hard while the tongue enjoys the pleasures.
The lord, his body smeared with ashes, wishes to carry off <s>Vyāla</s>,

children.text: anāsthāṃ tu suvarṇeṣu yuṣmāsu vidadhāti saḥ || 200 ||
children.translated_text: but he shows indifference towards you, who are like gold.
The king, making mere milk-drinking the pretext,
out of suspicion of your valor, killed <s>Timi</s> as one would kill a fish.
Thus split apart by such messages, the <s>Ṭakkas</s> and others, marked by the white (of rebellion),

children.text: Viṃśaprasthe kadācit te prajahrur atha bhūbhujam || 202 ||
children.translated_text: at <s>Viṃśaprastha</s>, at some point, attacked the king.
Through the blows of their sword-edges, <s>Vyāla</s> drove out from their hearts
the burning pain of his own sovereignty; the king, however, merely fainted.
Then, those who considered themselves victorious, their pride swollen by his supposed death,
went arrogantly toward the city to seize the kingdom.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ mṛta iva sthitvā bhūyoghātabhayān nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having remained for a moment as if dead, the king, seeing the enemies had gone far away

children.text: dūraṃ gatān ripūn dṛṣṭvā rājye rājodatiṣṭhata || 205 ||
children.translated_text: out of fear of further blows, arose again to his kingdom.

children.text: ārukṣan rājadhānīṃ te yāvat tāvan narādhipam /
children.translated_text: Just as they were ascending to the capital, those of petty minds
saw the king approaching, having recovered from his faint.

children.text: "tvayā kiṃ na tvayā kiṃ na hato rāje"ty anītayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Was it you who did not kill the king, or was it you?" — thus, those lacking in strategy,
fell into mutual quarrel and became agitated at that very moment, those fools.
Bearing mutual grudges and plundering one another from the royal palace,

children.text: kartavyaṃ maraṇaṃ rājñā vyadhus svasya svayaṃ jaḍāḥ || 208 ||
children.translated_text: the fools brought upon themselves the death that the king should have accomplished.
The king then dealt with the remaining wicked ones only by impalement,
the proud one raised them high, but sent them to the lowest state forever.
In his rage, that king tore open a pregnant woman of the enemy's fortress
with swords, as one would tear open a pod containing grain-seeds with nails.
The torment born of rage against the traitors, through the slaughter of their entire clan,

children.text: citte śāntim agāt khaḍgaghātotthā na tu mūrdhani || 211 ||
children.translated_text: found peace in his mind, but the wound from the sword-blow on his head did not.

children.text: dussvapnam iva tad dṛṣṭvā Ṭakkādicaritaṃ kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Seeing the conduct of the <s>Ṭakkas</s> and others as if a bad dream, in a moment,

children.text: prabuddheva punaḫ prāpad abhayena śamaṃ mahī || 212 ||
children.translated_text: the earth, as if awakened, again attained peace through fearlessness.
The king, with a contented mind, in loyal <s>Śāhmera</s>,
gave his son <s>Haidara</s>, together with <s>Koṭā</s> as his foster-mother, for his upbringing.
Nourished by Queen <s>Koṭā</s>, like a tree in the rainy season,
<s>Śāhmera</s>, with his leaves (qualities) shining, provided good shade and served well.
The king built a city bearing his own name, surrounded by a moat — a pretext —

children.text: parito valitaṃ rājā svanāmāṅkaṃ puraṃ vyadhāt || 215 ||
children.translated_text: encircled by the infamy born of his own defeat.
Like a winter sun on a cloudy day in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, the king

children.text: māsāṃś ca katicid bhūyaḫ prakāśam akarod bhuvaḥ || 216 ||
children.translated_text: illuminated the earth for a few more months.
In winter, through the affliction of the harshness of cold, the king's
headache was greatly seized by the fury of the wind, causing severe congestion.
Of the king who had the glory of relieving the pain of many heads at all times,
the pain of his own head, alas, increased greatly.
Then, on the <s>Ekādaśī</s> (eleventh day) in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, in the year marked by nine and nine,
the agony of death was removed by the physician of death from the king.

children.text: ekādaśadinair nyūnau māsau trīn vatsarān api /
children.translated_text: Having protected the earth for three years and three months less eleven days,

children.text: kṣamāṃ saṃrakṣya sa svargaṃ yayau Riñcanabhūpatiḥ || 220 ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Riñcana</s> went to heaven.
14) <s>Udyānadeva</s> (LS 4399-4414)
His son, named <s>Haidara</s>, being young, was not consecrated;
not having the capacity for such a task, he could not bear the burden of the kingdom even on his own.
Through the <s>Lavanyas</s>, because of their clan-lordship, and despite resentment toward <s>Riñcana</s>,
the wise <s>Śāhmeraka</s> had unobstructed hopes of entry.
Together with Queen <s>Śrī Koṭā</s>, as if embodiments of the goddess of victory,
he then made that <s>Udyānadeva</s> attain the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
The great swing of royal fortune, bound by virtues and weighty,
having gone to the high seat of <s>Riñcana</s>, now descended to the king below.
The king then pleased <s>Jyaṃśir</s> and <s>Āleśir</s>, the two sons of <s>Śāhmera</s>,
by granting them lordship over <s>Kramarājya</s> and other territories.

children.text: dhīr ivāsīt tadā Koṭā devī sarvādhikāriṇī /
children.translated_text: Queen <s>Koṭā</s> was then like the intellect itself, having authority over all affairs;
the king, like the body, carried out exactly what she directed.
Those lights of the <s>Lavanyas</s>, which had been concealed by the brilliance
of <s>Riñcana</s> the sun, arose at the twilight of that king's reign.
He whose household was occupied by his wife <s>Koṭā</s> — the gentle one —

children.text: viṣayākramaṇaṃ tasya Lavanyaiẖ kiṃ nu śocyate || 228 ||
children.translated_text: why should the invasion of his territory by the <s>Lavanyas</s> be mourned?
Avoiding contact with the houses of <s>Caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts) in the <s>Lavanya</s> territory,
he, like a learned Brahmin, spent his time in bathing, austerity, and prayer.
How much can the piety of that upholder of <s>varṇa</s> (caste) be described —
he who tied a bell to his horse's neck out of fear of crushing insects!
Meanwhile, granting his treasury the quality of mere monetary wealth as its ornament,
he offered to Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>Cakrin</s>) a golden necklace together with a crown.
Then, <s>Acala</s>, emboldened by the army given by the lord of <s>Mugdhapura</s>,
looked upon <s>Kaśmīra</s> forcefully, like another <s>Ḍalca</s>.
He who, with his own forces, dashes hopes and conquers the earth with his army —

children.text: nĀcale gotrabhittvaṃ sa kartum aiṣṭa mahīvṛṣā || 233 ||
children.translated_text: that bull among kings did not desire to achieve <s>Acala</s>'s destruction of his lineage.

children.text: prāpte Bhīmānakaṃ tasmin sasainye dainyam āśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: When that one, together with his army, reached <s>Bhīmānaka</s>, having fallen into distress,
the lord of the earth quickly went to the <s>Bhoṭṭa</s> country out of fear.
"Turn back your army; what is the point of needlessly tormenting the country?
The kingless <s>Kaśmīrīs</s> are to be protected by you as their clan-lord."
Thus, through letter-bearers sent by Queen <s>Śrī Koṭā</s> and the ministers,
<s>Acala</s>, deluded, released his rain-like army.
Having released his rain-like forces, <s>Acala</s>, rendered powerless by them,
was delayed on the road for some time under the pretext of a road-festival.

children.text: tāvac chrīKoṭayā devyā tadā pālayituṃ prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, by Queen <s>Śrī Koṭā</s>, in order to protect the subjects,
a <s>Bhauṭṭa</s> named <s>Kheriñcana</s> was appointed to the role of king.
She, like a widow whose children have all died, was then
tormented by all her own people, the steadfast one, for a long time.
Having fulfilled his days with the worship of the <s>Tuṣāra</s> (ice) <s>liṅga</s>,

children.text: Bhoṭṭadeśān nijaṃ deśam agacchad vītabhīr nṛpaḥ || 240 ||
children.translated_text: the king, free from fear, returned from the <s>Bhoṭṭa</s> country to his own land.
Like the moon filled by the land of the eastern mountain, he, together with <s>Koṭā</s>,
dispelling the darkness of <s>Kheriñcana</s>, was reverently borne upon the head.
The one whom <s>Koṭā</s> bore, named <s>Jaṭṭa</s>, of the minister named <s>Bhikṣaṇa</s> —

children.text: vardhanāyātmajaṃ rājā sa taṃ mṛtyum ivādita || 242 ||
children.translated_text: the king gave that son for advancement, as if giving him to death.
That brave <s>Śāhmera</s>, who had protected <s>Riñcana</s>'s legacy,
became an eyesore to the lord of the earth, due to the excess of paternal love.

children.text: devyās tu samadṛṣṭitvāt putrayor ubhayor api /
children.translated_text: But because of the queen's impartiality toward both sons,

children.text: rājño dveṣyo 'pi Śāhmero na bhayena sa paspṛśe || 244 ||
children.translated_text: even though <s>Śāhmera</s> was hated by the king, he was not touched by fear.
During the alarm of <s>Acala</s>'s invasion, when <s>Śāhmera</s> was sought refuge by the people out of fear,

children.text: Śāhmeraś sa rājānaṃ na tṛṇāyāpy ajīgaṇat || 245 ||
children.translated_text: he did not regard the king even as a straw.
<s>Śāhmera</s>, by repeatedly displaying <s>Haidara</s> like a hawk,
frightened that royal bird all the more, day and night.
Protecting the bystanders, free from agitation and waterless,
that flood of <s>Alleśvara</s>'s waters carried the people across wonderfully.
<s>Śiraśśāṭaka</s> and <s>Hinda</s> — both adorned

children.text: candrārkāv iva tasyāśāṃ śūrau pautrau guṇocchritau || 248 ||
children.translated_text: his reputation like the sun and moon, those two valorous grandsons, elevated by virtues.
Swelling with pride due to the power of his gatekeepers, ready to transgress the king's orders,
<s>Śāhmera</s> became a gateway to disaster for the king's servants.
He, having given the daughter of <s>Alleśira</s> to <s>Lusta</s>, the ruler of that region,
and having conquered <s>Śrī Śaṅkarapura</s>, increased the king's apprehension.
The hero <s>Telāka</s> was under his control, holding the lordship of <s>Bhāṅgila</s> in his hands;
having taken the daughter of <s>Jyaṃśira</s> in hand, the politically skilled one became powerful.
Conqueror of <s>Bahurūpa</s>, a treasury of fortune, attaining an unshakable position,
that man-lion then shook <s>Śamālā</s> as <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> would the fortune of the demon.
Having the depth of the ocean, with a terrible grasp on the goddess of victory,

children.text: Karāle sa karālaujāẖ karam ālambayaj janān || 253 ||
children.translated_text: that one of terrible might, in <s>Karāla</s>, seized the people by the hand.
He, of smiling fame, then recalled the burning city of <s>Vijayeśapura</s>
of King <s>Kalaśadeva</s>, from here and there.
Having established <s>Cakradharācala</s> for the stability of his own dominion,
<s>Śāhmera</s> demonstrated unshakable deeds to the people.
Granting the entire wealth of <s>Lakṣmī</s> to one who was the target of <s>Kampaneśvara</s>,

children.text: citraṃ sa labdhavāñ śuddhaṃ sudāyam iva sadyaśāḥ || 256 ||
children.translated_text: wonderfully, that one of pure fame obtained a pure revenue.
<s>Śāhmera</s> then seized <s>Koṭarāja</s>, the actor on the stage of kings,
through the intoxication of seizing the jewel of a daughter.

children.text: sāmnā kecit pare daṇḍād dānād anye pare bhayāt /
children.translated_text: Some through conciliation, others through punishment, some through gifts, and others through fear —

children.text: mānyatām anayan dhanyā Lavanyās tasya śāsanam || 258 ||
children.translated_text: The prosperous ones brought respect to the command of <s>Lavanya</s>'s rule. || 258 ||

children.text: Lavanyalokas tatputrīr mālā iva babhāra tāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Lavanyaloka</s> bore his daughters like a garland,
but he did not realize they were serpent-women, of terrible poison, capable of taking life. || 259 ||
