<s>Śrī Śiraśśāṭaka</s> obtained the gatekeeping authority from the king.
That king had a son named <s>Śāhābhadenaka</s>,
endowed with the qualities of strength, wisdom, forbearance, valor, counsel, and enthusiasm.
That prince, wandering through the <s>Vākpuṣṭā</s> forest out of the delight of play,
once beheld a circle of <s>yoginīs</s> in a mountain cavern.
<s>Udayaśrī</s> and <s>Candraḍāmara</s> were his favorites —

children.text: apaśyatāṃ na kiṃ labhyaṃ mahatām anuyānataḥ || 344 ||
children.translated_text: what is not obtainable by following great ones? They too saw the sight.
The fierce clanging of the <s>yoginīs</s>' staffs, rods, and bells shook the ground,

children.text: manāṃsi na punas teṣāṃ vīrāṇāṃ sāhasaspṛśām || 345 ||
children.translated_text: but not the minds of those heroes, who were accustomed to daring.
Ps-JRT 26

children.text:
ghaṭitāśātaṭasvāṭṭahāsasaṃvāhanādibhiḥ /
yoginyo ḍamarudhvānair bhayād iva calair babhuḥ // JRt_B.396 //
children.translated_text: The <s>yoginīs</s>, attended by the sounds of assembled clapping at the cliff-edge, loud laughter, massage and the like, and the sounds of <s>ḍamaru</s> drums, became agitated as if from fear.

children.text: māntardhāsiṣur evaitāḫ praṣṭuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca kāṅkṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Lest they vanish — for they wished to question and see them —

children.text: iti te 'śvād avārohan pravīrā na tu tadbhayāt || 346 ||
children.translated_text: those brave ones dismounted from their horses, but not out of fear of them.

children.text: śanaiś śanais tato yānto maunapūrvaṃ mahāśayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Slowly, slowly then advancing, silently, those great-souled ones,
those of formidable and manifest power, approached the vicinity of the <s>yoginīs</s>.
The leader of the <s>yoginīs</s>, recognizing the prince from afar,
then sent a consecrated cup of liquor with blessings.
<s>Candra</s>, who was to share in the satisfaction, left a remainder of that nectar from the king,
and looking to <s>Udayaśrī</s>'s face, did not finish the rest.
By the force of destiny, <s>Udayaśrī</s>, instantly forgetting the horse-keeper,

children.text: Udayaśrīr aśeṣaṃ tat pītvā tṛptiṃ parām agāt || 350 ||
children.translated_text: drank the entire remainder and attained supreme satisfaction.
When those men, their eyes filled with wonder, were satisfied, the <s>yoginī</s>,
knower of omens, then addressed the prince, who stood with joined palms:
"Your kingdom shall be undivided; <s>Candra</s> shall share a portion of your splendor;
<s>Udayaśrī</s> shall be adorned with undivided glory for life.
But that horse-keeper, deprived of our grace,
will surely be separated from his life-breath within a short time."
Having thus foretold the future, accompanied by her fellow <s>yoginīs</s>,
she vanished; and soon after, the horse-keeper lost his life.
Lords arise through the merit of the people, as causes for the increase of light,
to uplift beings submerged in the darkness of thoughtlessness.

children.text: śvaśurād bhartṛbhāgaṃ yad avīrā puṃścalī vadhūḥ /
children.translated_text: The custom by which a childless unfaithful widow would take the husband's share from the father-in-law —

children.text: haranty āsīt sa taṃ rājā durācāraṃ nyavārayat || 356 ||
children.translated_text: that king put a stop to that evil practice.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 28
The <s>Rājasthānīyas</s> who had come from <s>Kāṣṭhavāṭa</s>, intent on battle formations,

children.text: yuktyānīya mahīpālo baddhvā rājyaṃ sukhaṃ vyadhāt // JRt_B.408 //
children.translated_text: the king, having lured them by stratagem, captured them and ruled the kingdom in comfort.
He imprisoned the son-in-law of <s>Koṭarāja</s>,

children.text: bhītyā pratyaham evātha jīvanmṛtyum avārayat // JRt_B.409 //
children.translated_text: and then, out of fear, daily averted his living death.

children.text:
bubhuje Kṣemarājaśrīsvasthāṃ śastranakhaiś śataiḥ /
vidārya Khaṭikābhūmiṃ rājā saukaryabhājanam // JRt_B.410 //
children.translated_text: The king, having torn apart the land of <s>Khaṭikā</s> with a hundred weapon-like nails, enjoyed the prosperity of <s>Kṣemarāja</s> and its comforts.
The highly intelligent one, having made <s>Jayāpīḍapura</s> his capital,
constructed an embankment called <s>Buddhagiri</s> at <s>Śrī Riñcanapura</s>.
Then, in the twenty-ninth year, a terrible famine born of evil deeds

children.text: durbhikṣaṃ kṣobhayām āsa lokaṃ śokākulaṃ mahat || 358 ||
children.translated_text: greatly disturbed the people, who were overcome with grief.

children.text: māsān aṣṭau dvādaśābdāṃs trayodaśa dināni ca /
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed the earth for twelve years, eight months, and thirteen days,

children.text: kṣmāṃ bhuktvā triṃśavarṣe 'tha caitre rājā vyapadyata || 359 ||
children.translated_text: the king passed away in the thirtieth year, in the month of <s>Caitra</s>.
19) <s>Šihāb ad-Dīn</s> (LS 4430-4449)
The sluggishness in speech caused by the narration of the story of a foolish king
is destroyed by the account of <s>Śāhābadena</s> of fierce valor.
Under King <s>Śāhābadena</s>, the earth then abandoned the memory
of the joys and sorrows, prosperity and adversity of <s>Lalitāditya</s>.
Ps-JRT 29

children.text:
śrīmān Śāhābadeno 'tha prājyaṃ sāmrājyam agrahīt /
yena rājanvatī bhūr dyām ahasat tadyaśomiṣāt // JRt_B.416 //
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Śāhābadena</s> then seized the abundant empire, by whose fame-arrows the earth, having a king, laughed at heaven.

children.text: grīṣmārkaṃ dyaur ivānyartūn rājño 'tītya bahūn mahī /
children.translated_text: The earth, surpassing many former kings as the sky surpasses the summer sun and other seasons,

children.text: dhruvam āpaj jayāpīḍam etaṃ na tu sa kilviṣī || 362 ||
children.translated_text: firmly attained this <s>Jayāpīḍa</s> — but he was not a sinner.

children.text: pūrve pare ca bhūpālā nāyakeneva bhūṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Former and later kings were adorned as if by a hero —
by that lord of the earth, resplendent with the beauty of a string of pearls.
Ps-JRT 30

children.text:
sindhau vāḍavataptāmbuny api bimbitam ambaram /
yatpratāpāgnitāpārtaṃ majjatīva divāniśam // JRt_B.419 //
children.translated_text: Even in the ocean where the waters are heated by the submarine fire, the reflected sky, tormented by the fire of his valor, seems to sink day and night.
The fire of his valor was not satisfied by the goddesses of victory entering at every step,
just as the ocean is not satisfied by rivers.

children.text: jayaṃ vinā gaṇayataẖ kṣaṇamātraṃ vṛthā gatam /
children.translated_text: He who counted even a moment without victory as time wasted —
military campaigns were as dear to him as a young woman to an old man.

children.text: na mṛgākṣī na vā śīdhupānalīlā na candrikā /
children.translated_text: Neither a doe-eyed woman, nor the sport of wine-drinking, nor moonlight —
only military campaigns captivated the mind of that lord of the earth.

children.text: na tāpo na himaṃ tasya na sandhyā na niśā tathā /
children.translated_text: Neither heat, nor cold, nor twilight, nor night,

children.text: na kṣun na vā pipāsā ca rājño yātrām avighnayat || 367 ||
children.translated_text: nor hunger, nor thirst impeded the king's campaigns.

children.text: na sarid dustaratarā durāroho na parvataḥ /
children.translated_text: No river too difficult to cross, no mountain too hard to ascend,

children.text: durlaṅghyo na maruś cābhūd yātrāyāṃ māninaḫ prabhoḥ || 368 ||
children.translated_text: no desert too hard to traverse existed for that proud lord during his campaigns.
To conquer the northern direction — unconquered by former kings and teeming with <s>Pārasīka</s> (Persian) clans —

children.text: uttarāśāṃ vijetuṃ sa prasthānaṃ prathamaṃ vyadhāt || 369 ||
children.translated_text: he made his first expedition.
The lord, conqueror of the world, like <s>Kāma</s> selecting wine and women,
chose <s>Candra</s>, <s>Lolaka</s>, and <s>Śūra</s> as his companions.
He filled the minds of his army with courage, the minds of his enemies with darkness,
and the horizons with dust — that one of terrible death-dealing.
He first entered <s>Udabhāṇḍapura</s>, which was under the protection of <s>Govindakhāna</s>,
initially with arrows and then with soldiers.
When the king's army reached the mountain peak, his adversaries,
stricken with fear, descended from the lofty summit.
The lord of <s>Sindhu</s>, unable to give a worthy tribute to him,
deceitfully offered a jewel of a maiden and took from the king.

children.text: rājñas tu gauravaṃ bāhau Gāndhārāṇāṃ bhuvoḍhayā /
children.translated_text: The dignity of the king's arm was enhanced by bearing the land of the <s>Gāndhāras</s>;
but wonderful was their loss of weight through the burden of fear that followed.

children.text: bhaṅgas tuṅgasya śṛṅgasya khaḍgānāṃ naiva bhūbhujā /
children.translated_text: The king, endowed with valor, caused the breaking not only of lofty peaks
but also of the <s>Śiṅgas</s>' swords in this land.
Hearing the lion-roar-like army of the lion among kings,
the city of <s>Gajinī</s> (Ghazni) lost its arrogance, stumbled, and trembled.
Ps-JRT 31

children.text:
snātaṃ raktair dviṣāṃ bhuktaṃ prāṇavātair mahītale /
vratasthābhir ivāsvāpi tasyāho dhīrahetibhiḥ // JRt_B.434 //
children.translated_text: Bathed in the blood of enemies, feasting on life-breaths on the battlefield, his steady weapons behaved like women observing a vow — unsleeping.
In <s>Aṣṭanagara</s>, by <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Brahmins) and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, stricken with fear, there were lamentations
over the two subsiding fires — of youth and of valor — as if by their smoke.

children.text: yaśasā saha sampattiṃ tasmiṃl luṇṭhayati prabhau /
children.translated_text: When that lord plundered wealth along with fame there,
the name of the land called <s>Puruṣavīra</s> acquired a conventional meaning.
The women of <s>Nagarāgrahara</s>, having offered tear-drops as water-oblations,

children.text: jīvatas svasya patyuś ca piṇḍau stananibhād daduḥ || 380 ||
children.translated_text: They gave funeral offerings resembling their breasts, even while their husbands were still alive.
When the horse-keepers departed, under the pretext of visiting the cow-pastures,
the lord composed a eulogy disparaging <s>Udakpati</s>.

children.text: tato vyāvṛtya gacchan sa dakṣiṇāśāṃ svavājinām /
children.translated_text: Then, turning and proceeding toward the southern direction, he relieved the fatigue of his horses,
appropriate to the weariness of the road, with the waters of the <s>Śatadrū</s> (Sutlej).
Having plundered <s>Ḍhillī</s> (Delhi) and at that time approaching <s>Udakpati</s>,
the king greatly alarmed him by blocking his route.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s>

children.text:
Yoginīpurapaurān yān dhāṭyānaiṣīd Udakpatiḥ /
mārgadānopakāreṇa sa tān adita bhūbhuje || 384 ||
children.translated_text: The people of <s>Yoginīpura</s> whom <s>Udakpati</s> had carried off in a raid— the king gave them to the ruler through the service of granting safe passage.
Having honored them with gifts of horses and cloth, the king

children.text: svadeśaṃ prāhiṇot kīrtirāśīn mūrtān bahūn iva || 385 ||
children.translated_text: sent them to their own land, like many embodied blessings of fame.
By the king of <s>Suśarmapura</s>, who therefore feared for his own peace,
abandoning the pride of his fortress, the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) alone was made his refuge.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 32

children.text:
tatpratāpānalaḫ pītvā Kedārāśrayiṇāṃ rasam /
jātānāṃ śivaliṅgānāṃ vata bhaṅgam adarśayat // JRt_B.444 //
children.translated_text: The fire of his prowess, having consumed the essence of those sheltering in <s>Kedāra</s>, alas, demonstrated the destruction of the <s>Śivaliṅgas</s> that had arisen there.

children.text: svayaṃ natyā na tūnnatyā Bhauṭṭānām asya bhūpateḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhauṭṭas</s>' longing to ascend the mountains for their horses
was deterred by this king, through his own submission, not through arrogance.
The flood of the <s>Sindhu</s>, standing on the bank, was made shallow by the deities—

children.text: Sindhvogho nṛpater evaṃ pūrvebhyaś śrutam adbhutam || 388 ||
children.translated_text: thus it was heard from the ancients, a wonder for the king.
Thus, due to his constant pursuit of victory, his own land became like a foreign land,

children.text: paradeśas tu tasyāsīt svadeśa iva bhūpateḥ || 389 ||
children.translated_text: while foreign lands became like his own for that king.
Having thus achieved the mark of glory on the face of the directions through his valor,

children.text: vyadhāt praviśya Kaśmīrān sa paurān ayanotsavam || 390 ||
children.translated_text: entering <s>Kaśmīra</s>, he arranged for the people a festival of the solstice.
Of those who describe his superhuman valor on occasion,
people of the future will recognize our flattery.
Once, that king, returning from a military expedition to a distant land,
heard of a certain doe-eyed woman resembling an <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymph).
Having deceived his own attendants by some stratagem,

children.text: athaikākī sa taṃ deśam aviśad bhogalālasaḥ || 393 ||
children.translated_text: the king then entered that place alone, eager for pleasure.

children.text: narmaṇā mohayitvā tāṃ dvitīya iva manmathaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having enchanted her with sweet words, like a second <s>Manmatha</s> (God of Love),
he fulfilled his desires by drinking the nectar of her lips.

children.text: apaśyantas tam āśaṅkya hataṃ kenāpi vairiṇā /
children.translated_text: Not seeing him and suspecting he had been slain by some enemy,
his fierce warriors then fell into a frenzy of rage and confusion.
By those searching for him, through his horse tied outside the dwelling,

children.text: samabhāvyata tai rājño vairibhir nirjayaẖ kṛtaḥ || 396 ||
children.translated_text: it was concluded that the king had been defeated by enemies.
The fierce warriors, out of loyalty to the valor and lordship [of the king],
besieged the house without even having donned their armor, to wage battle.

body.translated_text: And those who were unafraid, from that place previously filled with his lion-roars—

children.translated_text: Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s>
when the warriors made their assault, the enemies had fled into the forest.

children.text: athāśvāsya priyāṃ tāṃ tu śatrūn matvā samāgatān /
children.translated_text: Then, having reassured that beloved woman, considering that enemies had come,
the king sallied forth to fight, to make his valor bear fruit.
Seeing <s>Śāhābadena</s>, their retainers

body.text: cittaiḫ prītyā mukhair bhītyā nītyā mūrdhabhir ānatam // 400cd //
body.translated_text: bowed with hearts in joy, faces in fear, and heads in submission.

children.translated_text: Thus he performed many battle-sacrifices, with pillars of victory as sacrificial posts,
with slain enemies as sacrificial animals, with the flames of his own valor as fire.
In his own land, the two ministers <s>Koṭabhaṭṭa</s> and <s>Udayaśrī</s> [held sway],
while in battles the burden fell on <s>Candraḍāmara</s> and <s>Lola</s>.
The moon of the ocean of the <s>Devaśarman</s> lineage, who had been repeatedly given wealth by the king,

children.text: vairāgyād vibhavaṃ tyaktvā Koṭaśarmā vanaṃ yayau || 403 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Koṭaśarman</s> renounced his riches out of detachment and went to the forest.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 33
The illustrious <s>Koṭabhaṭṭa</s>, having diligently nourished the caravans of supplicants with the rain of fortune,

children.text: vyalālayad vanavyomni sa svaṃ niyamamārutaiḥ // JRt_B.462 //
children.translated_text: made himself soar in the sky of the forest through the winds of his austerities.

children.text:
Koṭaśarmā tathā dharmadrumaṃ dānāmbhasāsicat /
nanāśāśāmayo bhūyo yathā tatphalabhoginaḥ // JRt_B.463 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>Koṭaśarman</s> watered the tree of <s>dharma</s> with the waters of generosity, so that those who enjoyed its fruits would never again suffer the disease of distress.
To demonstrate to the king the superiority of his own power, surely,

children.text: kadācit tatprajā daivī vyāpad gāḍham apīḍayat || 404 ||
children.translated_text: a divine calamity once severely afflicted his subjects.
A fierce sun of the city's river, a hero against the tree-enemies,
in the thirty-sixth year, a cruel flood inundated the people.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 34

children.text:
tadantaḫpratibimbasthe svasmin sadmāntarabhramāt /
tadvīkṣārtham ivānīke toye tumbīr vyadhur gṛhāḥ // JRt_B.466 //
children.translated_text: Since their own reflections stood within it, the houses, as if confused about their own selves, placed gourds in the water in order to see those reflections—as if in a battle-formation.
Shedding tears from the bruising of the city, under the guise of waterfalls,
the mountains took the position of banks for that great flood.

children.text: na sa vṛkṣo na sā sīmā na sa setur na tad guham /
children.translated_text: There was no tree, no boundary, no bridge, no cave,

children.text: taṭastham api yan naiva jalapūro vyanāśayat || 407 ||
children.translated_text: not even standing on the bank, that the flood did not destroy.
He who never looked to mountain-fortresses out of fear of enemies,
that king roamed more among them out of fear of the water-flood.
When the flood, as if drunk by his radiance, subsided within a few days,
he, still fearing another deluge, desired to build a city on the mountain.

children.text: nāmnā Lakṣmyā mahiṣyāś ca prasiddhāṃ nagarīṃ vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: The king, not sparing the expense of construction,
built a famous city named after <s>Lakṣmī</s>, his queen, befitting his own generosity.
At the foot of <s>Śārikāśaila</s> (the mountain of <s>Śārikā</s>), frequented by holy beings,

children.text: yām adrākṣīttarāṃ lokas sumeror Alakām iva // 410gh //
children.translated_text: which the world beheld as superior, like <s>Alakā</s> of <s>Sumeru</s>.
At the confluence of the <s>Vitastā</s> and <s>Sindhu</s>, he built a city bearing his own name,
which, under the pretext of its reflection, shyly submerges into the water of heaven.
Like accumulated, immovable fame towering with the height of palaces,
<s>Lolaḍāmara</s>, of unwavering fortune, built a city bearing his own name.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 35

children.text:
sudhādhautair maṭhair lakṣmīṃ phalayadbhiẖ kṛtaiḫ purī /
kuliśacchinnakailāsaśṛṅgabhaṅgim ajījanat // JRt_B.475 //
children.translated_text: The city, with monasteries washed in lime plaster bearing the fruit of prosperity, assumed the appearance of severed peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s> cut by thunderbolts.
The restlessness born in me since birth, nurtured to match her essence,
destroys with its shadow the happiness born from the touch of the sun.
She who was <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s niece, a maiden raised in her presence,
called <s>Lāsā</s>, she invaded the mirror of the king's heart.

children.text: yaś cānurodhatantus taṃ ciraṃ Lakṣmyā nibaddhavān /
children.translated_text: And the thread of devotion that had long bound him to <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
was severed by the force of passion born from <s>Lāsā</s>'s beauty.
By him who was an embodiment of <s>Balijin</s>, dwelling on the breast of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune),
<s>Lāsā</s>, the sharer of good fortune, was made a neighbor.

children.text: chāyā tadracitodayāpi divasaśrībhogam ātanvataḥ sūryāt sammukhatāṃ jahāti vahati śreyoharīṃ kālatām /
children.translated_text: A shadow, though fashioned by his own rise, abandons face-to-face intimacy with the sun who extends the enjoyment of daylight's glory, and assumes a time that steals what is good—

children.text: strīṇām asti caturguṇā matir iti sthāne na hanta śrutir yad vā durvidhipaṅkam ākalayituṃ śakto na kaścid drutam || 417 ||
children.translated_text: rightly says the scripture that women's minds are fourfold; or rather, no one can quickly fathom the mud of evil fate.
Even <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the virtuous daughter of the commoner called <s>Avatāra</s>, of the <s>Bhalla</s> clan—
when the king became infatuated with <s>Lāsā</s>, she conceived anger.

children.text: roṣāt Sindhupater deśaṃ sambandhitvād gatāṃ nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The queen who had gone to the land of the <s>Sindhupati</s> (Lord of Sindh) out of anger, due to kinship—
the king brought her back out of excess of shame, not out of affection and respect.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 36

children.text: alābvo nyabruḍann antar aplavanta jale śilāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gourds sank within, stones floated in water—

children.text: Lakṣmīpakṣaẖ kṣayaṃ vṛddhiṃ Lāsāpakṣas tu labdhavān // JRt_B.483 //
children.translated_text: the side of <s>Lakṣmī</s> suffered decline, while the side of <s>Lāsā</s> gained ascendancy.

children.text:
yāvad yāvad agād dūraṃ Lakṣmī rātrir iva krudhā /
tāvat tāvat sa tāṃ Lāsāṃ divaṃ bhāsvān ivābhajat // JRt_B.484 //
children.translated_text: The more <s>Lakṣmī</s> departed in anger like the night, the more the king embraced <s>Lāsā</s> like the radiant sun embraces the day.
Removing the distress of heat with the waters of the lotus-pond, the she-elephant of the desert—
in the churning of the lotus-moss water at his feet, she becomes industrious.
Through <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s maternal aunt, all maternal rites were performed;
the king's beloved, <s>Lāsā</s>, then became like the full-moon night, intent on the waning of the fortnight.

children.text: satkarmapākasamayo 'sya na ced vikāsaśobhāṃ na kiṃ pariharet kumudākarasya /
children.translated_text: If it were not the time for the ripening of good deeds, would the lotus pond not abandon the beauty of its blooming?

children.text: viśvaprabodhaharaṇapravaṇakṣaṇena kustrī niśā ca sahasaiva niśākareṇa || 422 ||
children.translated_text: By the moon, at the moment intent on robbing the world's wakefulness—an unchaste woman and night [come] suddenly together.
With lips moistened by sighs indicative of anxiety, once
the serpent-woman called <s>Lāsā</s> thus spoke to the king like a cobra:

children.text: "na ced vikāsayed bhāsvān padminīṃ svarucā sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: "If the radiant sun does not clearly cause the lotus to bloom with its own splendor,

children.text: tasyāś chedāya śaivālavallyā iva yateta kaḥ || 424 ||
children.translated_text: who would strive to cut it down like a moss-creeper?
Unable to bear your glance falling on me, heavy with the weight of love,

children.text: māṃ nihantum upāyena kurute mahiṣī tava || 425 ||
children.translated_text: your queen contrives to kill me by some stratagem.
In sorcery, she has set in motion that ill-conducted one who feigns politeness—

children.text: sā cārākṣī mayi dveṣād Udayaśriyam airayat" || 426 ||
children.translated_text: that spy-eyed one, out of hatred toward me, has instigated <s>Udayaśrī</s>."
"In that one who is devoted to the commands of the gods, the fabrication of sorcery
is inconceivable"—thus the discerning king replied to her.
As she persistently insisted on the same statement,
he then spoke to the queen <s>Udayaśrī</s> in order to reassure her [<s>Lāsā</s>]:
"Alas, by excessive spending the treasury has become empty;

children.text: prārthayante janā rājñas sarvaṃ kalpatarūn iva || 429 ||
children.translated_text: people petition the king for everything, as if from wish-fulfilling trees.
Therefore, this plan occurs to me for generating wealth:
the image of the illustrious <s>Jayeśvarī</s> which is large and made of brass—
having broken it apart, with the coins thus struck bearing my name,
both the maintenance of expenditure and the permanence of fame shall arise."

children.text: "sādhv etat kiṃ tu tanmūrtir laghvī kiṃ prabhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: "This is good, but that image is small—what can it accomplish?
Let the coins be made by <s>Bṛhadbuddha</s>"—the petty minister suggested.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 37

children.text:
puṃnāgavrajam unmumūlayiṣati prāyaẖ karākarṣaṇair uddāmaṃ vijihīrṣati pratipadaṃ kakṣyāchidāṃ kāṅkṣati /
kāṃ naicchan nṛpagandhasindhurapatis tīvrāṃ na vaprakriyāṃ tīkṣṇāgrapratibhāṅkuśo 'sya nikaṭe mantrī niyantā punaḥ // JRt_B.499 //
children.translated_text: The king, like a rutting elephant-lord, was about to uproot groves of <s>puṃnāga</s> trees by pulling with his hands, to seize boldly at every step, and to desire the breaking of barriers— what fierce rampart-work did that royal elephant not wish for? But his minister, with the goad of sharp-pointed wit, was his restrainer.
Having prepared the equipment for minting the next day, upon arrival,

children.text: rājñīṃ pratyāyya bhūpālo raho mantriṇam abravīt || 433 ||
children.translated_text: the king, having reassured the queen, spoke to the minister in private:
"The divine images that were created by former kings for the attainment of fame and merit—
you are ready to break them easily?

children.text: amarapratimā vidhāya kecit paripūjyātha pare prasiddhim āptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some attained renown by fashioning divine images, others by worshipping and then making them famous,

children.text: paripālya yathocitaṃ tathānye vidalayyāham aho mahad durantam || 435 ||
children.translated_text: still others by properly protecting them; but I, by destroying them—alas, what a great and terrible [act]!

children.text: nirmāṇāj jaladhes kṛteś ca saritāṃ kaumāraśokāvadhiḫ prakhyātas Sagaro Bhagīrathanṛpo Gaṅgāvatārāc ca saḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sagara</s> was renowned for the creation of the ocean and the fashioning of rivers up to the boundary of <s>Kumāraśoka</s>; that <s>Bhagīratha</s> king for the descent of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: Duṣyantas sa ca viśvaviśvavijayāj Jiṣṇor bhayāny āvahan Rāmo hanta Daśānanena vihitāt Sītāpahārāt punaḥ || 436 ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Duṣyanta</s> who by the universal conquest of <s>Jiṣṇu</s> (Viṣṇu) brought terrors; <s>Rāma</s>, alas, again from the abduction of <s>Sītā</s> committed by <s>Daśānana</s> (Rāvaṇa).
The king named <s>Śāhābadīna</s> toppled divine images—

children.text: mā durvārtteyam atyugrā cakampad bhāvino janān" || 437 ||
children.translated_text: let this most terrible ill report not shake people of the future."
When <s>Udayaśrī</s>, with bowed head, herself said "O Queen,"
she looked at the ground as if desiring a swift downward course.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 38

children.text:
sarvaṃsahā tadā kṣmābhūd anvarthā prāgvad eva yat /
Lāsānuraktam api taṃ sā rājānam asevata // JRt_B.505 //
children.translated_text: The earth then was truly all-bearing, as before, for though he was enamored of <s>Lāsā</s>, she [<s>Lakṣmī</s>] continued to serve that king.
The sun, having attained the delight of embracing the sky's essence,
desires the decline of the planets headed by his own son <s>Śani</s> (Saturn).
The passionate one, aroused by that queen who spoke of faults,

children.text: vyavāsayat svadeśāt sa rājaputrān parān iva || 440 ||
children.translated_text: banished the princes from his own land as if they were strangers.
By those who provided assistance in tasks beyond human capacity,
The valor of the lord of <s>Yoginīpura</s> was made manifest. (JRt 441)

children.text: audāryād dattavṛttīn sa Hindukān eva bodhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Out of generosity, having given livelihood [to them], he was informed that the <s>Hindus</s> themselves —
The <s>Mlecchas</s> led by <s>Sekandara</s> [Alexander/Sikandar], who committed treason against the king, he slew. (JRt 442)
The valiant <s>Madanalāvika</s>, his suspicion aroused by informers,
Though ready for revolt, was restrained by the king's army. (JRt 443)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 39
'Raised by the generous king to be his equal,
<s>Madanalāvika</s> then conducted himself as superior to the king. (JRt B.511)
Equal in wealth and equal in power — he is to be suspected' — thus the king

children.text: īrṣyālubhiẖ kusacivais tasmai param akopyata // JRt_B.512 //
children.translated_text: Was exceedingly angered against him by jealous and wicked ministers. (JRt B.512)

children.text: śucim apy aśuciṃ matvā taṃ vītiṃ bhūmipāladhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Though he was pure, regarding him as impure, the king's mind,
Veiled by the intent to destroy the wicked, did not find peace. (JRt B.513)

children.text:
upaplāvayituṃ vāñchaṃs taṃ muhuẖ krodhavegataḥ /
rājaratnākaro 'rodhi tadīyaguṇavelayā // JRt_B.514 //
children.translated_text: Wishing to destroy him, repeatedly driven by the force of anger, the king, a mine of royal gems, was checked by the tide of that man's virtues. (JRt B.514)
The king, eagerly setting out on a campaign impelled by passion [for the hunt],
Brought the curiosity of boats and bridges from the <s>Sindhu</s> river, as if from a moat. (JRt 444)
The valiant king, roaming in the city of <s>Khaḍga</s> out of delight in the hunt,
Charged at a lion — that king whose daring was united with the lion's [own ferocity]. (JRt 445)
The king, surpassing thought in speed on his horse swift as a king [of beasts],
Was followed only by <s>Madana</s>, out of supreme devotion. (JRt 446)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 40

children.text:
ārūḍhaḫ pauruṣaṃ rājā so 'varūḍhas turaṅgamāt /
Yameneva vyadhād yuddhaṃ hariṇā krauryadhāriṇā // JRt_B.518 //
children.translated_text: The king, mounting his manly valor, dismounted from his horse and fought with the tawny-maned [lion], fierce as <s>Yama</s>. (JRt B.518)
Fighting alone for a long time, the lion with bristling mane
Brought down that lion among kings with extreme daring. (JRt 447)
Leaping swiftly from his horse, the valiant <s>Madanalāvika</s>
Instantly killed the lion that had felled the king, with his sword. (JRt 448)
Pleased by the service of saving his life, [yet] from slanderous people
Suspecting a plot to kill him, the lord of men — (JRt 449)
That compassionate one, giving wealth under the pretext of a wedding,
Sent <s>Madana</s> away directly to the court of the lord of <s>Ḍhillī</s> [Delhi]. (JRt 450)
A golden city that, with its brilliance, made the sky bloom with <s>campaka</s> flowers,
The one named <s>Śarkarasūha</s> once beheld in a dream. (JRt 451)

children.text: veśma veśma viśaṃs tatra śūnyaṃ paśyann ayaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Entering house after house there and seeing them all empty,
He then beheld in the royal capital a certain woman whose beauty was radiant. (JRt 452)
He asked: 'You alone — alas! — in this great city,

children.text: vyomnīva śaśilekhā kiṃ citraṃ tiṣṭhasi nirbhayā || 453 ||
children.translated_text: Like a sliver of moonlight in the sky, why do you stand fearlessly? (JRt 453)

children.text: kasyeyaṃ nagarī kasmāc chūnyā sarvatra vartate /
children.translated_text: Whose is this city? Why is it empty everywhere?

children.text: atredaṃ patitaṃ kasya vartate ca kalevaram" || 454 ||
children.translated_text: And whose corpse lies fallen here?' (JRt 454)
She told him: 'This is the great city of the king of the <s>Gandharvas</s>,
[Now] beautiful [yet desolate], like a woman bereft of her husband, like a night without the moon. (JRt 455)

children.text: sa cāmātyais samaṃ sarvaiḫ pātuṃ Kaśmīramedinīm /
children.translated_text: He, together with all his ministers, descended to protect the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s>,
Leaving his own body here. (JRt 456)
He who is renowned in the three worlds as <s>Śāhābadena</s> [Šāh Bādān] —
I remain here alone to guard his body. (JRt 457)
He, having accomplished all his tasks within three months,

children.text: svām imāṃ nagarīm eva dhruvaṃ rakṣitum eṣyati" || 458 ||
children.translated_text: Will surely come to protect this city of his.' (JRt 458)
Awakening, [the dreamer], immersed in a state between wonder, grief, and anxiety,
Narrated the unbroken dream-story to the king. (JRt 459)

children.text: "asatye kiṃ bhayaṃ svapne satye tv aiśvaryam eva me" /
children.translated_text: 'If the dream is false, what fear? But if true, sovereignty itself is mine' —

children.text: itthaṃ tad vimṛśan rājā na tathā paspṛśe śucā || 460 ||
children.translated_text: Deliberating thus, the king was not greatly touched by sorrow. (JRt 460)
'Come to my side' — thus the lord of the earth thereupon
Immediately dispatched letters to his sons who were far away. (JRt 461)

children.text: tato mumūrṣur bhūpālo Hindukānāṃ nije pade /
children.translated_text: Then the king, about to die, [bestowed] upon the <s>Hindus</s> their own rank,
And the wise one, his son not having arrived, consecrated [a successor] himself. (JRt 462)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 43

children.text: taṃ bhaktaṃ nEśvaro 'naiṣīt sadehaṃ yat sadharmatām /
children.translated_text: That the Lord did not take that devotee to the state of the virtuous with his body —

children.text: tatra hetur dhruvaṃ tasmin saubhāgyān Madanabhramaḥ // JRt_B.534 //
children.translated_text: The reason was surely the illusion of <s>Madana</s> [Kāma, god of love] due to his good fortune. (JRt B.534)

children.text: śauryaudāryavidhau vidhautavividhaśloke nṛlokeśvare tasminn astam upāgate guṇigaṇatrāṇoccarannaipuṇe /
children.translated_text: When that lord of men, accomplished in the ways of valor and generosity, whose manifold glory was purified, who was skilled in uttering the protection of the virtuous, set [like the sun],

children.text: Śakreṇonnamitaṃ śiraḫ paribhavatrāsāpasārād dhruvaṃ bhūbhārodvahanāt punar vinamitaṃ śeṣeṇa śokaspṛśā // JRt_B.535 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> [Indra] surely raised his head from the retreat caused by the fear of humiliation, and <s>Śeṣa</s> [the cosmic serpent] bent his again from bearing the earth's burden, touched by grief. (JRt B.535)

children.text:
pratyakṣaṃ jvalataḫ pratāpaśikhinas svīkṛtya yāṃ bhuktavān nānyān ādriyatādhikaṃ spṛhayatas tadrāgabandhāc ca yā /
tāṃ bhūmiṃ pravihāya hāyam agamad dyāṃ Śakrabhuktāṃ ciraṃ puṃsāṃ strīṣu kadāpi na prabhavati premagrahapratyayaḥ // JRt_B.536 //
children.translated_text: The earth which he visibly enjoyed, having taken her from the blazing fire of his valor, and which, out of the bond of his passion, he did not regard others [as worthy of] — abandoning that earth, alas, he went to heaven long enjoyed by <s>Śakra</s>; in men, the conviction of love toward women never prevails [in the end]. (JRt B.536)
On the fourteenth of the bright fortnight of <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s>, in the [Laukika] year,
The king, embracing the celestial women, made the fullness of their breasts bear fruit. (JRt 463)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 44

children.text:
matveva bhūjayād bhūyaḫ punaruktāpavādatām /
Śāhābhadīne nirjetuṃ dyām iva prasthite sati // JRt_B.538 //
children.translated_text: As if [to avoid] the censure of repetition in enjoying the earth again, when <s>Śāhābadīna</s> set out, as if to conquer heaven — (JRt B.538)
Then the king <s>Kudbhadena</s> [Quṭb-ad-Dīn] placed upon the crowns of kings his command,

children.text: citte sukhaṃ mukhe harṣaṃ stutiṃ vāci nyadhāt tataḥ || 464 ||
children.translated_text: Happiness in their hearts, joy on their faces, and praise on their lips. (JRt 464)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 46
The lotus of his glory went along a proud path,
As if distressed by the absence of former kings who were addicted to conquest. (JRt B.540)

children.text: tadviyogāsahā deśadevī jayam adhāt svayam / JRt_B.541ab /
children.translated_text: The goddess of the land, unable to bear separation from him, herself bestowed victory. (JRt B.541ab)

children.text: nātitīvro na vā mandas sarvasyaiva mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither too fierce nor too mild, the king [won] the hearts

children.text: cittam ādita lokasya vaiṣuvo bhānumān iva || 465 ||
children.translated_text: Of all people from the start, like the equinoctial sun. (JRt 465)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 47
The twang of his bow in battle, imitated [i.e., echoed] by day,
[Was drowned out] as if from jealousy by the wailing of the lamenting wives of enemies. (JRt B.542)
His fame was like sandalwood paste on the face of the directions, like moonlight on the firmament,
Souring the faces of the enemies of that lord of the earth. (JRt B.543)

children.text:
kṣema lakṣmīṃ prajāẖ kṣoṇīpāle tanvati tanvati /
bhūmāv eva sthitā nākabhogasaukhyam abhuñjata // JRt_B.544 //
children.translated_text: As the guardian of the earth bestowed security and prosperity upon the subjects, they, while remaining on earth itself, enjoyed the bliss of heavenly pleasures. (JRt B.544)
Those whom the previous king had stationed for the supervision of <s>Lohara</s>,

children.text: Loharādhipater bhītyā te palāyya gatās tataḥ || 466 ||
children.translated_text: They, out of fear of the lord of <s>Lohara</s>, fled from there. (JRt 466)

children.text: śāmyanty oṣadhayas sarvāś śaśiny astaṃ gate sati /
children.translated_text: All herbs lose their power when the moon has set;

children.text: dṛṣṭo hi sūryakāntānāṃ ravau yāti dyutikṣayaḥ || 467 ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, the <s>sūryakānta</s> [sun-gems] are seen to lose their brilliance when the sun departs. (JRt 467)
To reattach <s>Lohara</s> [to the kingdom], King <s>Kudbhadena</s>
Appointed the valorous rebel chief <s>Lolaka</s> at the front. (JRt 468)

children.text: aveṣṭayat tato gatvā Loharādriṃ sa sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Going there, he then besieged the mountain of <s>Lohara</s> from all sides;
For the lives of great souls devoted to their master are [counted as light as] straw. (JRt 469)
Unable [to hold] his own fortress, the lord of the fortress thereupon
Sent <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> as envoys to the rebel chief. (JRt 470)

children.text: dvijaliṅgān sa tān matvā sāraṃ draṣṭum upāgatān /
children.translated_text: Considering those [envoys] in <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> guise to have come to spy out his strength,
He, with unperturbed mind, arrested the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> instead of waging fierce war. (JRt 471)
Hearing that this man, though one for whom <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are divine, had harmed them,
The lord of <s>Lohara</s> gave up hope of both [keeping] the fortress and [saving] his life. (JRt 472)

children.text: paśyanto maraṇaṃ svasya yuddhe vātha palāyane /
children.translated_text: Seeing death as certain for themselves whether in battle or in flight,

children.text: kṣatriyāṇāṃ nijaṃ dharmam agrahīṣus tato raṇam || 473 ||
children.translated_text: They then embraced the inherent <s>dharma</s> of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> — the battlefield. (JRt 473)
With torrents of boulders and solid stones, terrible like storm-clouds,

children.text: Loharādrer avārohann ārohaṃs tu yaśāṃsi te || 474 ||
children.translated_text: They descended from the mountain of <s>Lohara</s>, while ascending in glory. (JRt 474)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 49

children.text:
svaṃ khaṇḍīkṛtya śailena vibhaktaṃ svāmibhaktitaḥ /
pratyekaṃ śatravas teṣu śilāvarṣiṣv amaṃsata // JRt_B.554 //
children.translated_text: Breaking themselves against the mountain, divided [into pieces] out of devotion to their master, the enemies regarded each one of those stone-showerers [as formidable]. (JRt B.554)
The <s>ḍāmara</s>-chief <s>Lola</s>, [buried] by the scattered stones,

children.text: antarhitas samaṃ kīrtyā bhāvi ko nāma laṅghati || 475 ||
children.translated_text: Disappeared along with his fame — who can transgress what is destined? (JRt 475)
<s>Ḍāmara</s> <s>Lolaka</s>, covered by a heap of stones [hurled by] enemies,
Did not abandon even in calamity the <s>Yavana</s> funeral rites. (JRt 476)
King <s>Śāhābadena</s>, even while banishing his own sons,
Summoned [them] himself through letters adorned with his own script. (JRt 477)

children.text: guṇaiś ca vayasā teṣāṃ jyeṣṭho Māhendramaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: The eldest of them in virtues and age, [who had gone to] the region of <s>Māhendra</s>,

children.text: Hassano rājaputras sa prāpa tāvad anaṅkuśam || 478 ||
children.translated_text: The prince <s>Hassana</s>, reached [that land] by then, unchecked. (JRt 478)
With tears streaming from the pearl-shells of his eyes, with liberated waves of tears,

children.text: śrutvā tatra pitur mṛtyuṃ nivāpāñjalim ārpayat || 479 ||
children.translated_text: Upon hearing there of his father's death, he offered the water-oblation with cupped hands. (JRt 479)
Turning him away from his desire to journey, [appealing to] his pure-hearted [nature],
A letter from his paternal uncle, the king of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, restrained him. (JRt 480)
'Out of greed for the pleasures of <s>Śakra</s> [Indra's heaven] and the like, abandoning us, his servants,
The lord of the earth <s>Śāhābadīna</s> made heaven his equal [abode]. (JRt 481)
As if in eagerness to go, driven by the passion for the enjoyment of his own wife [i.e., the earth],
All his affairs were completed by us on your behalf. (JRt 482)
The command to protect the earth, marked with the characteristics [of sovereignty], from the crest-jewel among the wise —
That garland, strung upon his counsel, we place at the base of the crown. (JRt 483)
By [your] exile and return, obeying the command of your father,

children.text: śrīRāma iva bhūlokaṃ yaśobhis svam apūpuraḥ || 484 ||
children.translated_text: You, like <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, have filled the mortal world with your fame. (JRt 484)

children.text: bhūto bhāvī ca sammāno yady api svaguṇais tava /
children.translated_text: Though honor, past and future, is yours by your own virtues,
By accepting the position of heir-apparent, you would lighten my burden. (JRt 485)
Your steadfastness, the company of the court, the gathering of various kinsmen,
And the charge of your protection — these dispel [my] despondency. (JRt 486)
For great men who have died and who dwell in foreign lands,

children.text: mahatāṃ na hi jātu syād vibhavena sukhodgamaḥ || 487 ||
children.translated_text: There is never any arising of happiness through fame alone without prosperity. (JRt 487)
Through you, who are the mirror-image of his form, [and] of the heaven-dweller —
Let our burden of longing for him be removed by [your] sight. (JRt 488)
'That one is the son of <s>Śāhābadena</s>' — in another realm,
May you not have the finger-pointing designation [given] as to a commoner. (JRt 489)
You, looked to by kings worthy of my compassion, being their observer —

children.text: Kaśmīraiśvaryam atulaṃ mā naiṣīr alpakaṃ svayam || 490 ||
children.translated_text: Do not bring the incomparable sovereignty of <s>Kaśmīra</s> to a small state yourself. (JRt 490)
Sharing the burden of the earth with you, as upon Mount <s>Meru</s>,
May I, <s>Anantadyuti</s>, attain incomparable prosperity and happiness.' (JRt 491)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 52
Filling his ears with fame sung by celestial women, through the bestowal of royal fortune upon a worthy one,

children.text: sa karṇapūrayan rājā mādṛta svargamālatīḥ // JRt_B.572 //
children.translated_text: That king cherished the jasmine-garlands of heaven. (JRt B.572)

children.text:
priyayor āvayos snehaśrutisaukhyena śītalaiḥ /
niśśvāsair bhūpates svīyais syād aspṛhyaṃ ca cāmaram // JRt_B.573 //
children.translated_text: By the breath of the king, cooled by the pleasure of hearing of the love between us two dear ones, the royal fan would have been unnecessary. (JRt B.573)

children.text: yena mānena mām anvagrahīt sa vasudhādhipaḥ /
children.translated_text: With the same honor with which that lord of the earth received me,

children.text: tvaṃ sañcarasva tenaiva mayi pālayati prajāḥ || 492 ||
children.translated_text: Do you conduct yourself in the same manner while I protect the subjects.' (JRt 492)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 53

children.text:
trātā dyauś Śakrarājabhyām āvābhyāṃ ca samaṃ mahī /
Śeṣaikanāthāṃ pātālaLakṣmīṃ hasatu nissukhām // JRt_B.575 //
children.translated_text: 'Heaven is protected by <s>Śakra</s> and the king, and the earth equally by us two; let the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the netherworld, which has only <s>Śeṣa</s> as lord, laugh joylessly.' (JRt B.575)
The prosperity attended by the execution of the counsel of ministers led by <s>Udayaśrī</s> —
Do not render it vain by prohibiting my interest.' (JRt 493)
Then, not knowing the fickleness of the ears of the king of elephants [i.e., the king's susceptibility to counsel],
He, the reader of the letter, entered the territory of the <s>Kaśmīras</s>. (JRt 494)
By the winds coming from the front, carrying the buzzing sound [of bees],
The prince was as if being turned back from entering <s>Kaśmīra</s>. (JRt 495)
As he entered the road to <s>Kaśmīra</s>, he blazed forth,
but the incitement of wicked men clouded the king's hearing. || 496 ||

children.text: nakrās samudram iva kecid udetukāmā vātā latāntam iva kecana darpavṛttyā /
children.translated_text: Like crocodiles wishing to rise from the ocean, like winds assailing the tips of creepers with arrogance,
evil-minded counselors — fires consuming the forest-circle of the world — agitated the king. || 497 ||
Then, when <s>Hassana</s>, the king's son, entered <s>Kaśmīra</s>,
King <s>Kudbhadena</s> was told by slanderers: || 498 ||
"The wisdom of the Supreme Lord is above all wisdoms;
nevertheless, the determination of what is beneficial and harmful should be communicated by ministers. || 499 ||
Among kings who shine with portions of the splendor of <s>Purandara</s> and other world-lords,
danger is seen to come from their own kinsmen. || 500 ||
From one renowned as destructive by mere touch, in the form of a brother — a crooked-moving one —

children.text: kṛṣṇasarpād ivāśliṣṭāt kaṣṭaṃ dūre na kasyacit || 501 ||
children.translated_text: as from a black serpent when embraced — alas! no one is far from danger. || 501 ||

Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 92
As if out of fear of seeing him, the self-born sacred fires vanished;

children.text: tadā Hutāśo nāśoci nikaṭasthair drumaiḫ param // JRt_B.770 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hutāśa</s> (fire) then mourned only for the nearby trees.

children.text:
bhītyevāpaḫ prakāśya svās trisandhyaṃ tatra majjataḥ /
Sandhyādevī paraṃ vandhyā tasyāgād anukampyatām // JRt_B.771 //
children.translated_text: As if out of fear, revealing her own waters at the three twilights, bathing there, the goddess <s>Sandhyā</s>, rendered barren, became worthy of compassion.
When the entire collection of images of the gods had been reduced to mere stories,
<s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s> then experienced bliss, as if freed from an illness.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 93
The illustrious <s>Sekandara</s>, through the marriage of two daughters of <s>Śrī Śobhā</s>,
won over the lords of <s>Sindhu</s> and <s>Udabhāṇḍapura</s>.
The king released <s>Merasaida Mahammada</s>, who was eager for his own country,

children.text: rājā sahacarīkṛtya Śobhāputraṃ sa Pirvajam // JRt_B.774 //
children.translated_text: having made <s>Pirvaja</s>, the son of <s>Śobhā</s>, his companion.

children.text:
darśitair Mausulaiś śāstrair jātidveṣamayair iva /
aśrāvi tena tad rājā kim asādhyaṃ durātmanā // JRt_B.775 //
children.translated_text: By showing him <s>Mausulī</s> (Mosul/Islamic) scriptures, which seemed filled with caste-hatred, the king was made to listen — what is unachievable for that wicked one?
Like a child eating unwholesome food, that <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>, together with the feudatories,
then exerted himself in the destruction of the people's caste.
When the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> declared "We shall die if our caste is destroyed,"
he, on the pretext of protecting their caste, seized them with severe punishment.
Through greed for obtaining the king's favor, among those who depended on the king,
even those of a caste higher than <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> abandoned it without delay.
The illustrious <s>Siṃhabhaṭṭa</s> and <s>Kastūṭa</s>, merchants who attained praise,
and the excellent <s>Śrī Nirmalācārya</s>, who attained praise in the three worlds —
since those two, relinquishing caste-attachment and following another religion,
then opposed both the drought and the <s>Turuṣka</s> punishment.
The excellent <s>Nirmalācārya</s>, in an instant abandoning all his possessions like straw,

children.text: tyajan rājaprasādena na jātiṃ svām adūṣayat || 610 ||
children.translated_text: did not defile his own caste through royal favor.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 94
Before the eyes of all people, <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s> (the staff of Brahmā) fell from heaven.
Wounded by it on his body, his frame soaked with spreading sores,
swarming with clusters of worms, he was as if worked upon by saws.
Having experienced agony that was a foretaste of the torments of hell,
after several nights, his life-breaths, eager to depart, left him;
the lord of punishment suffered the punishment inflicted by <s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s>.

children.text:
daṇḍākrāntas sa rājātha Merakhānaṃ nije pade /
abhiṣicyĀliśāhākhyāṃ kṛtvāsyāgād Yamālayam // JRt_B.781 //
children.translated_text: That king, struck by punishment, then consecrated <s>Merakhāna</s> in his own position, gave him the name <s>Āliśāha</s>, and went to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Since the master is punishable for the offenses of his servants,
Time became wrathful with the king due to the offenses of <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>.
King <s>Sikandara</s>, having consecrated his eldest son,
then passed away in the year [ending in] eight-nine, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s>.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 95

children.text: rūpaṃ niṣphalam arcitaṃ kim api tan mandān amandāgrahān bhaktān yas samanugrahītum atulasvācchandyavandyakriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: That Lord who, with incomparable, sovereign, and worshipful acts, graciously favors his devotees — whether slow or swift in their grasp — who have worshipped his form, whatever it may be, though fruitless otherwise;

children.text: Gaurīrūpakarīṃ vapussahacarīṃ svāṃ śaktim avyaktayad bhuktiṃ muktipurassarīṃ diśatu vo devas svayambhūr ayam // JRt_B.784 //
children.translated_text: who manifested his own <s>Śakti</s> (power), the companion of his body, fashioner of <s>Gaurī</s>'s form — may that self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>) god bestow upon you enjoyment preceded by liberation!
Let my voice rest all the more on the plain of the account of <s>Śāhikhāna</s>,
fatigued by the climbing of the peak-summits of the narratives of other kings.

children.text:
tadguṇaugharasaślāghyāṃ pibantv api giraṃ mama /
sugandhighanasāreṇa kūpāmbho 'pi manoramam // JRt_B.786 //
children.translated_text: Let people drink even this speech of mine, praiseworthy for the flavor of his flood of virtues — even well-water becomes delightful with fragrant dense camphor.
<s>Āliśāha</s>, the moon of nectar for the earth, then cut through the darkness of the world
that had begun at twilight, after the setting of his father the sun.

children.text: adarpakacitaṃ bālaṃ prauḍhā Lakṣmīr muhur muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: The mature <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune), repeatedly, with limbs full of modesty,
embraced that young king, born of a noble family.
Ps-JRT 96

children.text:
tasya bālyaṃ manohāri viśeṣād rājyarājitam /
kāntiṃ kalayate kāntaḫ pūrṇenduś śaradi sphuran // JRt_B.789 //
children.translated_text: His captivating youth, especially adorned by kingship, possesses a beauty that the lovely full moon radiating in autumn alone can match.
Even though he was young, the kings bowed to him as to the previous lord of the earth;

children.text: ahidaṣṭo hi dāmāpi kramituṃ na pragalbhate || 615 ||
children.translated_text: for one bitten by a snake does not dare even to step over a rope.
Through the strength of his own intelligence, brought about as being conducive to fate,
<s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s> attained the foremost position among the ministers.
He forcibly captured the lord of the <s>Ladda</s> route, who had laid down his weapons in trust,
together with his sons, except for <s>Muhammad</s>.
The valorous <s>Muhammad</s>, upon merely hearing of the capture of the lord of the route,
fled by the <s>Bhāṅgilācala</s> mountain path, being familiar with the routes.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 99

children.text: mārutasyeva vīrasyeva gatiẖ kvāpi na hanyate /
children.translated_text: Like the wind, like a hero — his course was not obstructed anywhere.
Hearing of his departure, the one suspicious of a breach in counsel, through messengers,
suddenly resolved to imprison the lord of the <s>Ladda</s> route.
Under the pretext of examining <s>Mārgeśa</s>'s illness, for the sake of obtaining his bed,

children.text: viśvāsanāya ca prāsyad bhaṭṭOtsaṃ tasya sadmani // JRt_B.817 //
children.translated_text: and for gaining his trust, he cast <s>Bhaṭṭa Utsava</s> into his house.
<s>Utsava</s>, the carrier of medicines for treatment, disregarded by <s>Mārgeśa</s> the great fish,
did not perceive the fish-hook concealed within the bait.
Meanwhile, the minister swiftly besieged the mansion of the lord of the path

children.text: javād rodhitavān mantrī dāśo nīḍaṃ tṛṇair iva // JRt_B.819 //
children.translated_text: with warriors fierce in their lion-roars, like a fisherman [blocks] a nest with reeds.

children.text:
tīkṣṇair api dayāviṣṭair iṣṭair iva sa vihvalaiḥ /
kathañcid doṣarahito mārgeśas samarudhyata // JRt_B.820 //
children.translated_text: By men who, though sharp, were filled with compassion, though beloved, were agitated— somehow <s>Mārgeśa</s> was confined without fault.
The fearless one being confined—like <s>Śaṅkara</s> who deems himself free of poison—
was mocked even by the surgical blade of wisdom, though extremely sharp and yet unused.

children.text: apaśyan darpataẖ kiñcit siṃho viśatu vāgurām /
children.translated_text: Out of pride, not seeing a thing, a lion may enter a snare;

children.text: citraṃ tu tad viśet pāśaṃ dūradṛśvāpi yat khagaḥ || 620 ||
children.translated_text: but it is wondrous that even a far-sighted bird should enter a trap.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 100

children.text: tato mārgapateḫ putrān meṣān iva sa saunikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, like a butcher [seizing] sheep, he confined the sons of the lord of the path,

children.text: ruddhavān uddhatakrodhaḫ pāpmā mūrta ivāparaḥ // JRt_B.823 //
children.translated_text: with rage fully aroused—like sin incarnate in another form.

children.text:
tābhyāṃ saparivārābhyāṃ kārāgāram apūpurat /
na paraṃ bhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ duryaśobhiś ca niścalaiḥ // JRt_B.824 //
children.translated_text: With those two and their retinues he filled the prison, and the entire world was filled with unshakeable infamy.
Hearing this in a single day, <s>Mahmada</s>, anxious about his prospects,
was tormented day and night, like a poor man over a daughter.
In the <s>Durdaṇḍa</s> region, in the house of a friend named <s>Govinda</s>,
<s>Muhammad</s> entered trustingly, for the purpose of rest.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 101

children.text:
śrīSekandaradattaitaddeśādhīkāraśālinā /
Mahmadasya purā śākhī tenānāṭi hi durdhiyā // JRt_B.827 //
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Sekandara</s> had previously granted authority over that region, but that evil-minded one did not honor the friendship with <s>Mahmada</s>.

children.text: vahner dhūmavivardhitaś śamayati jvālābharaṃ vārido vṛkṣakṣodabhavo vanāni nayati kṣipraṃ kṛśānuẖ kṣayam /
children.translated_text: Rain quenches the blaze of fire intensified by smoke; fire born from the felling of trees quickly reduces forests to ashes; a poison-tree may cause the burning of its own birthplace—a person overcome by greed betrays even his greatest benefactor.

children.text: dāhaṃ janmabhuvo diśed viṣatarur vairasyadoṣāvahaṃ druhyaty atyupakāriṇe 'pi nitarāṃ lobhābhibhūto janaḥ || 623 ||
children.translated_text: Enmity born of fault brings ruin.
When <s>Muhammad</s> arrived and entered the house of the path-lord in trust,

children.text: sa Govindakhaśaś citte kṣaṇam evam acintayat || 624 ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Khaśa</s> <s>Govinda</s> pondered in his mind for a moment thus:
"By minister <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>, the guardian against upheavals in the kingdom,
the evil-minded <s>Muhammad</s> was branded as one who caused dual sovereignty.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 102
The harm done to one who commits harm is like play;

children.text: nāḍīva vraṇitā jātu na śuṣyati kathañcana // JRt_B.831 //
children.translated_text: yet that harm, like a wounded vein, never dries up.

children.text:
pariṇāme 'tiduẖkhena sukhenāsukhasīmani /
apathyeneva kiṃ nas syāt sevitenāmunā phalam // JRt_B.832 //
children.translated_text: If the result, at the boundary of joy and sorrow, brings great suffering in the end, what fruit would we gain by serving this man, as if from unwholesome food?
This sinner, inclined toward treason against the king, powerless and afraid,

children.text: mama deśaṃ praviṣṭo 'dya rakṣaṇīyo na yujyate" || 626 ||
children.translated_text: has entered my territory today—he ought not to be protected."
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 103
Thus having deliberated, that crooked one who had [betrayed] the trust—

children.text: suptaṃ harim iva vyādho Govindas taṃ nibaddhavān // JRt_B.834 //
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> bound <s>Mahmada</s> then, like a hunter [binding] a sleeping lion.

children.text:
anekenātha ratnena nissapatnatvalipsayā /
ekaṃ Sūhas sa puṃratnam akrīṇān Mahmadaṃ tataḥ // JRt_B.835 //
children.translated_text: Desiring unrivaled possession, with many jewels, <s>Sūha</s> then purchased that one gem among men, <s>Mahmada</s>.
Meanwhile, the searchers of excellent intellect, dispatched by <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>,
arrived at the house of <s>Govinda</s>, the <s>Khaśa</s> lord.

children.text: maitrīm ullaṅghya nirvyūḍhām āsritasya ca rakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Transgressing the established friendship and the duty of protecting one who sought refuge,

children.text: Muhammadaṃ nijam mitram arpayām āsa durmatiḥ || 628 ||
children.translated_text: that wicked-minded one surrendered his own friend <s>Muhammad</s>.

children.text: suptaṃ harim iva vyādho yadā baddhvākṣipat Khaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the <s>Khaśa</s>, having bound him like a hunter [binds] a sleeping lion, cast him away,

children.text: paśuvat taṃ tadā te 'tha Kaśmīrān ānayan drutam || 629 ||
children.translated_text: they then swiftly brought him to <s>Kaśmīra</s> like a beast.

children.text: mantrārditasya phaṇinaḫ plavagāś capeṭair vyādhās saṭāvighaṭanān nirasor hareś ca /
children.translated_text: Monkeys slap a snake subdued by charms; hunters part the mane of a captive lion— what do they gain from a bound one, weakened and cowardly, through insults, besides blame?

children.text: baddhasya kātaratayābalino 'vamānair nindāṃ vinā kim iva nāma paraṃ labhante || 630 ||
children.translated_text: Nothing indeed.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 104

children.text:
karoṭīṭaṅkanāghaṭṭaradaṭāṅkārakuṭṭanaiḥ /
paryabhūyata jihmena Sūhabhaṭṭena Mahmadaḥ // JRt_B.839 //
children.translated_text: With blows of skull-striking, the clanging of teeth, and poundings, <s>Mahmada</s> was humiliated by the crooked <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>.
Fearing that the honored one who had been dishonored would flee,
<s>Sūha</s> imprisoned him in <s>Bahurūpa</s>, a mighty fortress.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 105

children.text:
hitaiṣiṇo nijaprāṇair devasya svānujīvinaḥ /
viṣaye 'smin hy adhīkāras tenāmandam adhīyata // JRt_B.841 //
children.translated_text: The well-wishing retainers of the lord, with their own lives, acquired authority in this realm through him, and not without joy.

children.text: vidyuddyotabharair niśi pravasataḫ pānthān navo vāridaḥ pañcāsyo vanavāsino mṛgagaṇān vyāvṛttya viprekṣitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: A new rain-cloud terrifies travelers at night with bursts of lightning-glow; a five-faced [lion] turns back herds of deer with sidelong glances of forest-dwellers; the son of the sun-god, <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), with crooked movements through the zodiac signs beginning with Aries, fate, reassuring sinners with auspicious appearances, then overthrows them.

children.text: gatyā vakragatair dineśatanayo rāśīn ajādīn vidhir bhadrābhāsavilokanair duritino viśvāsya paryasyati || 632 ||
children.translated_text: Such is destiny.
Then, awakened through the agency of a slave-woman named <s>Śāhā</s>,
<s>Mahmada</s> was extracted from the place of bondage by his foster-brothers.
He, saying "I am drenched in sweat and will bathe," deceived his guards,
and having entered the bathing chamber, departed from there.
Reaching the spot where a breach had been made in the joint by his foster-brothers,
<s>Muhammad</s> then slipped out, like a <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) through the gap of <s>Krauñca</s> mountain.

children.text: roṣād iva srutiṃ hantuṃ niṣpatan nirjharāmbhasām /
children.translated_text: Rushing forth as if in rage to strike the cascade of waterfall streams,

children.text: bhṛgor iva tato durgād adāj jhampām akampitaḥ || 636 ||
children.translated_text: he leaped unflinchingly from that fortress, as if from the cliff of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: aśaknuvann amuṃ roddhuṃ pāṣāṇā rakṣiṇo na ca /
children.translated_text: Unable to restrain him, neither the boulders nor the guards—
only the waterfalls [echoed] the clanking imitation of the fetters on his feet.
The foster-brothers of <s>Mahmada</s>, breaking the strong fetters,
considered <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s> broken along with his kinsmen.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 106

children.text:
himagamanataẖ klāntasvānto himaṃ manute 'nalaṃ taṭatarumukhaṃ nāvā gacchan vrajat paripaśyati /
valati nitarāṃ viśvaṃ viśvaṃ vivetti ca mūrchitaḥ saralahṛdaye śaṅkāgrastas tanoty atiśaṅkitām // JRt_B.849 //
children.translated_text: Exhausted from traveling through snow, he considers snow to be fire; traveling on a boat, he perceives the riverbank trees as moving; he keeps revolving and perceiving the whole world, the fainted one—in his guileless heart, seized by suspicion, he extends extreme apprehension.
Fearing <s>Muhammad</s>'s escape in the same manner,
the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, though he had already drained the treasury, killed the aged <s>Mārgeśa</s>.
When the aged lord of the path was killed by the evil-minded <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>,
all the people wept as if for their own father, with intense reproach.

children.text: ṛkṣais saṃlakṣayann āśāviśeṣaṃ niśi niśy atha /
children.translated_text: Observing the particular directions by the stars night after night,

children.text: pakṣīva nīḍabhraṣṭas sa Sūho lokabhayād ayāt || 641 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūha</s> then fled from fear of the world, like a bird dislodged from its nest.

children.text: ahas tasya vihastasya rātrir āsīn niśā dinam /
children.translated_text: Day became night for that distressed one, and night became day;

children.text: viparyeti dhruvaṃ sarvaṃ vidhau vidhuratāṃ gate || 642 ||
children.translated_text: certainly everything becomes reversed when fate turns hostile.

children.text: kārānāvaṃ samullaṅghya calitaṃ taṃ smaran muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Remembering again and again that one who had leaped over the prison-boat and departed,
the fisherman <s>Sūha</s> attained grief over the great fish <s>Muhammad</s>.
By the people who had been protected and cherished by minister <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>,
the illustrious <s>Sekandara</s> was recognized as deceased merely by his disappearance.
The illustrious <s>Sekandaraśāhi</s>, <s>Śobhādevī</s>'s own son—
for the purpose of eliminating sedition, he had banished him from his own land.
Honored by the lord of the north as a prince,

children.text: Kaśmīrān āyayau jetuṃ tam ādāyātha Mahmadaḥ || 646 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahmada</s> then came to conquer <s>Kaśmīra</s>, having taken him along.
Hearing that <s>Piruja</s> had come along with <s>Turuṣka</s> armies,
<s>Sūha</s> dispatched the illustrious <s>Ladda</s> and <s>Gauraka</s> to oppose them.
Through the counsel of the illustrious <s>Laddarāja</s> and the valor of <s>Gauraka</s>,

children.text: sā Turuṣkacamūś śāntā vyādhir dānajapair iva || 648 ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Turuṣka</s> army was pacified, like a disease by gifts and chanting.
The minister, freed from fear, then appointed governors:
<s>Laddarāja</s>, <s>Gaurabhaṭṭa</s>, and <s>Kramarājyeśvara</s>.
Like at the twilight hour, when <s>Sūha</s> had colored the mountain-king above,
the king and the crown prince did not rise together like sun and moon.

children.text: śyeno hanti patatriṇo mṛgapatir niṣpātayiṣṇur mṛgān bhidyante maṇayo 'pi vajramaṇinā khātā khanitrair mahī /
children.translated_text: A hawk kills birds; a lion, eager to strike, slays deer; even gems are split by the diamond-stone; the earth is excavated by pickaxes; planets and their hosts are scattered by the radiant sun, like flowers— mostly, the fear of humiliation is observed to come from one's own kind.

children.text: puṣpāṇīva ca bhāsvatā grahagaṇās sūryeṇa nirdhūnitāḥ prāyeṇātra vilokyate paribhavatrāsas sajātīyataḥ || 651 ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is seen in this world.
Though urged again and again by this one to persecute the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
the illustrious King <s>Sekandara</s> was compassionate and tender of heart.
Whatever limit the great tide of the <s>Yavanas</s> had somehow established,
the settled order of taxation upon the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> was thereafter transgressed by him.
Hostile to other faiths, the twilight that is a storehouse of darkness—
that wicked one prohibited the <s>nāgas</s>' (serpent deities') sacrifices, pilgrimages, and other rites.
Fearing that the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, contracted by terror, would protect their caste
by emigrating to foreign lands, that one of undiminished jealousy
commanded all the guards of the roads thus: "Without the passport of liberation, no one is to be given a way out."
Thus he ordered all those in charge of road-checkpoints.

children.text: tato mīnān iva vyādho dattabandhe sarijjale /
children.translated_text: Then, like a hunter [trapping] fish in the river's waters where a net has been cast,
that most wicked-born one further oppressed the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> in this land.
Many <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, [to escape] the torment of the fire of his fear and sin,
suddenly ended it by entering the flames of fire.

children.text: kecid viṣeṇa pāśena pare toyena cāpare /
children.translated_text: Some by poison, some by noose, others by water,

children.text: bhṛguṇā vahninā cānye viprā bhītyā vipedire || 659 ||
children.translated_text: and yet others by casting themselves from cliffs or into fire—the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> perished from fear.
Even the king's favorites, through a thousand acts of treason,

children.text: na tv ekam aśakan vipram etasmin dveṣadūṣite || 660 ||
children.translated_text: could not save a single <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in this one corrupted by hatred.

children.text: durvahatvena nindan sa rājyabhāram alaṃ khalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Censuring the burden of kingship as unbearable, that villain, alas,
boasted of the joy he gained from hearing the cries of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Like smoke from a house, the rows of proud <s>brāhmaṇas</s>
departed from that land of closed doors by side-paths.

children.text: tyaktvāpi pitaraṃ putras taṃ pitā cāgamad dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> son abandoned his father, and a father his son, and went,
as <s>Sūha</s> the destroyer cast aspersions, to foreign lands as if to the next world.

children.text: kṣmā rūkṣā kṣāmam aśanaṃ vyāyāmo vedanāmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Rough earth, meager food, exertion that brought only pain and disease—
foreign lands became a living hell for those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
On the road, many <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, afflicted by fear of raiding snake-lords, by severe heat, and by meager food,
considered the attainment of death to be happiness.

children.text: kva ca snānaṃ kva ca dhyānaṃ tapaẖ kva ca japaẖ kva ca /
children.translated_text: Where was bathing, where was meditation, where was austerity, where was chanting?

children.text: bhikṣārtham aṭatāṃ grāmān agāt kālo dvijanmanām || 666 ||
children.translated_text: The time of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> passed in wandering through villages for alms.
Alas, benefit came to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> from the face of persecution—

children.text: yat tannirvāsitās sarve pāpaṃ tīrtheṣv anāśayan || 667 ||
children.translated_text: in that all those who were exiled destroyed their sins at holy pilgrimage sites.
Having gone to foreign lands, drying up with anxiety over protecting their families,

children.text: Mlecchaveṣā dvijāẖ kecit Kaśmīreṣv eva cābhraman || 668 ||
children.translated_text: some <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, wearing the garb of <s>Mlecchas</s>, still wandered within <s>Kaśmīra</s>.
Wishing to sever learning, by him whose livelihood had been destroyed,
the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> begged from door to door for offerings, like dogs, out of greed for alms-balls.

children.text: Turuṣkadarśane bhaktyā na tu dveṣeṇa sa dvijān /
children.translated_text: He flooded the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> into the <s>Turuṣka</s> faith by devotion, not by hatred—

children.text: vyaplāvayad ataś cāsmin hatyā na prajagalbhire || 670 ||
children.translated_text: therefore killings were not boasted of in this regard.

children.text: ity ākhyac ca sa evaiṣāṃ sa tasya parihāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus he himself proclaimed, and he was their exemption-giver—
but the sight of deeds capable of illuminating hatred [told a different story].
The ocean of jewels upon which the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> relied, as protectors of the earth,
who made efforts to protect their faction—that was <s>Kṣudrabhaṭṭa</s>, his favorite.
The supreme teacher of the <s>Yavanas</s>, named <s>Malānordīna</s>,
he, out of shrewdness, suspecting "he is a traitor," had him imprisoned.

children.text: yataḫ prabhṛti sa prāpad rājyam acchattracāmaram /
children.translated_text: From the time he obtained a kingdom without royal parasol or fly-whisk,
from that time, the blemish upon his faith [appeared] like an affliction of disease.
Even in dreams he did not abandon <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>, who had crushed his enemies;
enjoyment and virtuous impressions are the fruit of exceedingly pure austerities. || 675 ||
Of his ministers, like seasons full of fruit,
honor's loss or gain depended on the luminous one, as the sun governs seasons. || 676 ||
Seeing in <s>Śāhikhāna</s> alone both counsel and valor,
he was so utterly alarmed by anxiety that he never fell asleep. || 677 ||
Though watching the turbid <s>Sūha</s>-serpent with a venomous gaze,
<s>Śāhikhāna</s>, that lamp, was unable to dispel the darkness. || 678 ||
With the persecution of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the condemnation of the scriptures, the contemplation of treachery,

children.text: cikitsayā ca tasyābdair yātaṃ tricaturais tathā || 679 ||
children.translated_text: and with remedies, thus three or four years passed. || 679 ||
Ps-JRT 107
His fault, as if inherited, through the examination of mere pretexts,
with restrained energy, persisted in harassing <s>Śāhikhāna</s>. // JRt_B.891 //

children.text:
valīmukhamanojñas sa prajābhāgyabalodayāt /
anaiṣīd bhagnatāṃ Śāhikhānacintāmaṇiṃ na ca // JRt_B.892 //
children.translated_text: He, whose wrinkled face was charming, through the rise of fortune and the power of the people's merit, did not bring the wish-fulfilling gem of <s>Śāhikhāna</s> to destruction. // JRt_B.892 //
Impelled solely by the rise of the people's merit, arising from evil deeds,
a wasting disease, difficult to cure, consumed the twice-born king. || 680 ||

children.text: anālokyaivendor udayam agamiṣyad yadi śamaṃ samantān nādityopaladahanarāśivyatikaraḥ /
children.translated_text: If he had not seen the moonrise and was about to attain peace, and if there were no conflagration of sun-stones all around,
why then did he not see the cooling of the earth's heat by the waters of moon-stones, which flow at the rise of the moon? || 681 ||

children.text: varṣāṃs tricaturān anyāñ jīvec cet sa na kiṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: If he were to live another three or four years, what then?
At the rise of <s>Śāhikhāna</s>, he would see here itself the fruit of his own sins. || 682 ||

children.text: jīvaty eva tatas Sūhabhaṭṭe bhītyā palāyitam /
children.translated_text: Thus, while <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s> was still alive, having fled out of fear,
resting briefly, <s>Haṃsa</s> and <s>Gaura</s> quickly bound <s>Laddarāja</s>. || 683 ||

children.text: Śrīdhenau rāgiṇau tau dvau madodagrau vṛṣāv iva /
children.translated_text: Those two, passionate over <s>Śrī</s> (sovereignty), like two bulls maddened with rut,
began fighting each other for the breaking of horns, after the twice-born one died. || 684 ||
When <s>Laddarāja</s> was released from prison by <s>Haṃsa</s> in battle,

children.text: prāṇāṃs tyaktvā Gaurabhaṭṭas surastrīṇāṃ mudaṃ vyadhāt || 685 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurabhaṭṭa</s>, giving up his life, delighted the celestial women. || 685 ||
Abandoning the fickleness of an elephant's ear, having no other course,

children.text: puṃścalyeva patir vṛddho bheje Haṃsas tadā Śriyā || 686 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (sovereignty), like a wanton woman, embraced old <s>Haṃsa</s> as her husband. || 686 ||
Though young, <s>Śāhikhāna</s> did not tolerate his arrogance;

children.text: śaśīva timirasphāraṃ na hi tejo vayo'nugam || 687 ||
children.translated_text: for splendor does not follow age, as the moon's [brightness defies] the spread of darkness. || 687 ||
The crown prince, skilled in counsel, having conferred with the <s>Ṭhakkuras</s>,
slew <s>Haṃsabhaṭṭa</s> in battle as he was destroying <s>Laddarāja</s>. || 688 ||
The people's love flowed toward <s>Śāhikhāna</s> like water to a low place;
when there is abundant mango fruit, the bee scorns the jasmine. || 689 ||
Eager to embrace the crown prince, exalted by victory,
<s>Rājyaśrī</s> (the goddess of sovereignty), for lack of opportunity, became anxious with longing. || 690 ||
Out of affection, out of refined sensibility, and from the weight of the people's devotion,
the king entrusted the burden of authority to the crown prince. || 691 ||
Of the evil-minded <s>Turk</s> named <s>Merakaṃsāra</s>,
blinded by rut like an elephant, his (<s>Śāhikhāna</s>'s) virtues served as the goad that was detested. || 692 ||

children.text: suciraṃ malinai rājño mānasaṃ vāridair iva /
children.translated_text: For a long time, the impure ones, like rain-clouds raining slander,

children.text: paiśunyavarṣibhir netuṃ mālinyaṃ na sma śakyate || 693 ||
children.translated_text: were unable to lead the king's mind to defilement. || 693 ||
The king, affectionate toward his devoted, capable younger brother, fond of dependents,
through their excessive incitement, became anxious even about the kingdom. || 694 ||

children.text: yuvarājaṃ sevakāṃś ca rakṣituṃ svān mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: To protect the crown prince and his own servants, the king,
expressing a desire to visit sacred sites, spoke to him thus: || 695 ||
"Wealth that is not used for offerings, a mind that is not a mirror for meditation,
a body that does not journey to sacred sites — in the end, these come to a pitiable state. || 696 ||

children.text: diggajeṣv iva yuṣmāsu bhūbhāraṃ nyastavān aham /
children.translated_text: I have placed the burden of the earth upon you, as upon the elephants of the quarters;
like another <s>Śeṣa</s>, I depart for the service of <s>Puruṣottama</s>." || 697 ||
The ocean that was <s>Śāhikhāna</s>, churned by the <s>Mandara</s>-mountain of love,
then offered to the lord a new speech, like a digit of the nectar-moon. || 698 ||
"Let the abuse of sacred sites be far from the mass of doubts;
let the protection of the subjects, the door to fame and merit, be yours. || 699 ||

children.text: cirasya pālitāṃ pitryāṃ hitvā niśśaraṇāṃ mahīm /
children.translated_text: Abandoning the ancestral earth, long protected and without refuge,
you, a hero, will be marked by all as either merciless or powerless. || 700 ||
If the lord's longing for pilgrimage is indeed excessive,

children.text: ārādhakānām asmākaṃ kim anyat kāryam ucyatām" || 701 ||
children.translated_text: let it be spoken — what other task is there for us, your devotees?" || 701 ||

children.text: vyaktam ity uktavaty eva yuvarāje nareśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: When the crown prince spoke thus clearly, the king
with the gleam of a slight smile spoke beautiful words again: || 702 ||
"How much merit is gained from merely protecting subjects?
The supreme among elixirs is the savoring of multiple essences. || 703 ||

children.text: dehāt pṛthaṅ nivasato madbhujasyeva te vata /
children.translated_text: Seeing the valor of your arm, dwelling apart from my body,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā parākramaṃ śaṅkā madaśaktau kathaṃ bhavet || 704 ||
children.translated_text: how could there be doubt about my power? || 704 ||

children.text: etāvad api vākyaṃ me yadi naivānutiṣṭhasi /
children.translated_text: If you do not even carry out this much of my request,

children.text: tvayi saṅkalpitāś śeṣās tad āśās santu dūrataḥ" || 705 ||
children.translated_text: then let the remaining hopes I have placed in you be far away." || 705 ||
Speaking thus insistently, the king, for the purpose of pilgrimage,
by force compelled the crown prince to bear the burden of sovereignty for a long time. || 706 ||
23a) <s>Sulṭān Zayn al-'Ābidīn</s> (LS 4494-4495)
"You, bearing the illustrious name <s>Jainollābhadīna</s>, being a protector of the gods,

children.text: ciraṃ rājyaṃ kriyād" evaṃ rājāsyāśiṣam abhyadhāt || 707 ||
children.translated_text: may you reign long" — thus the king bestowed his blessing. || 707 ||
Out of eagerness to see sacred sites, the king departed from his own land,
but not from the heart of the crown prince, which was bolted with the lock of love. || 708 ||
Offering the essences of the treasury, jewels, and the best of horses,
the prince followed his brother for two or three halts, out of love and reverence. || 709 ||
Speaking of hardship on the road, of the effort involved, the meager fruit of pilgrimage,

children.text: uktvā mārge khalā rājñas tīrthaśraddhām akhaṇḍayan || 710 ||
children.translated_text: wicked men on the road broke the king's faith in sacred sites. || 710 ||
Considering it an insult to his own son-in-law, the proud
<s>Madrendra</s> then forcibly turned the king back from the pilgrimage. || 711 ||
When autumn arrived, the best of seasons, the king,

children.text: Madrarājas tam ādāya Kaśmīrān pratyagāt tataḥ || 712 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madrarāja</s>, taking him along, returned to <s>Kaśmīra</s>. || 712 ||
The new king was immersed in both delight — at his brother's return — and in displeasure — at <s>Madra</s>'s insistence;

children.text: navarājaḫ prasāde ca kāluṣye ca nimagnavān || 713 ||
children.translated_text: in both favor and resentment. || 713 ||
Ps-JRT 109
"Lest the army of <s>Madrendra</s> cause harm to the lord" —

children.text: iyeṣa Ṭhakkuraṃ rājā taṃ niroddhuṃ visṛṣṭavān // JRt_B.927 //
children.translated_text: thinking thus, the king released a <s>Ṭhakkura</s>, wishing to restrain him. // JRt_B.927 //

children.text:
yuddhaṃ vinānivartinyāṃ senāyāṃ Madrabhūpateḥ /
ājñāṃ vinākṣamo yoddhuṃ vyāvartata sa Ṭhakkuraḥ // JRt_B.928 //
children.translated_text: Since the army of the <s>Madra</s> king would not retreat without battle, and unable to fight without orders, that <s>Ṭhakkura</s> turned back. // JRt_B.928 //

children.text: kṣudreṣv atha sa Madreṣu yuvarājo mahāmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, against the petty <s>Madras</s>, the crown prince of great intellect,

children.text: bhrātus snehād ruṣaṃ tyaktvā rājyatyāgaṃ svayaṃ vyadhāt || 714 ||
children.translated_text: out of affection for his brother, abandoning his anger, voluntarily relinquished the kingdom. || 714 ||

children.text: tan nyastaṃ divasāvasānasamaye sūryasya tejo nijaṃ pratyūṣe pratipādayann atiśayaślāghyasvatejā bhavan /
children.translated_text: That glory of the sun deposited at the end of the day, restoring it at dawn, becoming one of surpassingly praiseworthy splendor —

children.text: vahnir yajvakulais tato 'pi divase śraddhānubandhākulais tejovṛddhimuṣā navena haviṣā yajñeṣu santarpyate || 715 ||
