children.translated_text: the fire is then further nourished in sacrifices by sacrificial families, anxious with faithful devotion, with fresh oblations that augment its splendor. || 715 ||

children.text: Ṭhakkurair anvito rājā pavanaẖ kusumair iva /
children.translated_text: The king, accompanied by the <s>Ṭhakkuras</s> like wind accompanied by flowers,

children.text: Kaśmīrebhyo gatas sarvair deśādhīśair natas tataḥ || 716 ||
children.translated_text: departed from <s>Kaśmīra</s>, honored by all the lords of provinces. || 716 ||

children.text: sukhaṃ tāvad agāhiṣṭa vītanakrāṃ nadīm iva /
children.translated_text: As long as it remained free of crocodiles, like entering a river,
the <s>Ṭhakkuras</s> enjoyed the land of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, abandoned by the <s>Madra</s> army. || 717 ||
Then the ancestral throne was extensively occupied by <s>Ālīśāha</s> (‛Alī Šāh), the king,

children.text: pitryaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ tena na tu sajjanamānasam || 718 ||
children.translated_text: but not the hearts of virtuous people. || 718 ||

children.text: udyaccheta kathaṃ jaḍadyutir aho dūrollasallāñchano gacched dīptakaro na ced dinakaro lokāntaraṃ svecchayā /
children.translated_text: How would one of dim luster rise? Alas, if the sun with its far-shining mark did not depart of its own will to another world with blazing rays,

children.text: vīreṇātyavahelayā viracito 'pakṣo jaḍaẖ kātaraḥ sambhāvya svaparākrameṇa vijayaṃ viśvaṃ tṛṇaṃ manyate || 719 ||
children.translated_text: the cowardly, dull, partisanless one, fashioned with utter contempt by the hero, presuming victory through his own valor, considers the world as straw. || 719 ||
By breaking branches, monkeys destroy a shady garden;
similarly, the <s>Turk</s> royal servants disturbed the realm. || 720 ||
From the cowardly king, with unaccomplished restraint,
the <s>Yavana</s> <s>Merakaṃsāra</s> wrought havoc upon the realm. || 721 ||
Like a dark bee making lotus-ponds shrink, that ignoble one
defiled the city women, polluted through forceful violation. || 722 ||
With great tuskers blinded by rut, creating muddiness —

children.text: akṣobhi maṇḍalaṃ svacchais saro marugajair iva || 723 ||
children.translated_text: the clear realm became turbid, like a lake by desert elephants. || 723 ||
Unstoppable by the counsel of ministers, unreturning even in daylight,

children.text: rakṣasām eva Kaśmīrās tadā hastavaśaṃ gatāḥ || 724 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Kaśmīras</s> then fell into the hands of what were verily demons. || 724 ||

children.text: arājakaṃ varaṃ rājyaṃ na svāmī tādṛśaḫ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Better a kingdom without a king than such a master;

children.text: abhūṣaṇau varaṃ karṇau na punar lohakuṇḍalam || 725 ||
children.translated_text: better ears without ornaments than iron earrings. || 725 ||
Ps-JRT 110

children.text:
himād agnis tamas sūryāc chilā vyomnas tadāpatat /
yat pālako 'pi bhūpālas sarvalokakṣayo 'bhavat // JRt_B.941 //
children.translated_text: Fire fell from snow, darkness from the sun, stones from the sky — for even the king who was the protector became the destroyer of all people. // JRt_B.941 //

children.text: sadma tuṅgaṃ varo vājī svacchaṃ vāso maṇir mahān /
children.translated_text: A lofty mansion, an excellent horse, fine garments, great jewels —

children.text: svīkṛtaṃ Yavanais tat tad yad yac chobhāvahaṃ prabhoḥ || 726 ||
children.translated_text: whatever was splendid and belonged to the lord was seized by the <s>Yavanas</s>. || 726 ||

children.text: akārṣīt pañcaṣān māsān rājyaṃ sa jaḍanāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: That dull-witted leader ruled for five or six months,
not through his own deed but through the ripening of the people's sins. || 727 ||

children.text: mālinyaṃ sumanaḫprathāḫ prathayate dainyaṃ nidhatte dṛśaḥ sūryālokatiraskṛtaṃ ca kurute saṃhāram āśā nayan /
children.translated_text: Filth spreads the fame of flowers, dejection dwells in the eyes, it obscures the sight of the sun, and bringing destruction to hopes —

children.text: unnidraẖ kam upadravaṃ na tarasā kurvīta dhūmodgamo noddyotetatarāṃ śikhī yadi mahājvālākalāpākulaḥ || 728 ||
children.translated_text: what oppression would the awakened one not swiftly inflict through the rising of smoke? The fire would not blaze even more if agitated by a mass of great flames. || 728 ||
To repay the debt of the kingdom given by the illustrious <s>Sekandara</s>,
desiring the fruit of his own sovereignty, || 729 ||
filled with hatred for <s>Madrendra</s>, Lord <s>Khuṅkhura</s>
then invited the new king through messengers to come to his own land. || 730 ||

children.text: nakro na cej jalanidher bahir abhyupeyāt kākas tyajen na varapādapam unnataṃ cet /
children.translated_text: If the crocodile would not come out of the ocean, if the crow would not abandon the lofty tree,

children.text: ākhur na ced gahanagartaguhāṃ vimuñced dhantavyatāṃ katham avāpnuyur eva tat te || 731 ||
children.translated_text: if the mouse would not leave the deep hole of its burrow — how then would they be subject to being killed? || 731 ||
"This one gives shelter to the crown prince, my enemy" —

children.text: Jasrathaṃ prati bhūpālaẖ krodhād ity abhyaṣeṇayat || 732 ||
children.translated_text: thus the king, in anger, dispatched forces against <s>Jasratha</s>. || 732 ||
By his own disturbed ministers, whose greatness was eclipsed by the <s>Mlecchas</s>,
with his unrestrained zeal for enterprise, by double-salaried messengers, || 733 ||
his faith being shaken through stratagem, and by those living off two kingdoms,
those who wished to bring about the rise of the new king through letters, || 734 ||
the <s>Yavanas</s>, excessively praising him out of greed for favors,
whose daring was shattered upon hearing of the new king's overwhelming victory, || 735 ||
the king, whose enterprise was condemned by his own army, cowering with despair,

children.text: Mallekaṃ Jasrathaṃ jetuṃ prasthānam akarot tataḥ || 736 ||
children.translated_text: then set out to conquer the <s>Malleka</s> <s>Jasratha</s>. || 736 ||
As the lord of <s>Kaśmīra</s> went forth to confront the enemy,

children.text: āsīn mitrasya sāmmukhyaṃ na mitrāṇāṃ mahībhujām || 737 ||
children.translated_text: his friend stood face to face with him, but not his allied kings. || 737 ||
Ps-JRT 111
Perceiving his own excessive elevation and fearing a downfall,

children.text: Khujyākādas samaṃ mantram amantrayata mantribhiḥ // JRt_B.954 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khujyākāda</s> conferred together with ministers upon a counsel. // JRt_B.954 //
"The chief attributes of kings — counsel, valor, and the like —

children.text: ayaṃ bāliśabhāvasya bhājanaṃ kva janādhipaḥ // JRt_B.955 //
children.translated_text: Where is this lord of the people who is a vessel of childishness? (JRt B.955)

children.text: asmābhir nihitāś cāsminn upadeśā hitā api /
children.translated_text: The beneficial instructions placed by us upon him

children.text: pratīpaṃ yānti śaśinaḫ paṅkaje kiraṇā iva // JRt_B.956 //
children.translated_text: Go in the opposite direction, like the rays of the moon upon a lotus [which closes at night]. (JRt B.956)
Already before, as heir-apparent, he was unconquerable and of unbearable daring,
And especially now, honored by <s>Jasratha</s> out of enmity toward the lord of <s>Madra</s>. (JRt B.957)
The new king does not trust us who are shelters of sovereignty;

children.text: hāralubdhasya dāmnas tu hāro na maṇibhṛtphaṇī // JRt_B.958 //
children.translated_text: But the necklace sought by the rope greedy for pearls is not a jewel-bearing serpent-hood. (JRt B.958)

children.text: tasmād asmābhir ete na yuvarājo vijīyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by us he — this heir-apparent — should not be defeated;

children.text: yogyāḫ prāhuṇakenaiva gṛhe ghnanti bhujaṅgamam // JRt_B.959 //
children.translated_text: The capable ones kill a snake in the house only with an appropriate instrument. (JRt B.959)
When the emperor is defeated — not the heir-apparent — let all come

children.text: āyāntu maṇḍalaṃ sarve sādhayāmaś cikīrṣitam" // JRt_B.960 //
children.translated_text: Unchecked to the assembly; we shall accomplish our design.' (JRt B.960)

children.text:
iti sammantrya mantrī sa yuvarājābhiyojane /
sodyamasya narendrasya hetukartṛdaśām agāt // JRt_B.961 //
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, that minister, in the matter of engaging the heir-apparent, became the instigator of the king's effort [against him]. (JRt B.961)
Wherever the fierce <s>Mleccha</s> army went,

children.text: tatra tatra rajovyājāt tamo mūrtam adṛśyata || 738 ||
children.translated_text: There, under the guise of dust, embodied darkness was seen. (JRt 738)
In the territories to be protected, such as <s>Rājapurī</s>, the arrogant one
Wrought the degradation of plunder as if in foreign lands. (JRt 739)
When the king then reached the place called <s>Mudgaravyāla</s>,
The lord of <s>Madra</s>, of no slight vigor, sent [him] a message: (JRt 740)
'Though in your army there are foot-soldiers with all their equipment,

children.text: bhaṭā raṇodbhaṭās santi kaṭake tava yady api || 741 ||
children.translated_text: Horses swift as kings [of beasts], and warriors fierce in battle, (JRt 741)
Still, in the stratagems of deceit well-known on earth,
You are not at all bold in the <s>Khuṅkhura</s> style of warfare. (JRt 742)

children.text: vayam eva tu jānīmaẖ Khuẖkhurāṇāṃ raṇacchalam /
children.translated_text: We alone know the battle-stratagems of the <s>Khuṅkhuras</s>;

children.text: ahir eva bhujaṅgasya padaṃ jānāti netaraḥ || 743 ||
children.translated_text: Only a serpent knows the track of a serpent, not another. (JRt 743)
Therefore, until we arrive for the accomplishment of your military objectives,
You should remain right here, upon the mountain.' (JRt 744)
That message of the lord of <s>Madra</s> was understood by the dull <s>Yavana</s> chiefs,
Whose vision was clouded by pride, as [merely a means] for gaining their own fame. (JRt 745)
When the deluded king descended, as if from a mountain of pride,
The banners fluttering in the wind departed, out of fear of the <s>Khuṅkhura</s> lord's forces. (JRt 746)
The earth, thinning from the trampling of the charging cavalry,
<s>Phaṇīśvara</s> [Śeṣa, the cosmic serpent], was sinking in the confusion of joy and fear. (JRt 747)
On the ground trampled by horses, sprinkled with blood, bristling with swords and spears,
The heroes offered their lives as oblation into the fire of valor in that battle. (JRt 748)

children.text: Āliśāhas tato rājā Sindhau pravahaṇaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Āliśāha</s> [ʿAlī Šāh], like a boat in the <s>Sindhu</s> [river],
Was broken apart in the ocean of battle by the violent winds of misfortune. (JRt 749)
23b) Sulṭān <s>Zayn al-'Ābidīn</s> (LS 4496-4546)

children.text: viśvāndhaṅkaraṇāndhakāranikaragrastasya sūryodayaṃ hemante himamārutair hatadhṛteḫ puṣpākarābhyāgamam /
children.translated_text: For the world engulfed by masses of darkness that blind the universe — a sunrise; for one whose fortitude is destroyed by the cold winds of winter — the arrival of spring;

children.text: duṣṭakṣmāpatitarjitasya jagato nirdoṣaleśaṃ prabhuṃ lokeśo janayan vyanakti nitarāṃ kāruṇyam atyujjvalam || 750 ||
children.translated_text: For the world threatened by wicked kings — a lord without the slightest fault: the Lord of the World, producing such [a king], reveals most brilliantly his supreme compassion. (JRt 750)
Then the illustrious <s>Jainollābhadīna</s> [Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn], free from impurity,
Entered <s>Kaśmīra</s>, propitious as the Creator himself, fortified with victory. (JRt 751)

children.text: satāṃ stutyā diśāṃ bheryā mukhāni dhvanayann ayam /
children.translated_text: Making the faces of the directions resound with the praise of the virtuous and the drums of victory,

children.text: paurāṇāṃ prāṅ manaḫ paścād rājadhānīṃ nṛpo 'viśat || 752 ||
children.translated_text: The king first entered the hearts of the citizens, then the capital. (JRt 752)
Alas! The purity of the people's minds arose from the king's consecration;

children.text: pratāpo vairiṇāṃ śāntas tasmiṃś chatrāṇi bibhrati || 753 ||
children.translated_text: The pride of the enemies was quelled when he bore the royal umbrella. (JRt 753)
His statecraft, surpassing that of former kings, made the subjects eagerly yearn [for him],
And it far exceeded [theirs] in virtues, as sugar exceeds sugarcane juice. (JRt 754)
He renewed the lost institutions of former kings,
As spring [revives] the creepers damaged by winter, so did the king. (JRt 755)
His counsels conquered enemies who were mutually surpassing and unconquerable even by those who defeated others

children.text: śastrair mantrā jitās tasya mantraiś śastrāṇi ca prabhoḥ || 756 ||
children.translated_text: With weapons; and weapons [were conquered] by the counsels of that lord. (JRt 756)

children.text: Kāntyāṅgaṃ vadanaṃ Vācā Śriyoraẖ Kṣamayā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kānti</s> (Beauty) occupied his body, <s>Vāc</s> (Speech) his face, <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) his chest, <s>Kṣamā</s> (Patience) his mind —

children.text: śritaṃ paśyanty agād dūraṃ Kīrtir īrṣyāvaśād iva || 757 ||
children.translated_text: Seeing these sheltered [there], <s>Kīrti</s> (Fame) went far away, as if out of jealousy. (JRt 757)
The king's righteous path of sovereignty, amidst the age of <s>Kali</s>,
Shone like an auspicious interval of the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> [golden age]. (JRt 758)

children.text: bhoge sakhā naye mantrī vivektā śāstranirṇaye /
children.translated_text: A companion in pleasure, a counselor in policy, a discriminator in the determination of <s>śāstra</s>,
Such was <s>Śrī Muhammadakhāna</s>, the brother of the lord of <s>Kaśmīra</s>. (JRt 759)
What else was it but a kingdom — only without the royal umbrella and fly-whisk —
That which <s>Śrī Muhammadakhāna</s> held, by the power of the lord of <s>Kaśmīra</s>? (JRt 760)

children.text: vasanta iva kāmasya vayasyo bhūpater abhūt /
children.translated_text: Like spring is the companion of <s>Kāma</s> [Love], so to the king was
The lord of the <s>Khuṅkharas</s>, the most beloved among his servants. (JRt 761)
While this [king] was thinking that having averted the disorder in this land destroyed by <s>Mlecchas</s>
Was the fruit of attaining sovereignty, (JRt 762)
Meanwhile, the treacherous ones, without even consulting the king,
Openly carried out a treasonous deed with the king's favorites, being fearless. (JRt 763)

children.text: yaśo diśi śriyaṃ sādhau sukhaṃ lokeṣu ropayan /
children.translated_text: Planting fame in the directions, prosperity among the virtuous, and happiness among the people,

children.text: vyadhāt prakramabhaṅgaṃ taṃ yac chatrūn udamūlayat || 764 ||
children.translated_text: He [accomplished] that breach of procedure by which he uprooted the enemies. (JRt 764)

children.text: ekāntā tigmatā bhānor mradimā śaśinaḫ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sun's exclusive fierceness [and] the moon's softness on the other hand —

children.text: sa dvau jetum ivāpuṣyat tatsaṃsargamayīṃ śriyam || 765 ||
children.translated_text: He seemed to nourish a prosperity compounded of both, as if to conquer both. (JRt 765)

children.text: asaṅkhyān atra saṅkṣipte tadguṇān varṇayāmi kim /
children.translated_text: Why should I describe his innumerable virtues in this brief [account]?
How could the lord of elephants dwell in a cave of jackals? (JRt 766)
Therefore, like a mountain-peak on a painting, like the sun's orb in a mirror,
I place the account of his virtues here in the mind, as in the three worlds. (JRt 767)
As at the equinox of hot and cold, or at the equinox of day and night,

children.text: tasya māno 'bhavat tulyas sve pare vāpi darśane || 768 ||
children.translated_text: His regard was equal whether toward his own or toward others. (JRt 768)

children.text: rājā vaṇig ivātyarthaṃ tulāyāḫ puṭayor iva /
children.translated_text: The king, like a merchant, as if in the two pans of a scale,
Would not tolerate in any way a breach of equality in [his] two ways of seeing. (JRt 769)

children.text: śānte siddhāśrame siṃhair mṛgā iva na pīḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the peaceful <s>Siddhāśrama</s>, the deer were not harassed by lions;
So the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, though greatly frightened of the <s>Turuṣkas</s>, were [left undisturbed] as before. (JRt 770)
Those virtuous ones whose existence had been contracted by <s>Sūha</s>, a repository of faults —

children.text: vyakāsayat tato bhāsvān guṇinas tān mahīpatiḥ || 771 ||
children.translated_text: That radiant king then caused them to blossom. (JRt 771)
Learning, which had sunk to a low state through crevices, was raised up by the king
And made to flow again, like a canal [restored], by that virtuous one who delighted in virtues. (JRt 772)
The king, a remover of faults, like a physician gradually [applying] fire [therapy],
Nurtured good conduct in <s>Kaśmīra</s> by [appropriate] measures. (JRt 773)
The king, a conqueror of the disease of ego, for the growth of his subjects,
Purified the excess [impurities] of the elements of [various] philosophies, as of minerals. (JRt 774)
The enforcement of the law of the strong [<s>mātsyanyāya</s>, law of the fish] by the powerful force of time —
This was the mark of his bearing the radiance of the eight world-guardians. (JRt 775)
For the purification of the earth corrupted by the touch of <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>,
He surely kindled the fire of his valor into a great, blazing conflagration. (JRt 776)
As the king gathered the fivefold expanse of counsel,
His enemy faction, as if by [that very] desire for conquest, met its dissolution. (JRt 777)
The praise and glorification of [his] conquest of transient external enemies [was one thing],
But [there was] rather censure of his perpetual destruction of the inner enemies. (JRt 778)
Though capable, the <s>Indra</s> of <s>Kāśyapa</s>'s land campaigned only against those he could [justly] subdue;

children.text: vyomni yātrāṃ karoty arkas satāre na tu soḍupe || 779 ||
children.translated_text: The sun makes its journey through the sky with the stars, but not with the moon. (JRt 779)
That glorious one did not seek to conquer enemies out of greed for their wealth;

children.text: harir māṃsādilobhena hinasti na hi hastinaḥ || 780 ||
children.translated_text: A lion does not kill elephants out of greed for flesh and the like. (JRt 780)
His enemies in the mountains, [exhausted] by the forest-fire-like labors of his sun-like valor,
Surely resorted to the five austerities as if in expiation. (JRt 781)
Though the greatest on earth, he never once proceeded on a wrong path;

children.text: rākendur na niśārambhaṃ vinā jātv apy udeti yat || 782 ||
children.translated_text: For the full moon never rises without the beginning of night. (JRt 782)

children.text: "garvaṃ pravṛddhā vāstavyā hīnā maiva kṣayaṃ gaman" /
children.translated_text: 'Let those who have grown proud remain; let the diminished not go to ruin' —

children.text: iti nītividā rājñā tebhyo balir agṛhyata || 783 ||
children.translated_text: With such statesmanship, the king collected tribute from them. (JRt 783)
Let the fame of the enemy offer itself [as fuel] from separation from his valor;
Into the king's valor, like a forest fire, together with [their] prosperity. (JRt 784)
Once, when <s>Jasratha</s>, persecuted by the lord of <s>Ḍhillī</s> [Delhi], came seeking refuge,
He protected him in mountain caves, as a mountain [protects] darkness from the sun. (JRt 785)
While he ruled the earth, a tamer of the wicked,
A certain land-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [i.e., a farmer] in the vicinity of <s>Jayāpīḍa</s>[-pura], (JRt 786)
Whether from desire for grass-fodder or by the Creator's decree,
His cow wandered away — like the embodied hope of the ancestors. (JRt 787)
Having once gone to the kingdom of <s>Maḍava</s> for pilgrimage bathing,
The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> recognized his own cow by its familiar marks. (JRt 788)

children.text: saniścayo gṛhaṃ yāntīṃ sāyaṃ tām anugamya gām /
children.translated_text: Determined, following the cow going home in the evening,

children.text: vivādam akarod veśmasvāminā saha tatra saḥ || 789 ||
children.translated_text: He there entered into a dispute with the owner of the house. (JRt 789)
Those two, seized by greed and determination, their quarrel unresolved,
Both set out to conduct their dispute before the king's court. (JRt 790)
When neither of them was able to overcome the other's argument,

children.text: śṛṅgāṭāni parīkṣārthaṃ gor agre vyakiran nṛpaḥ || 791 ||
children.translated_text: The king scattered <s>śṛṅgāṭa</s> [water-caltrop] nuts before the cow as a test. (JRt 791)

children.text: sā bālye grasanābhyāsāc chīghram āghrāya saspṛhā /
children.translated_text: That cow, from habitual eating of them in youth, quickly sniffed [the nuts] eagerly

children.text: gaur abhuṅkta phalānīva na tu tatsantatiś ciram || 792 ||
children.translated_text: And ate them as if they were fruits; but her offspring [who had not known them] did not, for a long time. (JRt 792)
While the assembly praised the king's sagacity, the king, with firm conviction,
Collected the fine from the guilty party and [returned] the property from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (JRt 793)
For that one skilled in graciousness, for the sake of the welfare of the people,

children.text: putre mantriṇi mitre vā duṣṭe nālakṣyata kṣamā || 794 ||
children.translated_text: No forbearance was shown toward a son, minister, or friend who was corrupt. (JRt 794)

children.text: aparādhaṃ vinā jāyāṃ kṣībo nighnan priyo 'pi san /
children.translated_text: The <s>Yavana</s> <s>Mereśāya</s>, though a favorite, who while drunk struck his wife without cause,
Was given death by the king. (JRt 795)
That <s>Indra</s> of the earth, casting humiliation upon the enemy faction,
Always showed respect to <s>yogīs</s> who were masters of statecraft. (JRt 796)

children.text: parākramaś ca nītiś ca tasya teṣāṃ ca bhūbhujām /
children.translated_text: The valor and statecraft of those other kings,

children.text: karuṇā ca vivekaś ca yasmin rājani rājati || 797 ||
children.translated_text: The compassion and discernment — all shone in this one king. (JRt 797)
<s>Kāma</s> (Love) always pays homage to the class of those who are separated [from their beloveds];
But he, passionless like <s>Smara</s> [Love, paradoxically], paid homage to the class of <s>yogīs</s>. (JRt 798)

children.text: saumyā bhīmā guṇā yasminn avasan navasaṅgamam /
children.translated_text: In him gentle and terrible qualities dwelt in fresh union;
Where else but in the ocean are poison, nectar, water, and fire seen together? (JRt 799)
The seizure of wealth from plaintiff and defendant by those who should have long been steadfast,
Was prevented by that one of righteous conduct and good character. (JRt 800)
Once before, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Laularāja</s>, for some reason,
Sold one <s>prastha</s> [land unit] out of ten from the royal estates, with written documentation. (JRt 801)
Having raised the young sons of <s>Nonarāja</s> and others, he —
<s>Laularāja</s> — then attained <s>Brahma</s>-hood [died] in the year of the sale. (JRt 802)
Due to the inability of <s>Nonarāja</s>'s [heirs], the remaining nine <s>prasthas</s> [of land] were enjoyed
By the powerful [usurpers], though unsold, through tribute. (JRt 803)

body.text:
evaṃ kṛte daśaprasthabhoge tair balibhiś ciram /
nagabhogāya kapaṭaṃ kṛtaṃ vikrayapattrake /
body.translated_text: When the enjoyment of ten <s>prasthas</s> had thus been [accomplished] by the powerful ones for a long time, a forgery was made in the deed of sale for [the claim to] the town's revenue.

children.translated_text: Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 112
The scribes of old, for the recognition of the vowel form <s>ī</s> standing at the head of a consonant,

children.text: rekhāṃ pūrve vyañjanānāṃ paścādbhāge kilālikhan // JRt_B.1029 //
children.translated_text: Used to draw the stroke after the latter part of the consonant. (JRt B.1029)

children.text: kālāntare liper bhedād upary adyatanāḫ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the course of time, due to the change in script, the modern [scribes] on the other hand —

children.text: vyañjanānāṃ likhanty eva rekhām ekārabodhikām // JRt_B.1030 //
children.translated_text: they write only the stroke indicating the vowel 'e' after consonants. // JRt_B.1030 //
"One <s>bhūprastha</s> (land measure) has been sold" — thus in the deed of sale,
at the position of the stroke indicating 'e' placed after the consonant 'ma', // JRt_B.1031 //
the fraudsters who received the <s>bhūprastha</s> then wrote the consonant 'da',

children.text: makāraṃ te śakāraṃ ca kārayām āsur añjasā // JRt_B.1032 //
children.translated_text: and they also had the 'ma' turned into 'śa' straightaway. // JRt_B.1032 //

children.text: bhūprastham ekaṃ vikrītam iti vikrayapattrake / JRt_B.1033ab /
children.translated_text: "One <s>bhūprastha</s> has been sold" — thus in the deed of sale — // JRt_B.1033ab //

body.translated_text: "Ten <s>prasthas</s> have been sold" — thus they wrote the letters. // 804ef //

children.translated_text: When that king, skilled in adjudication, heard the case — the son of <s>Nonarāja</s>

children.text: balād dhṛtāṃ bhuvaṃ rājasabhāyām aham ākṣipam || 805 ||
children.translated_text: who had seized the land by force — I challenged him in the royal court. || 805 ||
The document brought by the adversaries was then, by the king's command, the king,
skilled in reasoning, having had it read under water, then dismissed it. || 806 ||
When the new letters had vanished while the old ones remained firm,

children.text: bhūprastham ekaṃ vikrītam iti sabhyān avācayat || 807 ||
children.translated_text: "One <s>bhūprastha</s> has been sold" — thus he had the court-members read it. || 807 ||

children.text: rājā kīrtim ahaṃ bhūmiṃ kūṭakṛd daṇḍam adbhutam /
children.translated_text: The king gained fame, I gained land, the forger received an extraordinary punishment,

children.text: prajās sukhaṃ khalā bhītiṃ prāptavantas samaṃ tataḥ || 808 ||
children.translated_text: the people gained happiness, and the wicked gained fear — all at once. || 808 ||

children.text: indo Rāhubhayaṃ kadāpi kurute kālaẖ kalāḫ pūrayan siñcan sañcinute taḍinnipatanakṣobhaṃ taror vāridaḥ /
children.translated_text: The moon sometimes creates fear of <s>Rāhu</s> even as it fills its digits; the rain-cloud, while watering and nourishing, causes the terror of lightning falling upon the tree;

children.text: Vedhās satpuruṣasya sarvajagatām āhlādanāyodyamaṃ kurvann āmayadarśanena kurute bhītiprakarṣaṃ kṣaṇam || 809 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, striving for the delight of all beings through a virtuous person, momentarily creates the height of fear through the sight of disease. || 809 ||
A terrible poisonous boil once severely afflicted

children.text: prakoṣṭhaṃ bhūmipālasya prajānāṃ hṛdayaṃ ca saḥ || 810 ||
children.translated_text: the forearm of the king and the hearts of the people. || 810 ||
As with flowers in the month of <s>Māgha</s> (winter), due to the affliction of the <s>Mleccha</s> frost,

children.text: na lābho viṣavaidyāṇāṃ deśe 'sminn abhavat tadā || 811 ||
children.translated_text: no poison-doctors could be found in this land at that time. || 811 ||
<s>Śivabhaṭṭa</s>, a sacrificer and knower of the <s>Gāruḍa-śāstra</s> (science of anti-venoms), was found by the king's attendants
searching for him — like a well found by travelers in a desert. || 812 ||
Though skilled in healing, he hesitated out of fear of the <s>Mlecchas</s>—

children.text: sphuliṅgadagdhaḫ puruṣas spṛśaty api maṇiṃ cirāt || 813 ||
children.translated_text: a man burned by a spark touches even a gem only after a long time. || 813 ||

children.text: svayaṃ dattābhayo rājñā prāptas tam udamūlayat /
children.translated_text: Given assurance of safety by the king himself, <s>Śivabhaṭṭa</s> came and uprooted
the poisonous boil, as an elephant uproots a poisonous tree. || 814 ||

children.text: tasya kīrtis sukhaṃ rājñaḫ prajānāṃ harṣasantatiḥ /
children.translated_text: His fame, the king's comfort, and a succession of joy for the people—
these three things sprouted when that single boil was lanced. || 815 ||

children.text: tuṣṭena bhūbhujā dattāṃ yatheṣṭam api sampadam /
children.translated_text: The wealth given at will by the pleased king
<s>Śivabhaṭṭa</s> did not desire — like a self-controlled ascetic does not desire a beautiful woman. || 816 ||
Ps-JRT 113

children.text: uddāhapātakavaśād iva nirghṛṇas san dagdhvā tṛṇaṃ tṛṇakṛśānur upaiti śāntim /
children.translated_text: As if compelled by the sin of conflagration, the merciless grass-fire, having burned the grass, subsides;

children.text: jātāmbuvāhakaruṇāpraṇayāt tṛṇasya kāntiḫ punaś śataguṇā masṛṇābhirāmā // JRt_B.1046 //
children.translated_text: then, through the compassion and love of the rain-cloud born for the grass, its beauty returns a hundredfold, smooth and delightful. // JRt_B.1046 //
As rain-clouds are dried up by intense <s>Āṣāḍha</s> (summer) heat,

children.text: Sūhabhaṭṭena saṃśuṣya parābhūtā yayur diśaḥ // JRt_B.1047 //
children.translated_text: so by <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>, the scholars were dried up and driven to the quarters, defeated. // JRt_B.1047 //
Like the autumn wind after the rains, the king, eager for the confidence of their learning,

children.text: ānāyayat sa tān sarvān paṇḍitān nijamaṇḍalam // JRt_B.1048 //
children.translated_text: summoned all those scholars to his own court. // JRt_B.1048 //
In this country resembling a pearl necklace, the leader placed the jewels of scholars

children.text: kāntyā vā sudhiyā tatra yathāyogaṃ nyavīviśat // JRt_B.1049 //
children.translated_text: each in their proper position, according to their brilliance or wisdom. // JRt_B.1049 //
The king nourished the scholars who had been established, through the gift of honor and stipends,
as a gardener nourishes trees with water. // JRt_B.1050 //
Whatever had been destroyed by <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s> in the domain of <s>Kaśmīra</s>,
was restored by <s>Śiryabhaṭṭa</s> at the king's request. // JRt_B.1051 //
<s>Bhaṭṭa Śiryaka</s>, having reinstituted sacrifices, pilgrimages, and other rites for the <s>Nāgas</s>,
caused the land seized by the <s>Turuṣkas</s> (Turks) to be restored to the learned. // JRt_B.1052 //
When the unbroken prosperity of the <s>Hindus</s> was restored by him,
all the <s>Yavana</s> demons became enraged at <s>Śiryabhaṭṭa</s>. // JRt_B.1053 //
At the breaking of the waters of the great serpent-king <s>Mahāpadma</s>, he, bound by a water-pot,

children.text: baddho 'pi dṛtivat sthitvā Yavanendrān vyalakṣayat // JRt_B.1054 //
children.translated_text: standing firm like a leather bag, confounded the <s>Yavana</s> lords. // JRt_B.1054 //

children.text: tāpo yasyāhni śailāñ jvalayati sa ravis sāyam akṣṇāpi gamyaḥ svagrāvṇaś śuṣyato 'hni dravayati na śaśī pūrakas sāyam abdheḥ /
children.translated_text: The sun, whose heat in daytime sets mountains ablaze, is visible even to the eye at evening; the moon, which dries its own rocks by day, does not melt them, yet fills the ocean at evening;

children.text: kāruṇyād eva loke nijamatisakalaṃ svecchayā darśayitvā taṃ tadbhāgyāvasānāt prathamam atha mahāṃs tūrṇam antardadhāti // JRt_B.1055 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, through compassion alone, showing his complete wisdom to the world at will, then suddenly conceals it first, at the end of their fortune. // JRt_B.1055 //
In the <s>Kali</s> age, the goddess <s>Śāradā</s>, distressed by the touch and sight of sinful men,

children.text: avaśyaṃ Śāradā devī tadāntardhānam āśrayat // JRt_B.1056 //
children.translated_text: inevitably resorted to disappearance. // JRt_B.1056 //

children.text: mukhe svedo bhuje kampaḫ pādasparśe vidāhitā /
children.translated_text: Sweat on her face, trembling in her arms, burning at the touch of feet—

children.text: jātu jātv abhavad devyā no tadā hi tathā kvacit // JRt_B.1057 //
children.translated_text: the goddess had occasionally experienced these, but never before as at that time. // JRt_B.1057 //
She does not bestow her grace upon the people of <s>Kaśmīra</s> who, by royal favor,

children.text: Kaśmīraloke sā devī nānugrahaparā hy abhūt // JRt_B.1058 //
children.translated_text: dedicate a portion of wealth obtained through treachery. // JRt_B.1058 //
The deities are pleased even with mere <s>dūrvā</s> grass, if it is pure;

children.text: prāṇair api na mālinyadūṣitair jātucit punaḥ // JRt_B.1059 //
children.translated_text: but never at all with offerings defiled by impurity, even if they be one's very life. // JRt_B.1059 //

children.text: Kalikāle tu devyās sa prabhāvo 'pi śamaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kali</s> age, even the power of the goddess had subsided;

children.text: jātv ity agān nṛpo devīṃ draṣṭuṃ tadyātrikais saha // JRt_B.1060 //
children.translated_text: and so the king went to see the goddess, accompanied by her pilgrims. // JRt_B.1060 //
Making the river <s>Madhumatī</s> fruitful through bathing and drinking,
he arrived at the <s>Śāradā</s> temple, crowded with a distressed assembly. // JRt_B.1061 //
Eager to grant fearlessness to the devotees of the goddess, and resolved to reveal her power,

children.text: yuktāyuktavivektā sa tatra rājā nyavikṣata // JRt_B.1062 //
children.translated_text: that king, a discerner of the fitting and unfitting, placed his trust there. // JRt_B.1062 //
There too, the king, astonished by the sight of their wickedness,

children.text: bhaktihrāsam agād devyāṃ yātrikeṣu ca kopitām // JRt_B.1063 //
children.translated_text: experienced a diminution of devotion toward the goddess, and became angered at the pilgrims. // JRt_B.1063 //
"O Goddess, the direct vision of you is rare even for the gods;
we, tainted by the <s>Kali</s> age, should not request it. // JRt_B.1064 //
For those unable to meditate upon or worship your formless essence,

children.text: bhaktibhājām anukrośād yat tu rūpaṃ tvam agrahīḥ // JRt_B.1065 //
children.translated_text: out of compassion for the devoted, you assumed a form. // JRt_B.1065 //

children.text: tavāsyāṃ pratimāyāṃ ced vyapeto naiva sannidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: If your presence has not departed from this image of yours,

children.text: pavitrayatarām adya svapne tad darśanena mām // JRt_B.1066 //
children.translated_text: then purify me today more fully by granting me your vision in a dream. // JRt_B.1066 //

children.text: asmābhiś ca tatas sā tvaṃ yathāśakti niṣevyase /
children.translated_text: And by us, therefore, you are worshipped to the best of our ability;

children.text: mithyābhaktadurātmatvāt tvaṃ ced dūram ito gatā // JRt_B.1067 //
children.translated_text: but if you have gone far from here due to the wickedness of false devotees, // JRt_B.1067 //
then why is the image condemned by the enemies of the <s>Hindus</s>?" —

children.text: vijñapyeti sa saptamyāṃ bhādre rājā jitendriyaḥ // JRt_B.1068 //
children.translated_text: having thus petitioned, on the seventh day of <s>Bhādra</s>, the king, master of his senses, // JRt_B.1068 //
slept upon the platform of the temple of the <s>Śāradā</s> precinct;

children.text: darśitaṃ na yadā svapne kiñcit sannidhisūcakam // JRt_B.1069 //
children.translated_text: but nothing indicative of her presence was shown to him in a dream. // JRt_B.1069 //

children.text: rājñāṣṭānavatau varṣe svāṃ mūrtiṃ devy acūrṇayat /
children.translated_text: In the ninety-eighth year, the king pulverized the goddess's own image;
the goddess did not grant him her vision, surely because of his association with <s>Mlecchas</s>;

children.text: svāmī bhṛtyāparādhena garhaṇīya iti sthitiḥ // JRt_B.1070 //
children.translated_text: the principle stands that a master is blameworthy for the transgressions of his servants. // JRt_B.1070 //
There was nothing in him that would obstruct the vision of the goddess;

children.text: dayā satyaṃ vivekaś ca tam evāśrayate tadā // JRt_B.1071 //
children.translated_text: compassion, truth, and discernment all resided in him at that time. // JRt_B.1071 //

children.text: vyāvṛtya Yavanānāṃ sa vanānām iva vāridaḥ /
children.translated_text: Turning away the <s>Yavanas</s>, like a rain-cloud turning away from forests,
he, overcome with the exaltation of joy, caused a great shower of gold. // JRt_B.1072 //

children.text: yatra daṇḍyā na daṇḍyante durbalās taskaraṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: Where the guilty were not punished, and the weak were not [punished] except for thieves—

children.text: bhūpateḫ prāḍvivākatvaṃ sa prāpad bhaṭṭaŚiryakaḥ // JRt_B.1073 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṭṭa Śiryaka</s> attained the position of chief justice of the king. // JRt_B.1073 //
Pledging, when there was no supply of treasury wealth,

children.text: svagalacchedanaṃ bhaṭṭo mithyāvaktuś ca viplavam // JRt_B.1074 //
children.translated_text: the cutting of his own throat, and the destruction of anyone who spoke falsely— // JRt_B.1074 //
with the sound produced from the breaking of branches filling all four directions,

children.text: samudīrayatāṃ nūnam abrāhmaṇyaṃ pade pade // JRt_B.1075 //
children.translated_text: surely producing un-Brahmanical conduct at every step— // JRt_B.1075 //

children.text:
drumāṇāṃ phalanamrāṇāṃ janānāṃ namatāṃ guṇaiḥ /
chedād rakṣām akārṣīt sa jiṣṇur indhanahetunā // JRt_B.1076 //
children.translated_text: he, victorious, protected the fruit-laden trees and the people bowing with virtues from being cut down, for the purpose of fuel. // JRt_B.1076 //
— — — — — — — — having averted the triple punishment,
he established a silver coin for the protection of the caste of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 817 ||
Ps-JRT 115
When people in the districts were killing cows with poison out of greed for meat,
he prevented the cooking-pots of cow-flesh by prohibiting their seizure and other means. // JRt_B.1079 //
The disorder caused by the husband's kinsmen against a <s>Śūdra</s> woman who went to another man after her husband died—

children.text: sa mahāmatimāñ śūdryā viplavaṃ vinyavārayat // JRt_B.1080 //
children.translated_text: that great-minded one prevented. // JRt_B.1080 //
He prevented the disorder in funeral rites for daughters,

children.text: aputrasya vipannasya lubdhais tadgotrajaiẖ kṛtam // JRt_B.1081 //
children.translated_text: committed by the greedy kinsmen of a man who died without sons. // JRt_B.1081 //
The study of scriptures by children, which had been destroyed by <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>,

children.text: vṛttidānena viduṣāṃ vidyāvān ānayat punaḥ // JRt_B.1082 //
children.translated_text: the learned king restored by giving stipends to scholars. // JRt_B.1082 //
Wishing to establish his own recognition upon <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> bodies, the king
created a distinction between truth and <s>dharma</s> under the guise of a <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark). // JRt_B.1083 //
In the first year of the villages, the tax transferred by those afflicted by officials
to the <s>pattalāghoṣa</s> territories — he abolished the bathing-tax. // JRt_B.1084 //
Having abolished the long-established fraud in cart-scales and measures,
he caused the establishment of standard prices for goods. // JRt_B.1085 //
For goods arriving from outside the country, taking into account place, time, and other factors,
having fixed the price and the gate-duty, he cut off the day-theft (daily extortion). // JRt_B.1086 //
The clever <s>Śiryabhaṭṭa</s> too did not accept the fruit of bribes,
but rather the imperishable fruit of <s>dharma</s>, through benefit brought by the rains (of justice). // JRt_B.1087 //
For supplicants embodied, desiring the relish of knowledge and wisdom,

children.text: tadecchāsiddhir abhavad rājñaḫ puṇyaphalād drutam // JRt_B.1088 //
children.translated_text: the fulfillment of their desires came quickly, through the fruit of the king's merit. // JRt_B.1088 //
From the mouth of the great and illustrious <s>Śiryabhaṭṭa</s>, the king, the lord,
promulgated the royal decree named <s>Dharmaprakāśana</s> (Illumination of Dharma). // JRt_B.1089 //
He widely prevented, stamped with the seal of determination,
the bolt on the path of misgovernance by future kings. // JRt_B.1090 //

children.text: asthāpayat sa dharmasthas sadvṛttaṃ pratipattanam / JRt_B.1091ab /
children.translated_text: Established in <s>dharma</s>, he set up good conduct as a port of arrival. // JRt_B.1091ab //
Having established village boundaries and obtained wealth from the villages,
by that king, travelers in the wilderness were protected from lawless brigands. || 818 ||
The laughter of the cremation-ground goddesses, as if directed at <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>—
the resting places and aerial chariots of the ghosts then ceased to shine. || 819 ||
The king, of undiminished compassion, gradually rescued the earth

children.text: udahārṣīt kramād evaṃ Dānavair iva Keśavaḥ || 820 ||
children.translated_text: afflicted by the <s>Mlecchas</s>, just as <s>Keśava</s> (Viṣṇu) rescued it from the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons). || 820 ||

children.text: ucchṛṅgān sa nayan bhaṅgaṃ nimnān āpūrayan nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Bringing down the arrogant peaks and filling up the valleys, the king
made the earth smooth and even, for the sowing of the seeds of his own fame. || 821 ||
The king's vow regarding others' wives was one of complete disinterest,
though he was supreme in the embrace of another's <s>Śrī</s> (sovereignty). || 822 ||
By that all-knowing king, endowed with the strength of the tenfold virtues,
the Buddhist <s>Tilakācārya</s> was placed in the highest position. || 823 ||
<s>Śivabhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Tilaka</s>, and <s>Siṃhagaṇanāpati</s>—

children.text: sopanāny abhavaṃs te ca padārohe dvijanmanām || 824 ||
children.translated_text: they became the steps for the ascent of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 824 ||
The <s>Indra</s> of the earth possessed, like a cuckoo with the beauty of melody,
unbroken expertise in aesthetics through the service of the <s>brahmakuṇḍala</s> (divine earring). || 825 ||
The illustrious <s>Karpūrabhaṭṭa</s>, protector of beings for the king,

children.text: guṇināṃ śaraṇaṃ cakre svaguṇais surabhiṃ sabhām || 826 ||
children.translated_text: a refuge of the virtuous, made the court fragrant with his own virtues. || 826 ||
From the movements of the planets in the previous year, the planetary positions of the coming year—
<s>Ruyyabhaṭṭa</s> knew these without any computational effort. || 827 ||
At the moment of the commentary and explanation of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> by the revered feet of <s>Rāmānanda</s>,
<s>Śāradā</s> (Sarasvatī) gazes upon the earth itself with an agitated mind. || 828 ||
The kings of <s>Gāndhāra</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, <s>Madra</s>, and other lands, of that king,
became like villagers, obedient to his commands, their enemies conquered.

children.text: yuddhe jitaṃ tato baddhaṃ Khuẖkhurendreṇa bhūpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having been defeated and captured in battle, the king, by the command of <s>Khuṅkhurendra</s>,
released <s>Māladeva</s>, the <s>Madra</s> king.
in a moment, by a mere frown, toppled <s>Raṇasūha</s>, the king of <s>Rājapurī</s>.

body.translated_text: The king, versed in statecraft, with his own foot-soldiers,

children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Udabhāṇḍapura</s>, strengthened by the <s>Sindhu</s> king,

children.text: sa kandukam ivotthāpya muhur muhur apātayat || 832 ||
children.translated_text: he lifted up and cast down repeatedly, like a ball.
In the <s>Bhoṭṭa</s> (Tibetan) land, once, in the <s>Gogga</s> region, by the great king,

children.text: bāṇā Gaurakharāsreṇa guṇair lokāś ca rañjitāḥ || 833 ||
children.translated_text: arrows colored the <s>Gaurakharā</s> stream, and his virtues colored the people.
When the <s>Śaya</s> country was ablaze, the king, fierce in his commands,
protected a golden <s>Buddha</s> image from the <s>Yavanas</s>.
Testing the brilliance of the <s>Bhauṭṭas</s> on the touchstone, which was bitter in its abrasion,
his valor then made the city of <s>Malūta</s> lose its luster.

children.text: kevalaṃ hṛdayaṃ śūnyaṃ Bhauṭṭānāṃ nābhavat tadā /
children.translated_text: Not only the hearts of the <s>Bhauṭṭas</s> were empty then,
but also their long-accumulated treasury, due to being possessed by fear of the king.
The king, giving the subjects their appropriate remaining nourishment,

children.text: pratyavekṣām akārṣīt sa śālinām iva kārṣakaḥ || 837 ||
children.translated_text: looked after them, like a farmer tending rice plants.
His bow could not bear comparison with the bows of <s>Śārṅga</s> (Viṣṇu's) and <s>Pināka</s> (Śiva's);
but his eyebrows, intoxicated like a bow, accomplished far-reaching purposes.

children.text: astaṃ yas tamasāṃ kulāni balato netuṃ sadā vāñchati kṣīṇaṃ taṃ vasunābhipūrya śaśinaṃ saṃvardhayaty añjasā /
children.translated_text: He who always desires to forcibly drive the clans of darkness to their destruction, who easily nourishes the waning moon by filling it with wealth —

children.text: Kāśyapyām avakāśamātraghaṭanāṃ śākhāmukhai rundhato vṛkṣān vṛṣṭibharaiś ca yo 'sya katamo bhānos tulām arhati || 839 ||
children.translated_text: he who blocks the trees that obstruct the openings of branches in the <s>Kāśyapī</s> (Kashmir) with torrents of rain — which sun is worthy of comparison with this one?
The king nurtured <s>Nosrata</s>, the son of <s>Laddarāja</s>;
but when his wealth was unrepaid, he banished him saying "he is a traitor."
Once, a <s>Yavana</s> named <s>Sadaulā</s>, having come from the <s>Makka</s> (Mecca) region,
bearing the ostentation of books, approached that king of kings.
The king, being fond of men of qualities, visited that man who boasted of his qualities
daily, coming to see him, like any other visitor.

children.text: sa tasya paṭahasyeva rājāpaśyat kramād asau /
children.translated_text: Like a drum, the discerning king gradually perceived
that man's hollowness within, upon examination.
Even though the <s>Mleccha</s> mendicant was devoid of qualities, the lord of the earth's life-breath
did not release his love for him, like a father, being an ocean of compassion.
Like the multitude of darkness at twilight, like the multitude of lightning in a dense cloud,
the multitude of his faults agitated the subjects.
At that time, a certain king of <s>yogins</s>, his senses conquered,
was seen on a tall pillar, for the perfection of his <s>yoga</s> practice.
As the king watched him for nine days without food atop the pillar,
by his very blessing, the king's queen gave birth to a son.

children.text: tapasyatas tathā tasya tatra tan navamaṃ dinam /
children.translated_text: As that <s>yogin</s> was performing austerities there, that ninth day
became for the king an unsurpassed day — a great festival of the birth of a son.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 116

children.text: hemantānte patati tuhinaṃ phālguṇe valgu valgad dīpasyāpi sphurati sutarāṃ śāntikāle 'tidāhaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the end of winter, snow falls beautifully in <s>Phālguna</s>; even a lamp flares up excessively at the moment of its extinction;

children.text: śaityodreko vahati vahati grīṣmakāle tuṣāraṃ vastu prāyaḫ prathayati nijaṃ dharmam āyāti nāśe // JRt_B.1122 //
children.translated_text: extreme cold comes and brings frost in the summer season — a thing mostly manifests its own nature when approaching destruction.

children.text: tapaẖkavacam aspṛṣṭvā tam adho mārgaṇair gatam /
children.translated_text: Without touching the armor of austerity, having gone below with arrows,

children.text: prahartur iva nirdeṣṭuṃ bhaviṣyantīṃ tathā gatim // JRt_B.1123 //
children.translated_text: as if to indicate the future fate of the striker,
seeing him honored by the king and becoming angry, the calm-minded ascetic

children.text: nirṇayād acalad varṇī nayān na tu bhayodayāt // JRt_B.1124 //
children.translated_text: departed from his resolve due to policy, not from the arising of fear.

children.text: sa stambhān na mahādhairyād avārohan mahāmanāḥ /
children.translated_text: He did not descend from the pillar out of great fortitude, the great-souled one;

children.text: naivārohaj jagaddṛṣṭiṃ sadyo dyām api yogavit // JRt_B.1125 //
children.translated_text: nor, being a knower of <s>yoga</s>, did he ascend to the sight of the world — rather to heaven itself, instantly.

children.text:
"atithiṃ yogapathikaṃ mā vadhīr mām" iti bruvan /
Mlecchamaskariṇā varṇī khaḍgaghātair acūrṇyata // JRt_B.1126 //
children.translated_text: "Do not kill me, a guest, a wayfarer on the path of <s>yoga</s>" — saying thus, the ascetic was pulverized by sword-blows from the <s>Mleccha</s> mendicant.
Out of extreme hatred for seeing him, intoxicated and deluded by liquor,

children.text: sa Mlecchasahito yogirājaṃ tam avadhīc charaiḥ || 849 ||
children.translated_text: he, together with the <s>Mleccha</s>, killed that king of <s>yogins</s> with arrows.
With heated, soiled, and coarse drops of tears from the people upon witnessing that,

children.text: bhūtale patitaṃ vāṣpair apavādaiś ca rājani || 850 ||
children.translated_text: and with reproaches, they fell upon the king on the ground.

children.text: pṛthvīnātho 'tha tac chrutvā śuddhyartham iva magnavān /
children.translated_text: The lord of the earth, hearing that, plunged as if for purification
into the oceans of fear, shame, grief, anger, wonder, duty, and anxiety.
Even though a first-born son had arrived on that very day, the king
did not bathe, did not eat, did not transact business, and did not speak.
The next day, the king, having consulted experts learned in <s>Smṛti</s> law,
hearing that the punishment for the killer was death, was restrained by compassion.
Mounting him backwards on a donkey, making him parade through the marketplace,
shaving his beard after anointing it with human urine,
spitting by all the people, binding his arms with entrails of the dead,
a living death — such was the punishment he decreed for that emaciated wretch.
Upon the king, free from dejection, carrying the fragrance of the directions,
celestial flowers and the citizens' blessings fell.
From the daughter of the <s>Madra</s> king, that king begot four sons,

children.text: yathā Daśaratho rājā janakān tān ajījanat || 857 ||
children.translated_text: just as King <s>Daśaratha</s> begot those who were progenitors.

children.text: jyāyān Ādhamakhānas sa Hājyakhānas tathā paraḥ /
children.translated_text: The eldest was <s>Ādhamakhāna</s>, then <s>Hājyakhāna</s>,

children.text: Khāno Jassarathaẖ Khāno Baharāmaś ca sañjñitaḥ || 858 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khāna Jassaratha</s>, and the one named <s>Khāna Baharāma</s>.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 117

children.text: Hindavas Sūhabhaṭṭena balād ye pīḍitā bhṛśam /
children.translated_text: The Hindus who were forcibly oppressed by <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>

children.text: paradeśaṃ gatās te tu bibhrato veṣakalpanām // JRt_B.1137 //
children.translated_text: had gone to foreign lands, maintaining a disguised appearance.
Always devoted to their own practices, hostile to those practices in their hearts,

children.text: svam ācāram anuṣṭhātuṃ preritāś ca dvijair balāt // JRt_B.1138 //
children.translated_text: they were urged forcibly by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> to follow their own rites.

children.text:
dāritās svatrāṇabhayād utkocārpaṇatatparāḥ /
rakṣitā bhūmipālena tadupadravavāraṇāt // JRt_B.1139 //
children.translated_text: Torn by fear for their own safety, eager to offer bribes, they were protected by the king from the prevention of that harassment.

children.text: Kṣīrārṇavasya mathanāt paratas sudhādiratnāni tāny anupabhoganirarthakāni /
children.translated_text: After the churning of the <s>Kṣīrārṇava</s> (Milk Ocean), those gems like nectar were useless without being enjoyed —

children.text: yo nītavān saphalatāṃ kila pātradānāt stutyas sa Mandaragirir girirājavarge || 859 ||
children.translated_text: he who brought them to fruitfulness through gifts to worthy recipients — that Mount <s>Mandara</s> is praiseworthy among the class of mountain-kings.
Joining rivers and wells with the earth's water, rendering the fruitless fruitful,
he generated wonderful fame through their combination.
Having brought a canal to the embanked land of <s>Utpalapura</s> for the king,
the flaw of their uselessness was thereby removed.
The king, having brought down a canal to the desert of <s>Nandaśaila</s>,
reminded one of <s>Cakradhara</s> (Viṣṇu), the dweller within the ocean.

children.text: karālambas satāṃ bibhrad akarālaṃ sitaṃ yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Extending a hand to the virtuous, bearing unfierce, white fame,
he made the land called <s>Karāla</s> cultivated through a canal — a worthy object of praise.

children.text: sāgrahārā dvijā yatra sāgrahārāś ca yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> had <s>agrahāras</s> (endowments) and women too had <s>agrahāras</s>,
there the king built a city named <s>Jainapurī</s> in <s>Karāla</s>.
And in the land of <s>Avantipura</s>, by the king with delightful effort,
a canal was brought down, incomparable, rich with the prosperity of rice.
When the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> was brought to <s>Mānasa</s> (lake) by a mountain path,

children.text: kiṃ pūtaṃ Mānasenedam amunā kim u Mānasam || 866 ||
children.translated_text: was it <s>Mānasa</s> that was purified by this, or was this purified by <s>Mānasa</s>?
That city which had mocked its own reflection mirrored in <s>Mānasa</s>,
by building it upon its bank, he brought it to fruition.
Pseudo-Jonarāja, verse 118

children.text: śrīSvayasya yam ānetuṃ prajñā na sphuṭam asphurat /
children.translated_text: That which the wisdom of <s>Śrī Svaya</s> could not clearly devise to bring,
even <s>Śrī Sekandara Śāha</s> became most anxiously eager for.
The illustrious <s>Jainollābhadena</s>, having brought the <s>Pahara</s> river,

children.text: prāsiñcad viṃśatikrośāñ chrīmān Svayapure marum // JRt_B.1150 //
children.translated_text: irrigated the desert of <s>Svayapura</s> for twenty <s>krośas</s> (leagues).

children.text:
durbhikṣavyāptacittānāṃ viśrāntijananān nṛṇām /
Viśrāntisañjñayā kulyā prasiddhābhūt pade pade // JRt_B.1151 //
children.translated_text: That canal, generating rest for people whose minds were consumed by famine, became famous at every step by the name <s>Viśrānti</s> (Rest).
The illustrious king, joining the <s>Pahara</s> with the <s>Vitastā</s> beyond <s>Suyyapura</s>,
on the earth, thereby averted the calamity of suffering.
From the slope of Mount <s>Pradyumna</s> to the limit of <s>Amareśapura</s>,
he built the city of <s>Jaina</s>, rich with monasteries, endowments, and markets.
As if rising to conquer heaven, with lofty stone mansions,
having transferred to the <s>Jaina Gaṅgā</s>, the prosperity of the serpent-world came.
The accomplished one, of smiling fame, having brought the <s>Jaina Gaṅgā</s> to the temple of <s>Raṇasvāmin</s>,
surpassed the wonder of <s>Haripāda</s>.
Beyond <s>Suyyapura</s>, he built a city named <s>Jainagiri</s>,
adorned with palaces, rivaling Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>.
At the holy field of <s>Sureśvarī</s>, he of radiant fame, having subdued his enemies,
established his capital, the city of <s>Siddhipurī</s>.
On the summits of palaces, the king established <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s> and <s>Amaranātha</s>
as royal capitals, with mansions whitening the distant sky.
Abundance was reportedly first sprouted by <s>Suyyarāja</s>,

children.text: tataḫ prabhṛty atīteṣu bahuṣv api ca rājasu || 875 ||
children.translated_text: and from that time onward, even though many kings had passed,
due to the meager merit of the people, it did not increase even slightly;
but through the power of austerity, it put forth leaves, flowers, and fruit.
By the illustrious <s>Jainollābhadīna</s>, all that was simultaneously accomplished;

children.text: tapasām atiśuddhatvāt kim iva jñāpakaṃ param || 877 ||
children.translated_text: what greater proof is there of the supreme purity of his austerities?
Other kings fall from sovereignty upon the exhaustion of their prior merit;

children.text: tasya janmāntare rājyaprāptyai rājyam abhūt prabhoḥ || 878 ||
children.translated_text: for this lord, sovereignty was for the attainment of sovereignty in the next life.
He, making the lands that were river-fed also god-fed,

children.text: agrahārān anu kṣmāpo dvijebhyo yad adāt sadā || 879 ||
children.translated_text: the king always gave <s>agrahāras</s> (endowments) to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in accordance with the grants.
At <s>Varāhakṣetra</s>, <s>Nagaravijayeśāna</s>, and other places,
he himself gave <s>agrahāras</s> with monasteries to the <s>Yavanas</s> as well.
At <s>Vijayakṣetra</s>, <s>Vārāhakṣetra</s>, <s>Śūrapura</s>, and other places,

body.text: sattradānena sa trāsam api Gotrabhido vyadhāt || 881 ||
body.translated_text: through the gift of <s>sattras</s> (feeding-houses), he inspired awe even in <s>Gotrabhid</s> (Indra).

children.translated_text: Land-sale documents on birch-bark marked by the king
were made as a court of <s>dharma</s> to prevent future denial.
The mountain that was the copper mine, obtained by King <s>Jayāpīḍadeva</s> through the grace of the <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: sa daṇḍam iva tasyādāt tāmraṃ tāmrākaro giriḥ || 883 ||
children.translated_text: yielded copper to him as if paying a tribute.

children.text: maṇīn khanibhyaś cālabhyāṃs tadrājye bhūr ajījanat /
children.translated_text: The earth produced gems from mines — previously unobtainable — during his reign,
which became famous as <s>Jaina</s> gems, surpassing the pride of rubies.
Gold found in the sands of rivers, destroying the pride of transported sand,

children.text: kāñcanaṃ kāñcana cchāyāṃ bibhral lokair acīyata || 885 ||
children.translated_text: bearing a golden hue, was then collected by the people.
"One-sixth of river-gold is to be taken by future rulers" —
such a request the king inscribed on a copper plate.
<s>Kācaḍāmara</s>, the city superintendent, on a difficult road,
built a bridge of stone, one <s>krośa</s> (league) in length, within the city.
Not he himself alone was lifted from the mud by that bridge-gift,
but all the people too — in the middle of the city — by that meritorious one.

children.text: viṣaye viṣaye cakre Śiryabhaṭṭo maṭhān pṛthūn /
children.translated_text: <s>Śiryabhaṭṭa</s> built large monasteries in each district,

children.text: anye 'pi sacivā rājño dharmaśālā bahūr vyadhuḥ || 889 ||
children.translated_text: and other ministers of the king also built many <s>dharmaśālās</s> (rest-houses).

children.text: padmākarasya mathanāya gajādhirājāv abhyudyatau satatam eva tadambudṛptau /
children.translated_text: Two king-elephants, constantly ready for the churning of the lotus-lake, proud of its waters — those two, fighting each other here with excessive intoxication out of delight, in a moment brought about their own destruction.

children.text: tāvat karākari rasād iha cātimattau kṛtvā kṣaṇād agamatāṃ svayam eva nāśam || 890 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Masoda</s> and <s>Śūra</s>, foster-brothers of the king, of the same clan,
The two remained, each seeking the other's weakness, unable to bear the other's prosperity.
Though their anger was restrained by the king, who was endowed with affection and courtesy,
having killed one of them, the two remained poised for sedition for a long time.

children.text: kadācid bhūpater agre spṛṣṭaś Śūreṇa vākcharaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Once, in the king's presence, <s>Masoda Ṭhakkura</s>, struck by the word-arrows of <s>Śūra</s>,
made him renounce his weapons.
Having laid down his weapons, going at night with scant provisions,

children.text: randhraṃ labdhvātha Śūreṇa Masodaṣ Ṭhakkuro hataḥ || 894 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Masoda Ṭhakkura</s>, having found an opening, was then killed by <s>Śūra</s>.
By <s>Vinna</s> and other <s>Ṭhakkuras</s>, his brothers of renowned valor,
<s>Śūra</s> was requested to be slain, [they being servants] of the king who was endowed with affection.
When <s>Śūra</s> along with his followers was killed by <s>Vinna Ṭhakkura</s>,

children.text: prasādam agamat kīrtiṣ Ṭhakkurāṇāṃ ca dhīs tadā || 896 ||
children.translated_text: the fame and the intellect of the <s>Ṭhakkuras</s> then attained clarity.

children.text: tathā sa yogināṃ mānam adād bhūlokaVāsavaḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) of the mortal world gave such honor to the <s>yogins</s>

children.text: teṣām agre yathā Madrarājādyair laḍitaṃ śvavat || 897 ||
children.translated_text: that before them, kings like the <s>Madra</s> king and others were treated like dogs.

children.text: sa dadad yogināṃ bhogaṃ yāgaṃ tebhyo 'grahīn nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: That king, while giving enjoyment to the <s>yogins</s>, took away their sacrifices from them;

children.text: bhayaṃ dadad arātibhyo dadhāv abhayam apy aho || 898 ||
children.translated_text: giving fear to enemies, he also gave fearlessness—how wondrous!
The king, while prohibiting the <s>yogins</s>' seals, begging bowls, necklaces, and such,

body.translated_text: gave them earrings, golden vessels, and fine silk.

children.text: chittvā parvatapakṣatīr api navāḫ pheṇena hatvāpy ahiṃ kṛtvā yajñaśataṃ trilokavijayī kīrtyā na tṛptiṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having clipped the wings of mountains, having killed serpents with foam, having performed a hundred sacrifices, the conqueror of the three worlds was not satisfied with fame— <s>Indra</s> displays his bow of white, black, red, and green colors upon a mere combination of smoke, wind, and water-clouds, even when they are insubstantial.

children.text: Indraḫ pītasitāsitāruṇaharidvarṇaṃ vidhatte dhanurjyotir dhūmasamīranīraghaṭanāmātre 'py asāre ghane || 900 ||
children.translated_text: Such is the nature of great beings.

children.text: bhūtānāṃ bhāvināṃ vāpi yad aśakyaṃ mahībhujām /
children.translated_text: What was impossible for kings past or future,

children.text: tad iṣṭasāhaso rājā kīrtaye kartum iṣṭavān || 901 ||
children.translated_text: that the king, bold in his desires, wished to accomplish for the sake of fame.

children.text: kartavyaṃ sāhasaṃ yad yad ucitaṃ yad ayaṃ nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever bold deed was proper and fitting for this king to do,
given the limitlessness of time and the vastness of the earth,

children.text: tat tat sambhāvya sādhyaṃ sa bhāvibhir medinīśvaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: considering all that accomplishable by future rulers,
he came from afar like the ocean toward gems of superior brilliance.

children.text: sāhaseṣv ekam ādātum api prāpa na niścayam /
children.translated_text: Among bold enterprises, he could not even decide which one to undertake,
being of a mind generous toward the circumstances of the poor.

children.text: na toṣitaś śrutai rājñām atītānāṃ ca sāhase /
children.translated_text: Not satisfied by the heard accounts of past kings' bold deeds,

children.text: agamyeṣv api bhūpālaś śaileṣu ca sarassu ca || 905 ||
children.translated_text: the king [turned his mind] to mountains and lakes that were even inaccessible.

children.text: śabdeṣv artheṣv iva kavis tatas samacaran nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a poet among words and meanings, the king then went about,
eager for practical affairs, like the words of merchants.
The king then heard from scholars the <s>Nīlapurāṇa</s> and other texts,
abandoning all other preoccupations, eager solely for bold enterprise.
Once, the protector of the earth pondered thus for a long time:
"As the face is to the body, so is the terrestrial sphere to the three worlds.
Foremost therein is the realm of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, like the eye,
where the peaks of the <s>Śailarāja</s> (King of Mountains) serve as eyelashes.

body.translated_text: There, like the circle of stars, is the lake <s>Mahāpadma</s>.

children.translated_text: Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 119
Where <s>Mainaka</s>, ever agitated, is intent on searching.
By the fruit of its reflection, I know the lord of the <s>Himālaya</s> shines—
where, under the guise of the sun's reflection, in that lake resembling the ocean,

children.text: antaẖ kṛtāspado dīpto lakṣyate Vaḍavānalaḥ / JRt_B.1196ab /
children.translated_text: the blazing submarine fire of <s>Vaḍavānala</s> is seen to have established itself within.

body.translated_text: The abode of <s>Mahāpadma</s> there is the twin of the celestial sphere.

children.text: tad āpūrya kathañcic cet kiyanmātram api kramāt /
children.translated_text: If that could somehow be gradually filled, even to a small extent,
then construction could be undertaken, and the fruit of sovereignty would arise.
That great king of lakes, twenty-eight <s>krośas</s> in extent, concealed by fathomless water,

children.text: sarorājas sa hi mahān āśayo mahatām api" || 912 ||
children.translated_text: is indeed a great aspiration even for the great."
Having pondered thus, to devise a means at that lake,
he went by boat to its center, like a <s>yogin</s> [going] to himself by himself.
The great lake <s>Mahāpadma</s>, always with surging waves—
previous kings never plunged into it, fearing the breaking of their boats.
Whether through the power of austerity, or through courage, or through the gravity of the task,

children.text: sthalavat salile tatra sa rājānvasarat sukham || 915 ||
children.translated_text: the king comfortably traversed the water there as if on dry land.

children.text: yac cetasā cirataraṃ paricintyamānaṃ cintāmaṇiẖ kila dadāti tad eva nānyat /
children.translated_text: That which the mind contemplates for a very long time, the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) indeed grants exactly that, and nothing else;

children.text: cittasya cāpi yad agocaratām upaiti tat tu prayacchatitarāṃ vata buddhiratnam || 916 ||
children.translated_text: but that which even transcends the reach of the mind—the jewel of intelligence grants that all the more.
For that protector of the earth, whose intellect was without support,

children.text: sarasas sthalatāṃ kartum upāyaḫ pratyabhād ayam || 917 ||
children.translated_text: this plan occurred to him for turning the lake into dry land:
"By boats filled with stones, dropped one on top of another,
I shall fill this up, as if with mountain peaks [filling] the ocean.
With platforms made of <s>devadāru</s> (deodar) wood, bound with iron,
they will not dissolve in the water, along with the stone-laden boats."
Then the king, returning, with eagerness bound upon him,

children.text: abhyagāc charaṇaṃ tatra te cainaṃ nṛpam abhyadhuḥ || 920 ||
children.translated_text: approached the elders for refuge, and they spoke to the king thus:
"The auspicious city of <s>Sandhimatī</s> was like <s>Dvārikā</s> of his,
protected by the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus for mankind.
The deity of that city was <s>Mahāpadma</s>, the lord of serpents,
who protected the four <s>varṇas</s> (castes) like children, just as you do.
Due to the power of the <s>Kali</s> age, the people dwelling in that land,

children.text: janās taddeśavāstavyāḫ prāpur vṛddhiṃ dinād dinam || 923 ||
children.translated_text: engaging in wicked conduct, grew in number day by day.
Then, according to the consequence of their deeds and the chain of reversals,

children.text: krodhaṃ nāgapatir yāto dūṣaṇād iva sajjanaḥ || 924 ||
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>nāgas</s> became angered, like a good man at being slandered.
To a certain potter who had not abandoned his own righteous conduct,
he spoke in a dream: 'I shall submerge the wicked citizens.'
'The <s>nāga</s> will drown the people because of their wicked conduct'—

children.text: prātar vadantam ahasan paurāḫ paśum ivākhilāḥ || 926 ||
children.translated_text: when he said this in the morning, all the citizens laughed at him as if he were an animal.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 120

children.text: tadāstike kumbhakāre gate tasmāt purād drutam /
children.translated_text: When that believing potter had quickly departed from the city,

children.text: nāgendro jalapūreṇa sarvam avroḍayat puram // JRt_B.1213 //
children.translated_text: the <s>nāga</s> lord submerged the entire city with a flood.

children.text:
yāvat paurāḫ purāc celus te sarve hariṇā iva /
tāvad evāgram ākrāmad dāvāgnir iva tajjalam // JRt_B.1214 //
children.translated_text: As soon as the citizens tried to move from the city, all of them like deer, the water advanced upon them just as swiftly, like a forest fire.
Terrifying with the sound of water-streams cascading from his hundreds of upraised hoods,
the <s>nāga</s> king then encircled the city with waters, like an enemy.
While the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> recited <s>mantras</s>, while people bowed in supplication,

children.text: rudatsv api ca bāleṣu nāsyābhūd Yamavad dayā || 928 ||
children.translated_text: while children wept—he had no compassion, like <s>Yama</s> (Death).
Out of fear, when children, their sons, clung to their necks, the women
performed worship of the serpent-lord, as it were, with pearl-fruits of tears.

children.text: pādād aṅkaṃ tataẖ kaṇṭhaṃ tatas skandhaṃ tataś śiraḥ /
children.translated_text: From feet to lap, then to neck, then to shoulders, then to head—

children.text: prāṇā iva sutā jagmur mātṝṇāṃ bhayavihvalāḥ || 930 ||
children.translated_text: like departing life-breaths, the sons climbed upon their mothers, bewildered by fear.
Like a passionate lover in the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (amorous) mood, the flood
touched all the trembling limbs of the women.

children.text: hrasvaṃ dīrghaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca sthūlaṃ cāṇu mahat tathā /
children.translated_text: Short and long, fine and thick, small and great—
the flood expanded, covering everything like darkness.
In that fathomless water, the serpent-king, unable to bear the touch of the wicked,

children.text: phaṇirājas sthitiṃ cakre vipine sajjano yathā || 933 ||
children.translated_text: then took up residence in the forest, as a good man does.

children.text: Kāliyas sa hi nāgendraḫ padākrānto Muradviṣā /
children.translated_text: He is indeed <s>Kāliya</s>, that lord of <s>nāgas</s>, whose head was trampled by the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
who, because a lotus grew upon his head, obtained the name <s>Mahāpadma</s>.

children.text: naṣṭān yojayituṃ bhūyaẖ Kaśmīrān icchato Hareḥ /
children.translated_text: You are the incarnation of <s>Hari</s> who wishes to re-establish the lost <s>Kaśmīra</s>—

children.text: avatāras tvam etat te sidhyaty eva cikīrṣitam" || 935 ||
children.translated_text: this desire of yours shall surely succeed."

children.text: rājā śrutveti sa svapne kṣaṇam evam acintayat /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, the king then pondered for a moment in his dream thus:
"How else could enterprises of this kind succeed?
The serpent could not tolerate the reversal of the people's conduct in the city—

children.text: nāniṣṭaṃ sahate 'lpo 'pi tādṛśas tu mahān katham || 937 ||
children.translated_text: even a small one does not endure what is undesirable; how then one so great?
I, of the same lineage as the parasol befitting the <s>nāga</s> king,
here undertake merely the dry-land foundation for the pitcher of the gem of fame.
When a great expanse of land comes to exist in the middle of <s>Ullola</s> lake,

children.text: pavitre vijane cātra siddhiṃ yāsyanti sādhakāḥ" || 939 ||
children.translated_text: in this sacred and solitary place, <s>sādhakas</s> (spiritual practitioners) will attain perfection."
Having pondered thus, the king with strong stone-laden boats
filled even the fathomless center of <s>Ullola</s> lake.

children.text: sarasas tu tatas tasya sthalībhūte 'tha bhūpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: When the lake had thus been turned into land, the great king
built <s>Jainalaṅkā</s> in the middle region of that lake.
At the edge of that very lake, by the grace of the lord of <s>rākṣasas</s>,
King <s>Jayāpīḍa</s> had caused it to become dry land.
In winter, through the digging up of lotus roots, water-chestnuts, and such,
the deep extent of the fort of the illustrious <s>Jayāpīḍa</s> becomes known.
In the inner parts of <s>Ullola</s>, <s>Suyyā-kuṇḍalaka</s> and other
many villages are seen, marked by spacious dwellings.

children.text: girayo 'pi nimajjanti yatra tatra tu sa vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: Where even mountains were submerged, there he built
<s>Jainalaṅkā</s>, a great endeavor, placing that officer in charge.
<s>Ruyya Bhāṇḍapati</s>, of intellect shining with skill in craftsmanship—
who restored the great gate of the capital that had been destroyed.
Thick with palaces that shattered the pride of <s>Himālaya</s>'s peaks,
in <s>Kramarājya</s>, with glistening sovereignty, he built <s>Suratrāṇapura</s>.
The king built <s>Jainakoṭṭa</s> (fort), with which he struck down enemies, full of watchtowers all around,
beautiful with dancing silk banners at its ends.
In all restorations of old buildings and in new constructions,

children.text: ājñā rājño babhau hetū Ruyyabhāṇḍapateś ca dhīḥ || 949 ||
children.translated_text: the king's command was the cause, and the intellect of <s>Ruyya Bhāṇḍapati</s> [was the means].
On the shore of <s>Mahāpadma</s> lake, endowed with the splendor of <s>Jaina</s>—
the sounds of the city pavilions, likewise the illustrious <s>Jainakuṇḍala</s>,
and also <s>Jainapattana</s>—the lord of the earth established them.
Pseudo-<s>Jonarāja</s> 121

children.text: kāruṇyāt kīrtilobhāc ca svayam evātha bhūpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Out of compassion and desire for fame, the king himself then

children.text: vāmaparśve girau vāri visraṣṭuṃ ciram abhramat // JRt_B.1232 //
children.translated_text: wandered for a long time on the mountain on the left side, to release water.
Seeing the mountain without water and eager to bring a channel,
he heard from scholars learned in scripture that at its base was <s>Amareśvara</s>.
For the unobstructed accomplishment of his purpose, to propitiate the Lord,
he then ascended Mount <s>Amareśa</s>, as if ascending his own pride.

children.text: te latābhya iva Mlecchā Nāgebhyaś śaṅkayākulāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Mlecchas</s>, like creepers, agitated by fear of the <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: nānyo'yam iva saṃlāpaṃ tatra svaka iva vyadhuḥ // JRt_B.1235 //
children.translated_text: conversed there among themselves as if they were not themselves.
Like healthy people [avoiding] those with skin disease, the <s>Nāgas</s> dwelling in the forest

children.text: Nāgā darśanam apy antar nāsahanta kadācana // JRt_B.1236 //
children.translated_text: could not at any time tolerate even the sight of the <s>Turuṣkas</s>.
The king, disturbed in his resolve, heard and could not bear them—
like a child scorched by a spark of fire [cannot bear] a flawless ruby.

children.text: kapīnām iva baddhānāṃ bhītānām api ca dhruvam /
children.translated_text: Certainly, even when the <s>Mlecchas</s> were restrained and frightened, like bound monkeys,
the fickleness of their wicked conduct did not cease.

children.text: yad udgarjadbhir udyadbhis savidyudbhir ghanair ghanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That upon them, with dense clouds roaring, rising, flashing with lightning,

children.text: kopenevābhavat teṣu tataẖ kālamukhaṃ nabhaḥ // JRt_B.1239 //
children.translated_text: the sky then assumed a face of doom, as if in anger.
When the <s>Mlecchas</s>, fleeing swiftly from the mountain like cowards from battle,
lost their courage under showers of hail at that very moment,

children.text: mānād iva kulīno 'tha bhaktyā dhairyād avicyutaḥ /
children.translated_text: as if out of dignity, like a nobleman, unwavering in devotion and courage,

children.text: avarūḍho na śailendrāt Kaśmīrendraẖ kathañcana // JRt_B.1241 //
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>Kaśmīra</s> by no means descended from the king of mountains.
When the <s>Yavana</s> serpents thundered like enchanted clouds,

children.text: tyakto nidhir iva kṣmāpo devo nāgair aśaṃsyata // JRt_B.1242 //
children.translated_text: The king, like a treasure abandoned [by its guardian serpents], was compared to a god by the <s>Nāgas</s>. (JRt B.1242)
'Turn back from here, O Lord! The task will be accomplished.

children.text: pūjopakaraṇaṃ Śambhoḫ prāptam eva visṛjyatām" // JRt_B.1243 //
children.translated_text: The materials for the worship of <s>Śambhu</s> have already been obtained — let them be dispatched.' (JRt B.1243)
Having heard thus from a divine-formed man in a dream, the lord of the earth,

children.text: siddhakāryas tataḫ prātaẖ Kaśmīrāntaram āviśat // JRt_B.1244 //
children.translated_text: His purpose accomplished, then in the morning entered the interior of <s>Kaśmīra</s>. (JRt B.1244)
'Bring the <s>Ledarī</s> [river] by a mountain path to the town of <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s>' —

children.text: iti rājā samādikṣad dhārmikaṃ Śiryabhaṭṭakam // JRt_B.1245 //
children.translated_text: Thus the king instructed the righteous <s>Śiryabhaṭṭaka</s>. (JRt B.1245)
Because of his compassion, his excellence, and his freedom from greed,

children.text: niyuktas sa nadīkṛṣṭāv alagad bhaṭṭaŚiryakaḥ // JRt_B.1246 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṭṭa Śiryaka</s> was appointed by the king in the task of diverting the river without delay. (JRt B.1246)
His authority unchallenged everywhere, he then, with the local chiefs,

children.text: lokam ānāyya śailendraṃ saritaḫ padavīṃ vyadhāt // JRt_B.1247 //
children.translated_text: Brought the people together and made a path for the river through the great mountain. (JRt B.1247)
In the pits, he made stone embankments; in the depressions, he filled them with boulders;

children.text: khanīṣu kuṭilaṃ mārgaṃ tasyās sa sarito vyadhāt // JRt_B.1248 //
children.translated_text: In the cuttings, he made a winding course for that river. (JRt B.1248)
The river, nourishing the trees standing on its banks from the front on high,

children.text: sā tu rājasabhevātha rabhasād udapūrayat // JRt_B.1249 //
children.translated_text: Then impetuously overflowed, like a king's assembly [filled to overflowing]. (JRt B.1249)

children.text: prajñeva viduṣas sthitvā ciraṃ pratipadaṃ sarit /
children.translated_text: Like the wisdom of a scholar, having stood long at each step, the river,
With waves fluttering like eyebrows, proceeded slowly, very slowly. (JRt B.1250)
By the power of the king's austerity, by the guidance of <s>Bhaṭṭa Śirya</s>,

children.text: prajānām api bhāgyena nāsyā vighno 'bhavat kvacit // JRt_B.1251 //
children.translated_text: And also by the good fortune of the people, no obstacle arose for it anywhere. (JRt B.1251)

children.text: sā bhajantī giriṃ kvāpi tyajantī dūrataẖ kvacit /
children.translated_text: That river, sometimes embracing a mountain, sometimes abandoning one from afar,
Seemed as if flowing from a rampart, quarreling noisily. (JRt B.1252)
Like the mental state of the new king, with its waters,
On the right of the river was a pit, on the left a mountain with jagged rocks,

children.text: puras tuṅgā ca dīrghā ca śileti kvāpy adṛśyata // JRt_B.1253 //
children.translated_text: And in front a stone both tall and long was seen in places. (JRt B.1253)
Its path blocked by a massive boulder in front,

children.text: na tasthau na yayau kulyā kāminīva vimānitā // JRt_B.1254 //
children.translated_text: The canal neither halted nor flowed — like a woman who feels insulted. (JRt B.1254)

children.text: rājñā svayam athāpy atra gaṇḍaśaile vidārite /
children.translated_text: When the king himself then had that boulder split,

children.text: sarit tīrṇapratijñena gacchantī kramate sma sā // JRt_B.1255 //
children.translated_text: The river, as if having fulfilled its vow [to cross], proceeded on its way. (JRt B.1255)
When the obstruction of the path of the desired river was caused by rock,

children.text: Mihirākhyo nṛpaẖ krodhāt strīlakṣāṇi jaghāna saḥ // JRt_B.1256 //
children.translated_text: The king named <s>Mihira</s> [in former times], out of anger, slew a hundred thousand women. (JRt B.1256)
