But <s>Śrī Jainollābhadīna</s>, having split with tools the rock

children.text: dārayitvā śilāṃ śastrair janatās samajīvayat // JRt_B.1257 //
children.translated_text: That obstructed the river's path, gave life to the people. (JRt B.1257)
Like <s>Bhagīratha</s> bringing the <s>Gaṅgā</s> fallen from the crest of <s>Girīśa</s> [Śiva],
He brought the <s>Ledarī</s>, wide as an ocean, to the land of <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s>. (JRt B.1258)

children.text: mekhaleva gires tasya rājñaẖ kīrtir ivāmalā /
children.translated_text: Like a girdle of the mountain, like the spotless fame of the king,

children.text: bhūmer muktālatevāsau sarit param aśobhata // JRt_B.1259 //
children.translated_text: Like a pearl necklace of the earth — that river shone supremely. (JRt B.1259)
'Even though <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s> [the Sun] stands nearby, he cannot dry me up' —

children.text: itīva taraloddāmā ninādam akarot sarit // JRt_B.1260 //
children.translated_text: Thus, as if [declaring so], the river made a roaring sound with restless, unbound [waves]. (JRt B.1260)
'<s>Śrī Jayānollābhadīna</s> alone, a king devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: saritpravāhakapaṭād iti rekhāṃ Vidhir vyadhāt // JRt_B.1261 //
children.translated_text: [Could accomplish] the feat of making a river flow' — thus the Creator drew a line [of distinction]. (JRt B.1261)
As trees scorched by celibacy [i.e., drought] [feel bliss] from the touch of a woman [i.e., rain],

children.text: sekāt saritkṛtāt tatra kim apy udabhavat sukham // JRt_B.1262 //
children.translated_text: From the irrigation provided by the river there, an indescribable happiness arose. (JRt B.1262)

children.text: darśitā vartanābhis sā gacchantī subhagaṃ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Shown its winding course, moving beautifully and slowly,
The river, with its foamy laughter, delighted <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s> most joyfully. (JRt B.1263)
The sun, reflected in the captivating stream of the river,

children.text: mūrtas sannihito jñātaẖ Kalāv api ciraṃ janaiḥ // JRt_B.1264 //
children.translated_text: Was known by people as present in embodied form, even in the age of <s>Kali</s>, for a long time. (JRt B.1264)

children.text: nanu dīnān pālayantī nadān abhimukhī satī /
children.translated_text: Indeed, protecting the humble, facing the rivers [head-on],

children.text: sarit prasiddhim agamaj Jainadharmanadīti sā // JRt_B.1265 //
children.translated_text: The river attained the renown of being called '<s>Jainadharmanadī</s>' (the River of Jaina's Dharma). (JRt B.1265)

children.text: sāndraṃ pradoṣajanitaṃ timiraṃ nivārya viśvaprakāśanaparasya divākarasya /
children.translated_text: Dispelling the thick darkness born of dusk, of the sun whose purpose is the illumination of the universe —

children.text: āyāti maṇḍalatalaṃ svayam eva tejaḥ śreṣṭhauṣadhīśa ṛṇam āstatarāṃ ciraṃ yat // JRt_B.1266 //
children.translated_text: Its radiance arrives at the disc's surface of its own accord: O supreme Lord of Herbs [the Moon], the debt [to the sun] that has long been stretched out. (JRt B.1266)
When fifteen groups of years of the <s>Kali</s> age had passed,

children.text: Atharvakauśalād Droṇo raṇaṃ Kurubalair vyadhāt // JRt_B.1267 //
children.translated_text: <s>Droṇa</s>, through expertise in the <s>Atharva</s> [Veda], waged war with the <s>Kuru</s> forces. (JRt B.1267)
When <s>Droṇa</s> was slain by the <s>Kurus</s>, his <s>Atharva</s> [knowledge], left without shelter,
Took refuge with the sharp-witted <s>Karṇāṭas</s> [people of Karnataka], along with the <s>Veda</s>. (JRt B.1268)
The <s>Kāśmīrikas</s>, seeing the greatness of the <s>Atharva Veda</s> in the <s>śāstras</s>,

children.text: Kāśmīrikāṇāṃ tatprāptyai ciram āsīn manorathaḥ // JRt_B.1269 //
children.translated_text: Long had a heartfelt desire for its acquisition. (JRt B.1269)
Then, after a great span of time, frightened by <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>,

children.text: Yuddhabhaṭṭābhidho mānī deśāntaram agād guṇī // JRt_B.1270 //
children.translated_text: The proud and virtuous one named <s>Yuddhabhaṭṭa</s> went to another country. (JRt B.1270)

children.text: Yajuṣaḫ paṭhanāt prītaiẖ Karṇāṭais so 'tha pāṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Pleased by his recitation of the <s>Yajus</s> [Veda], the <s>Karṇāṭas</s> then taught him

children.text: sarahasyam Atharvāṇaṃ nijāṃ pratyāgato bhuvam // JRt_B.1271 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Atharva</s> [Veda] with its esoteric portions, and he returned to his own land. (JRt B.1271)
Having received that <s>Veda</s> as initiation from the virtuous <s>Śrī Jainollābhadīna</s>,

children.text: upadīkṛtya taṃ Vedaṃ parāṃ tuṣṭim ajījanat // JRt_B.1272 //
children.translated_text: Who delighted in virtues, [the king] experienced supreme satisfaction. (JRt B.1272)
Then the righteous <s>Śiryabhaṭṭa</s>, having given his own clothes and food,
Caused the sons of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> to be taught that <s>Atharva Veda</s> by that very [Yuddhabhaṭṭa]. (JRt B.1273)
That righteous school of the wise <s>Śiryabhaṭṭa</s>

children.text: Karṇāṭāṇām api param agamat spṛhaṇīyatām // JRt_B.1274 //
children.translated_text: Came to be envied even by the <s>Karṇāṭas</s>. (JRt B.1274)

children.text: snigdhā vidyuc chravaṇamadhuraṃ garjitaṃ vṛṣṭir iṣṭā chāyā bhāsvatklamabharaharī māruto mandamandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Gentle lightning, thunder sweet to the ear, welcome rain, shade that removes the burden of the sun's heat, a soft and gentle breeze —

children.text: varṣākālaṃ Vidhir anudinaṃ vardhayan svair guṇaughair grīṣmārtāsu prathayati dayādakṣiṇatvaṃ prajāsu // JRt_B.1275 //
children.translated_text: The Creator, daily increasing the rainy season with the flood of his own virtues, displays his compassion and generosity toward the creatures afflicted by summer. (JRt B.1275)
Due to the unfavorable disposition of the decade, or by the strength of the opposition,
Turned away from what was fitting in matters of giving, consecration, and honor, (JRt B.1276)
Even toward <s>Ādhamakhāna</s>, his eldest son, the king
Was displeased — long regarded [as unworthy] by those lacking discernment. (JRt B.1277)
Toward his other sons, <s>Hājyakhāna</s> and the rest, special favor was shown;

children.text: vibhāsitas sa rājñāpi tilako madhunā yathā // JRt_B.1278 //
children.translated_text: He [Ādhamakhāna] was illuminated by the king too, like a <s>tilaka</s> mark with honey. (JRt B.1278)

children.text: ādau pādatale santaṃ karālambaṃ tataẖ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: First placed at the feet, then given a hand [to hold],

children.text: yaṃ darśanāntare ca drāg uttamāṅgopari sthitam // JRt_B.1279 //
children.translated_text: Then, at a [subsequent] audience, quickly placed atop the head — (JRt B.1279)

children.text: avardhayat kramād eva kalānāṃ nidhim īśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord gradually elevated that treasury of arts;
<s>Mallādaryāvakhāna</s> was appointed to authority everywhere. (JRt B.1280)

children.text:
samo Vaiśravaṇasyāsīd bhaṭṭaVaiśravaṇo guṇaiḥ /
īśvarasya prasādena rājabhir yad avartsyata // JRt_B.1281 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṭṭa Vaiśravaṇa</s> was equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> [Kubera] in virtues; by the grace of the Lord, he would have been honored by kings. (JRt B.1281)
The king's compassion, soft-handed and adorned with pleasing conduct,
Having great stories [of deeds], became [like] a beloved wife. (JRt 951)
The king, destroyer of the pitiless, did not kill the <s>Ḍomba</s> thieves
But binding them tightly with fetters, always made them do clay-work [forced labor]. (JRt 952)

children.text: nirdiśan yaśasā śubhrā diśo nṛpatir ādiśat /
children.translated_text: The king, illuminating the directions white with glory, prohibited
The killing of birds and fish in numerous lakes. (JRt 953)

children.text: atha jātu hṛtāṃ caurair gāṃ parijñāya kañcana /
children.translated_text: Then, once recognizing a cow stolen by thieves [belonging to] a certain [person]

children.text: krandantaṃ bhūmipaḫ pṛcchaṃs caurāṃś cāthāpy aḍhaukayat || 954 ||
children.translated_text: Who was crying, the king questioned [him] and then summoned the thieves. (JRt 954)
Without the correspondence of age and marks of the cow, except for its bent horns —
The truth-speaking <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> stated the cause, to the amazement of the court. (JRt 955)
'The bent-hornedness of this [cow] is natural, just like a <s>tilaka</s> [mark]' —

children.text: rājñā pṛṣṭe vadaty evaṃ caure mūkā sabhābhavat || 956 ||
children.translated_text: When the thief was questioned thus by the king, the assembly fell silent. (JRt 956)
As a test, when the king applied heat-sweat to the cow's horns,

children.text: kuṭilatvaṃ vyapaiti sma prāk caurasyātha śṛṅgayoḥ || 957 ||
children.translated_text: The crookedness first [disappeared] from the thief's [artificially bent horns], then from the [natural] horns. (JRt 957)
Thus, by his excellence of intellect in examining legal disputes,
He produced elation and uplifting of mind in the assembly of ministers. (JRt 958)
A judge of patient intellect, one who delighted [people] through appropriate punishment,
<s>Gaṇanāpati Gauraka</s> bore the burden of the king's subjects. (JRt 959)
Those who, out of [pretended] helpfulness, had given bribe-money themselves,
In the course of time, when ungrateful, in the very court assembly, (JRt 960)
When they made public those gifts, the angered king

children.text: Maulāno Malla Esākas tebhyas tat pratidāpitaḥ || 961 ||
children.translated_text: Caused <s>Maulāna Malla Esāka</s> to return them [the bribes]. (JRt 961)
First standing at the feet, then made to hold his hand,
Then coming into the field of vision, raised to the top of the head — (JRt 962)
<s>Daryāvakhāna</s> was then purchased [i.e., won over] by the grateful Lord,

children.text: kalānidhir himaruciẖ kaumudīṃ hi tato vahan || 963 ||
children.translated_text: A treasury of arts, like the cool-rayed [moon] bearing the moonlight. (JRt 963)

children.text: dinapatir na rasātalagaṃ tamaś śamayituṃ yatate yad avekṣya saḥ /
children.translated_text: The lord of the day [sun] does not endeavor to quell the darkness that has gone to the netherworld — seeing this,

children.text: ativaladruci kālaghanāvṛter harati tatpratibimbam aho jagat || 964 ||
children.translated_text: The darkness, of exceedingly powerful brilliance, veiled by the clouds of time, steals the reflection of that [sun] — alas — [stealing] the world. (JRt 964)
The king, though weary from the burden of the earth, though treading the edge of the sword [i.e., facing danger],

children.text: svadattaṃ vibhavaṃ yasya dṛṣṭvā viśrāmam āptavān || 965 ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the wealth bestowed by him [upon Daryāvakhāna], found rest. (JRt 965)
<s>Mahmadakhāna</s>, that treasury of arts, then set [like the moon];
How can things supremely beautiful last long? (JRt 966)

children.text: pratyabdaṃ pratihāryādyair yo vyadhāt prītim arthinām /
children.translated_text: He who, year after year, bestowed delight upon supplicants through <s>pratihārya</s> (magic/gifts) and other [means],

children.text: satyavrato divam agān Mahimaśrīs sa Ṭhakkuraḥ || 967 ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Ṭhakkura</s> <s>Mahimaśrī</s>, true to his vow, went to heaven. (JRt 967)

children.text: tadgotrajebhyas sa kilāgūḍhaṃ tasya vadhaṃ vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: One who, under the pretext of an embassy, was banished from his own land by the king —
He secretly carried out the murder of those of the same clan. (JRt 968)
At the king's place of salt-tax and such, in the city called <s>Sondhya</s>,

children.text: pratyāgatas sa tīrthādhvakhinno Vinno divaṃ yayau || 969 ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Vinna</s>, having returned, exhausted from the pilgrimage road, went to heaven. (JRt 969)
The great <s>Śrī Śiryabhaṭṭa</s>, always devoted to overseeing
The king's offices of <s>dharma</s>, also went to heaven at that time. (JRt 970)

children.text: gateṣv apy eṣu dharmo 'sya rājño naivālpatāṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when these [ministers] departed, the <s>dharma</s> of this king did not diminish;

children.text: kṣmāṃ dadhānasya Śeṣasya Diggajā hi paricchadaḥ || 971 ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Śeṣa</s> who bears the earth has the <s>Diggajas</s> [directional elephants] as his retinue. (JRt 971)
In a single day, one <s>crore</s> of <s>dīnāras</s> [gold coins] was given by the king
To children alone, through the hands of <s>Jayyabhaṭṭa</s>. (JRt 972)
A collection of wondrous objects existed in his kingdom;
How otherwise would one know this to be an incarnation of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>? (JRt 973)
Sugarcanes, whose streams of moonbeam-nectar are perpetual beggars [i.e., always in need of water],
Were planted by him in the lands of the <s>Mārtāṇḍa</s> region. (JRt 974)
By renouncing through the greatness of <s>yoga</s> the transformations of wrinkles and grey hair,
<s>Śrī Jainollābhadena</s> manifested his divinity. (JRt 975)
He diverted the <s>Sindhu</s> flowing toward <s>Bhārosa</s>, pulling it from <s>Tūlamūla</s>,
[Making it] a cause of destruction for the island of crop abundance. (JRt 976)
Pseudo-Jonarāja, section 122
With the sole means of the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), <s>vāra</s> (weekday), <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), <s>saṅkrānti</s> (solar ingress) and such of the previous year,
Writing instantly the <s>tithis</s>, <s>vāras</s>, <s>nakṣatras</s>, and <s>saṅkrāntis</s> of the coming year — (JRt B.1313)
<s>Ruyyabhaṭṭa</s> existed in that reign, renowned for the king's favor,
Causing contempt for the <s>Khaṇḍakhādya</s> [astronomical treatise] through [his mastery of] mathematical science. (JRt B.1314)

children.text: candre 'staṃ gata eva daivavaśataś śokāgniśāntyai niśā tatkāntā ravikāntavahnim udayāt kaṣṭaṃ praviṣṭā satī /
children.translated_text: When the moon had set, by the force of destiny, for the quelling of grief's fire, the night — his beloved — having entered the fire of the sun-gem [sūryakānta] at sunrise, alas,

children.text: dyām āruhya tadīyadhūmakapaṭāt prāptā punas tanmaho yat so 'yaṃ graharājapādamahimaprāptaḫ prasādodayaḥ // JRt_B.1315 //
children.translated_text: Ascending the sky through the disguise of his smoke, she again attained his glory: this is the rise of grace, attained through the majesty of the feet of the king of planets [the Sun]. (JRt B.1315)

children.text: ṛtupatiś śiśireṇa samatsaro 'py ativiruddhakaro na hitas sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the lord of the seasons [spring], though jealous of winter, does not stand as a hindrance, acting in complete opposition;

children.text: yadi bhuvaṃ śiśiro na vināśayet kim iva nāma madhur vata yojayet // JRt_B.1316 //
children.translated_text: If winter did not destroy the earth, what sweetness indeed would spring bring about? (JRt B.1316)
Then <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s>, though a <s>paṇḍita</s> adorned with knowledge of the <s>śāstras</s>,
Alas, prohibited the cremation of the dead out of hatred for [Hindu] philosophy. (JRt B.1317)

children.text: pretadehās tadā kecit tyaktā gūḍhaṃ jalāntare /
children.translated_text: Some dead bodies were then secretly abandoned in the water,

children.text: araṇye kecana tyaktā nikhātā bandhubhiḫ pare // JRt_B.1318 //
children.translated_text: some were left in the forest, and others were buried by their relatives. // JRt_B.1318 //
Then, when <s>Sūhabhaṭṭa</s> had passed away by the law of time, gradually

children.text: prajā vītabhayā kāṃścit pretān gūḍham adāhayan // JRt_B.1319 //
children.translated_text: the people, freed from fear, secretly cremated some of the dead. // JRt_B.1319 //

children.text: doṣān dṛṣṭvā svayaṃ rājñā Saidamakke nirākṛte /
children.translated_text: When <s>Saidamakka</s> was dismissed by the king himself, having seen his faults,

children.text: adahan prakaṭaṃ pretadehān ahani bāndhavāḥ // JRt_B.1320 //
children.translated_text: the relatives openly cremated the bodies of the dead during the day. // JRt_B.1320 //
Then, by following their husbands on the pyre, the wives of meritorious men
averted the exhaustion of merit through union with the limbs of heavenly women. // JRt_B.1321 //

children.text: bhoktuṃ rājyaṃ paitṛkaṃ tad Dhātrā dattaṃ saṬhakkuraḥ /
children.translated_text: To enjoy that ancestral kingdom given by <s>Dhātṛ</s> (the Creator), together with the <s>Ṭhakkuras</s>,
<s>Jayānollābhadīna</s> (Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn) returned to <s>Kaśmīra</s>. // JRt_B.1322 //
Taking the garments, weapons, and head-armor of the slain,

children.text: sadanaṃ sadhanaṃ Jassaratho 'py āgād vimucyatām // JRt_B.1323 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jassaratha</s> also came to his residence with his wealth — let him be released. // JRt_B.1323 //
On the bright day of <s>Brahman</s>, in the bright fortnight, in the year marked by the number six, when the moon was in conjunction,
<s>Jayānollābhadīna</s> entered the capital. // JRt_B.1324 //
To <s>Hanūmat</s>, the son of the lord of <s>Dānātakathana</s>,
the king bestowed the lordship of the village of <s>Sarvasvakarṣaṇa</s>. // JRt_B.1325 //
The king gave to <s>Meraka</s> the seat in the court of assembly,
skilled in conducting judicial investigation, the examination of truth and falsehood. // JRt_B.1326 //

children.text: vivṛddhaYavanādhikāravaravipravīrair viṭair bhaṭṭaiẖ kuṭilavartmagair mathitamohitāś ca prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: The people, churned and confused by the grown authority of <s>Yavanas</s>, by leading <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, heroes, courtesans, and officials following crooked paths —

children.text: Surejyadhiṣaṇaṃ vicāracaturaṃ paraṃ Ṭhakkuraṃ nirīkṣya yuyuje vicārapadanirṇaye Merakam // JRt_B.1327 //
children.translated_text: seeing the <s>Ṭhakkura</s> <s>Surejya</s>, who possessed <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s intellect and was skilled in judgment, he appointed <s>Meraka</s> to the determination of judicial positions. // JRt_B.1327 //
The king gave the generalship of the army to the heroic <s>Ṭhakkura</s>,
of foremost valor, born of the <s>Malleka</s> <s>Nauruja</s> from <s>Vinnaka</s>. // JRt_B.1328 //
He assigned to <s>Satājarāja</s> the administration of <s>Ledarī</s>,
and to <s>Malleśarāja</s> he gave a succession of great villages. // JRt_B.1329 //
The king also gave the district called <s>Ardhavana</s>, freed from tax obligations,
to the one named <s>Ādama</s>, endowed with great valor. // JRt_B.1330 //
The supreme lord gave the lordship of <s>Pravareśapura</s>
to the valorous and wise road-commander named <s>Mahmad</s>. // JRt_B.1331 //

children.text: Bhāṅgilaviṣayaṃ bhūbhṛt sa tulāyāṃ dadau nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: That king gave the district of <s>Bhāṅgila</s> in balance [as a gift], the king
to his younger brothers, road-commanders — the foremost being <s>Tājaka</s> — many. // JRt_B.1332 //
Having given the <s>Pañcagrāmī</s> (five villages) and precious horses, he gratified them;
he gave the lordship of <s>Śrījākoṭṭa</s> and the rank of <s>Mereṣkāra</s>. // JRt_B.1333 //

children.text:
ṬhakkurāyĀhmadākhyāya mahāgrāmāṃś ca pattalām /
Ṭhakkurebhyo 'parebhyo 'sāv api mānyatayā samam /
mahāgrāmasahasrāṇi yatheṣṭaṃ pradadau nṛpaḥ // JRt_B.1334 //
children.translated_text: To the <s>Ṭhakkura</s> named <s>Āhmad</s>, great villages and the <s>pattalā</s> (military district); and to the other <s>Ṭhakkuras</s> also, along with marks of respect, the king bestowed thousands of great villages as he wished. // JRt_B.1334 //
